title: Original fantasy with strong world building and characters
text:
Full disclosure: I won this in a Goodreads giveaway.

It's very, very rare to come across a truly original entry in the epic fantasy world, these days. Though in some ways I'm not even sure fantasy describes this book. Yes, it's obviously fantasy with magic and different races and such things, but at the same time it doesn't seem to focus on those things. It doesn't have the 'feel' of a typical fantasy book, and to me that's a good thing. Perhaps because it lacks some of the heaviness that many serious fantasy novels have. I did find that to be a good thing, though. It let the story move fairly quickly without getting bogged down on small details.

The world itself is very well laid out, especially because the reader is discovering it as the main character does. Rather clever of the author, there. Didn't even occur to me as I was reading, but in retrospect it worked and was very entertaining.

Characters...complex, interesting, well-rounded. I could go on, but you get the idea. At no point did I get the feeling I was dealing with cut outs or your typical fantasy cliches. Though I'll admit I'm a sucker for an anti-hero, which the main character definitely is. The relationships throughout the story are just as interesting, and nothing is ever quite as it seems.

I found the story itself to be very compelling and very original. It was one of those books that I couldn't wait to pick up when I had to set it down to go do something else. Halfway through I found myself lamenting the fact that there aren't any other books in the series written yet. I'm not going to talk much about it because there really is a lot to give away. I, for one, did not see the twists coming.

I really look forward to the next book in the series and finding out more about these characters, as well as the world they live in. Unlike so many books, these days, there's a very satisfying ending to this tale. Yes, it's apparently part of a larger story arc, but the author has not neglected the necessary resolution in each smaller part.

title: Great for costumes, not daily use
text:
I bought this for a Halloween costume last year, and it definitely delivered on the dramatic look I wanted. The pigmentation is intense, and it lasted through a night of dancing without smudging or fading. For a one-off event, it was perfect. However, I also tried to incorporate it into my regular routine a few times, and that’s where the product falls short.

The texture is thick and heavy. On a costume night, that’s fine because you want it to stay put, but for daily wear, it feels cakey and doesn’t blend well with other products. I noticed it settled into fine lines more than my usual makeup, and by midday it started to feel uncomfortable—like it was sitting on top of my skin rather than sinking in. Removing it also required a heavy-duty cleanser; my gentle daily makeup remover couldn’t handle it, which led to some irritation after repeated use.

I also had trouble with shade matching. The colors are bold and fun and bold, which is great for a costume, but the everyday neutral shades in this line seem slightly off—either too warm or too cool for my skin tone. If you are strictly looking for something to complete a cosplay, a stage performance, or a themed party, this is a solid choice. But if you want a versatile product for your daily bag, I would look elsewhere.

Overall, it earns four stars from me because it nails the costume purpose. Just don’t expect it to transition seamlessly into your everyday beauty routine.

title: Don't buy this item
text:
I really wanted to like this, but after spending an afternoon trying to make it work, I have to warn everyone: do not waste your money. The box art looked fantastic, and the description promised hours of creative play for my seven-year-old. In reality, the product is a complete mess.

First, the pieces are cut from the thinnest, cheapest cardboard I have ever seen. They started peeling and bending the moment we tried to punch them out. Several of the interlocking tabs snapped off before we even assembled the first section. The instructions are printed on a single sheet of paper in tiny, blurry font with no clear step numbering. My child and I ended up guessing how things fit together, and every guess was wrong. The final model looks nothing like the picture on the box—it wobbles, leans to one side, and falls apart if you breathe on it.

The advertised "premium sticker sheet" is actually a single sheet of low-tack stickers that refuse to stick to the textured surface. They curl up at the edges within minutes. Worse, the paint used on some of the pieces rubs off on your fingers, leaving a greasy, smudged mess. I tried contacting the seller about a missing part—the little flag that holds the main structure together was simply not in the bag. Their response was a form letter telling me to "double check" and offering a 10% refund, as if my time meant nothing.

I have bought dozens of toys and games on Amazon, and this is the first one that genuinely feels like a scam. It is not just disappointing; it is unsafe for younger kids because of the sharp plastic burrs left on the edges of some pieces that we had to file down ourselves. Save your money and buy a proper puzzle or building set from a brand that cares about quality. This thing is now in the trash, and I regret every penny I spent. I strongly advise you to avoid this product entirely.

The artwork is bright and engaging without being overwhelming. Characters and scenes are varied, which keeps each page feeling fresh. If there’s one small quibble, the glue pages are best used with a regular glue stick rather than the included paste to avoid mess, but that’s a minor issue and expected with kids’ activity books. Overall, a great purchase — affordable, high-quality, and thoughtfully designed for young children. title: Well Done Expose' On The Radical Right
text:
This book is part muckraking,part psyhcological analysis of the extreme right that has taken over the Republican Party.
Mr. Blumenthal did a large amount of research in this journalistic endeavor and he added a section at the end of the book to cover the first year of the Obama administration.

One Eisenhower quote that seldom gets mentioned is found in the Introduction, it's a warning and it's not about the military-industrial complex.
"His admonition to beware the danger posed to democracy by those who seek 'freedom from the necessity of informing themselves and making up their own minds concerning these tremendous complex ands difficult questions.'"
That is a tool used quite effectively by the conservative media apparatus.

One of the intriguing subjects in "Republican Gomorrah" was the discovery of Sarah Palin, who discovered her, how and what they did to promote her.
Another is the general history of the religious right on homosexuality and hypocrisy.
Contrasting the downfall of Larry Craig and Ted Haggard with conservatives like David Vitter and Newt Gingrich.
Added to the mix is the "kingmaker" that believes his endorsement is essential for any potential Republican presidential candidate.
Look too deeply into the conservative religious right and you see double-standards and lots of activity that runs counter to Scripture.
On page 42 the author writes "Under Reconstructionist rules of engagement, lying, deception, and stealth are considered legitimate tactics and are even encouraged."

This book is thoroughly documented and is a fast read. More important is what it exposes in the Republican Party and how that element wormed it's way in.
This is a fairly current work and one that every American voter should read.

title: Authentic characters make this a charming series starter
text:
I love how Austin's stories all knit together within the same small town community! You don't have to have read the other books in the series to enjoy each one individually, but by reading them all you get a fuller picture and more background on each of the characters. This start to the Bonfire Boys is a perfect example, taking minor characters from her other Love on Main series and putting them front and center.

Wild horses was a lot of fun, with city-girl-goes-country vibes. I loved Theron's inner battle and his relationship with his mother hits an unexpectedly heart-wrenching crux near the end. I didn't expect such a real moment in a romance novel, so it was a delightful surprise.

Skye is a satisfyingly believable character, with childhood damage and a lot of self-esteem issues. The way Austin describes her approach to and opinion of her paintings is incredibly accurate and gives the story an authenticity that many romance novels lack. Skye also gets her own personal wins that are unrelated to the romance, making you root for her even more. This (in addition to the sense of tight-knit small town community and over-protective family members) helps set a relatable stage full of players the reader can identify with.

Age gap usually isn't my thing, but this one worked fine for me. Skye is far more mature than her age. I enjoyed the self-conscious girl meets worshipping boy and city-vs-country tropes more. Theron has just the right amount of alpha-hole attitude and the steam is top notch. Looking forward to more in this series!

title: Sebastian has been trapped inside a dark dimension, and the three horsemen will do anything
text:
The final book of the Riders duology, and I’m happy with how it ended. Seeker by Veronica Rossi picks up where Riders left off. Sebastian has been trapped inside a dark dimension, and Darryn and the remaining three horsemen will do anything to bring him back.

One thing that I don’t care for about this book is the romance. Not every story needs a love story, especially a story that’s so tightly focused on a group of friends. The romance didn’t add to the story and Darryn’s continuous pulling away from Gideon was exasperating by the middle of the book.

Cutting the romance out of the story, like Riders, it’s a very neat story with a unique point of view. The remaining horsemen are doing all they can to find Bass in The Rift. The Rift forces them to face their fears, and face their innermost demons.

Without giving much away, the journey to find Sebastian is one full of haunting memories and really learning more about the characters. I don’t feel like there was as much character development as their was in the previous book, but I don’t think that it’s really a bad thing with this book. I also wish that this book only had Darryn’s or only Gideon’s point of view, like the first book, and not bouncing between both.

I do wish there were more books in the series. Books from the other horsemen’s points of views would be interesting, and I’d definitely read them. All in all, a series that is enjoyable and provides a pretty unique premise for the characters.

Build quality is surprisingly solid — the casing didn’t crack, and seams held up. They’re lightweight and comfortable, so I use them daily for calls and music. Battery life has been consistent with the product specs; no sudden drains or charging issues after the wash incident. Customer support was responsive when I emailed about care tips before my laundry mishap (yes, I felt sheepish), and they gave practical advice that matched my experience.

If you’re clumsy like me or have small pockets that eat earbuds, these are a great buy. I won’t deliberately put them through the washer again, obviously, but it’s incredibly reassuring to know they can survive that kind of accidental abuse. Highly recommend for anyone who needs reliable, durable earbuds that can handle real life.

title: The kind of book that you'll be reluctant to finish.
text:
Ever since the quality of Elizabeth George's books took a nosedive, I've been searching for another favorite mystery author. I've found her. And interestingly, like Ms. George, Deborah Crombie is an American woman who sets her mysteries in England.

The book has three threads: one is the ongoing romantic relationship between Superintendent Kincaid and his partner, Gemma James. A second is the mystery itself, involving a beautiful woman whose body is found carefully laid out in a park. The third is the genesis of the relationship among some of the characters/suspects and their families, a relationship which began back when English children were transported to the countryside to spare them the horrors of the World War II Blitz.

All three themes are handled beautifully. The characters of Duncan Kincaid and Gemma James continue to develop believably throughout this series. (This is, I believe, the sixth Kincaid/James book). The real-life problems and uncertainties they encounter while trying to maintain their family and professional obligations, and leave time for themselves and each other, will strike a believable chord with anyone old enough to have gone through this phase of life. The mystery is complex and unpredictable enough to be challenging but not confusing. The ending is beautiful - it settles both the mystery and the unresolved pain from the events of the 1940's.

If you haven't discovered the Crombie/Kincaid/James series yet, I recommend starting with the first one, "A Share in Death," which was nominated for an Agatha as best first novel of 1993. But I've read all of the first six, and they're all excellent.

title: A shamanic journey
text:
In this seventh instalment of Stoner's (and friends') adventures, Stoner and her business partner Marylou have moved their travel agency from Boston to Shelburne Falls. This small New Age town is perfect for Aunt Hermione's psychic activities and a new start for teacher Gwen, Stoner's life partner. But is seventy-five-year-old Hermione eventually getting old, or is her forgetfulness caused by hungry ghosts trying to steal her soul? It is up to reluctant believer Stoner to take a shamanic journey and save her aunt.

While previously her adventures mostly involved down-to-earth detective work on the side, Stoner is no stranger to shamanic journeying ('Grey Magic') and has even experienced time travel ('Captive in Time'). However she'd rather have a normal day-to-day life even if she feels like something is missing, despite Gwen's devoted love.

'Shaman's Moon' carries the trademark humour and feminist ideas of the Stoner McTavish series, even if no one is perfect. This volume, first published in 1998, is infused with light touches of philosophy and a dose of Native-American spirituality. It is captivating and colourful, and I guess would be pivotal in the series if Sarah Dreher had written more. I believe there is an 8th volume ('Love Murders'), but it is out of print or unavailable.

Sadly the author died in spring 2012. I'll be forever grateful to Sarah Dreher for creating one of my favourite fictional characters: the neurotic –but lovable, and forever hypothesizing too much, Stoner McTavish, a womon weary of cats, devoted to her aunt Hermione, passionately in love with her partner Gwen, and generally understanding of her best friend Marylou.

text:
I’ve tried several refill powders and capsules for my dog’s water fountain and this one is by far the best. I appreciate that a little goes a long way: one pouch lasted longer than I expected, so it’s economical compared with other brands I’ve used that required daily dosing. The formula doesn’t affect the fountain’s mechanics; no clogging, no buildup, and the filters continue to work normally.

My dog is picky about water — he prefers running water and will avoid bowls that taste off — but he took to his fountain instantly after I started using this refill. I noticed fewer paw-dips and less slime at the surface, which tells me the product is doing what it promises. Also, there’s no chemical smell like some other refills had, which made me worry about additives. This one feels safe and mild, and the ingredients list is straightforward.

Overall I’m very satisfied. It’s affordable, effective, and easy to use. If you have a pet water fountain and want a refill that actually keeps the water tasting fresh and encourages your pet to drink more, I’d recommend this without hesitation.

title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I’ve been using these for a few weeks after deciding to switch from my old gel pens to something the office kept recommending. There are definitely pros and cons, which is why I’m giving three stars.

On the plus side, the pens look and feel professional. The barrel is solidly built and has a pleasant weight — not too light, not too heavy — so they don’t feel cheap when you hand them out in meetings. The ink dries faster than my previous pens, which is great for left-handed notes and reduces smudging. The lines are consistent at a medium thickness; good for everyday note-taking, signing documents, and printing charts. The black ink is a true black and photocopies clearly without ghosting.

However, the experience isn’t flawless. First, the grip section is slightly slippery. If you tend to write for long stretches, your fingers start to feel a bit tired because there isn’t much cushioning. Second, a few of the pens in the pack (about 2 out of 12) started to feel scratchy after a couple of weeks, like the tip wasn’t as smooth as the others. They still write, but the feel is noticeably different and a little annoying. Also, while the ink dries faster than my old pens, it still smears a little on cheaper paper stock — not a dealbreaker, but something to be aware of if you frequently use lower-quality notebooks or thermal paper.

Refill availability is another concern. The product description hinted at long-lasting cartridges, but the pens don’t appear to be easily refillable, and I couldn’t find compatible refills locally. If you plan to use these heavily, be prepared to replace the entire pen instead of just swapping a cartridge.

Overall, these pens are solid for everyday office use: they look professional, write cleanly, and mostly avoid smudging. But the inconsistent tip quality in my pack, the slippery grip, and uncertain refill options mean they’re not perfect. If you want a reliable, mid-range pen for occasional to moderate use, these are a fine choice. If you’re looking for something with an ergonomic grip or long-term refillable convenience, you might want to keep looking.

I picked up this book expecting stories about the most notorious rock stars, and it definitely delivers on that front. The author covers a wide range of artists from different eras, offering juicy anecdotes about their wild antics on tour and off stage. Some chapters are better than others, in my view, with the sections on the 70s and 80s being particularly engaging and well-researched. But there are a few drawbacks. The book sometimes feels more like a list of scandalous events rather than a deep analysis of why these musicians behaved the way they did. I was hoping for more insight into their creative process or personal struggles, not just the party stories and hotel trashing. Also, a few of the "bad boys" profiled seemed a bit tame compared to others, making the title feel slightly exaggerated. The editing could have been tighter, as I noticed a couple of repetitive phrases slipped through.

Overall, it.

title: First impression and spooling line on the 2000 model.
text:
First impression:
- Body looks solid.
- if you can get it for about $20.00, you can't really complain, it's no $100 reel nor $200.00 but It will do the job.
- it's a good throw away, travel, back up reel at that price that can handle big fish. I would recommend spending more if you want something nicer but it would cost 2 or 3 times more.
-2000 spool size is too big. It's comparable to a 4000 spool. It's much deeper than a 2000. If I had to do it again I'll try for the 1000 instead for most applications.
- the line clip as shown on the picture fell off probably 3 times when messing with it at home or just spooling it. (I will probably try to glue the clip that holds it down together underneath before I end up losing it.) Highly recommend checking that all screw are tighten properly, you wouldn't want to loose any screw.
- the drag jumps from 33lb to no drag or 2/3lbs in about 10 clicks or a 90 degree dial turn. It's not very sensitive, it adjust at about 2/3lbs increments per clicks. You will probably need to set your drag gently to match your line if you do not want the line to snap under pressure for lighter lines. The drag is not ideal if you want to achieve a certain adjustable drag while fishing. Your drag might be too loose or too tight.
- line lay isn't impressive. It's ok at best just as shown. Not even. But it's only $20.00. When you fill pass 60%, it's hard not to get a few loose wrap. Tried to respool it couple times, I still have a few loose wrap every time. If you are picky and keep it under 60% you might be ok.

My guess is this reel will do the job for most applications and big fishes. The drag seems as if it will have very little to no play for some applications.

I will update after testing it enough on the water.

title: One of the most enlightening books on politics from the ...
text:
I picked this up on a whim, mostly because the description promised to cut through the noise of modern political discourse, and I am so glad I did. As someone who generally finds political theory dry and overly academic, I was surprisingly hooked from the very first chapter. The author has a rare gift for taking complex, tangled concepts and unraveling them with clarity and humor that never feels condescending. It does not feel like reading a textbook; it feels more like having a deep, insightful conversation with a wise friend who genuinely wants you to understand how the machinery of power really works.

What struck me most was the relevance. You might expect a book on politics to feel dated quickly, but the arguments here are timeless. The historical examples are chosen with precision, and the parallels to current events are drawn without being heavy-handed. I found myself pausing often to highlight passages that challenged my own assumptions, which is the sign of truly engaging non-fiction. It forced me to look at recent news cycles with a critical eye rather than just accepting the prevailing narratives. This is not just a book for politicians or academics; it is essential reading for any citizen who wants to participate more meaningfully in their democracy. It has genuinely expanded my perspective and equipped me with better tools to analyze the world around me. If you are looking for a page-turner that also enriches your mind, this is it. Five stars, easily.

title: Worst air mattress
text:
I never write negative reviews because I prefer to give people the benefit of the doubt, but this air mattress is absolutely the worst purchase I have made in the last five years. I bought it specifically for a weekend camping trip with my family, thinking it would be a convenient alternative to inflating and deflating sleeping bags every single night. That was a massive mistake. I followed the instructions exactly, using the recommended pump to inflate it to the maximum pressure level indicated in the manual. For the first thirty minutes, it seemed firm enough. I felt confident. However, by the time I actually got into bed, I could already feel a significant loss of support. It did not take long at all for the bottom side to begin drooping, creating a hammock effect that was incredibly uncomfortable and bad for my back.

By the second hour of sleep, I had to wake up multiple times because the mattress was slowly deflating on its own. I checked every seam and valve to ensure it was closed tightly, but there was no leak anywhere. It was just the material itself expanding and failing to hold the air pressure properly. The construction feels incredibly flimsy and cheap. The surface texture is rough and provides almost no grip, so I kept sliding off to one side throughout the entire night. It was a cold, hard, lumpy nightmare. I tried using the electric pump again in the morning to re-inflate it, but it barely went up. I am genuinely shocked that this product is still on the market with such a low rating that hasn't deterred buyers. Do not waste your money on this garbage. If you need an air mattress, save your time and go buy a reputable brand from a well-known manufacturer. This item is essentially trash wrapped in plastic. I threw it in the recycling bin immediately after this trip. It is an insult to customers who pay full price for comfort and reliability. I am extremely disappointed and will never trust this brand again.

title: Erik Larson leaves us wanting more...
text:
I read Erik Larson's book with great curiosity and high expectations, given the stellar reviews it has received in the media and academia. After finishing it, I have to admit I was torn between contradictory feelings:
- on one hand, the research is exhaustive and the reconstruction of the time he covers (basically July 1933-June 1934) is awesome, with great character depiction and an amazing ability to make intrigues in the State Department and events in Berlin come alive.
- on the other hand, the book left me deeply frustrated for at least 2 major reasons:

1) some major questions are left completely unanswered, esp. was Martha Dodd a Soviet spy? How did her obvious promiscuity not constitute more of an issue for the State Department, her father or a vulnerability to the German secret services?

2) even more importantly, what happens after the Night of the Long Knives (June 30, 1934)??? Dodd stayed in post until December 1937, i.e. another three and a half years (!) but barely a word is said about events during that time and his role in the American reaction to these events.

I would understand this silence if nothing had happened between June 1934 and the Anschluss, but there were extraordinary events that deserved at least a mention:
- the assassination of the Austrian chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss, which led to major tension between Germany and Italy, and took place less than a month after the June 1934 "epilogue" to the book
- the Saar referendum in January 1935
- the introduction of the Nuremberg laws in September 1935
- the referendum and remilitarization of Rhineland in March 1936
- the start of the Spanish Civil war in July 1936
All of these events were major milestones in the accession of Hitler to absolute power and the unstoppable march towards a world war, and it is unthinkable that Dodd (or Larson for that matter) has nothing to say about them... If the sources or archival materials dried up after Dodd's first year in Germany, why doesn't Larson tell us so and explain why he covers only the first 22% or so of his tenure as US ambassador !!!

Overall, a great read, but one that barely scratches the surface of a fascinating subject.

text: I honestly wasn’t sure what to expect when I ordered this product, largely because I had seen conflicting opinions online about its texture and efficacy. After finally using it for about two weeks, I feel like I have a pretty balanced perspective to share with you all. The primary selling point for me was the marketing claim that this could double as both a facial treatment and a hair conditioner. Unfortunately, this split personality is exactly where the product falls short for me. When I tried applying it to my face, the texture was far too abrasive. It felt less like a gentle exfoliant and more like crushed rock, which left my sensitive cheeks feeling irritated and slightly red the next morning. I have dry skin, and this definitely stripped away any natural oils, making my complexion look dull rather than radiant. I almost returned it because of that experience, but then I decided to give it another chance on my hair. This is where the product actually shines, quite literally. My hair is thick, curly, and notoriously difficult to moisturize. When I used it as a deep conditioning mask for my scalp and lengths, the results were undeniable. It detangled effortlessly, added serious shine, and left my curls defined without being heavy or greasy. I could feel the moisture penetrating the strands immediately. So, while I cannot recommend this for anyone looking for a gentle facial exfoliator, it is a solid addition to your hair care routine if you have coarse or dry hair. It earns three stars because it is mediocre at its marketed primary function but excellent at a secondary one. Do your research and know your skin type before committing to this, or you might end up with irritated skin like I did.

title: Flyover Nation- A window into our country's soul.
text:
I bought Flyover Nation out of curiosity and finished it in two sittings — surprised, moved, and a little ashamed that I’d underestimated what a “travel through America” book could do. The author doesn’t romanticize or caricature; instead, he listens. The portraits of small towns, factory floors, church basements, and open highways are honest and granular, full of people whose stories stay with you. What I appreciated most was the balance: empathy without sentimentality, critique without condescension. The writing is clear and often quietly lyrical, making the book both informative and emotionally resonant.

As someone who grew up in the Midwest but has lived in cities for years, this felt like a necessary reminder of the complexity and dignity of places often dismissed as “flyover.” It also challenged some of my assumptions and opened new ones. Thought-provoking, humane, and beautifully observed — a book I’ll recommend and return to.

title: World War One's Pearl Harbor?
text:
If we remember anything at all from our high school history class about why the United States got into World War I, it might have something to do with unrestricted submarine warfare. But the Zimmermann Telegram, if it was even mentioned, has long disappeared from memory, along with most of the other "facts" we learned in school. Barbara Tuchman, in this superb little book, makes a strong case for the argument that it was the revealing of the contents of this one message that convinced the American public that war with Germany was necessary.

The account reads like a spy thriller, which in fact it is. But there is not one statement which cannot be documented. Tuchman had access to American, British and German records which clearly illustrate the process of decision-making for each of the governments involved. The author has a knack for encapsulating her view of the often unimpressive character of the major players.

By 1916 World War I had degenerated into a horrible bloody stalemate from which there was no escape. Each side was desperate for fighting to end, but could accept nothing less than defeat of the enemy. None of the belligerents were prepared to consider Wilson's efforts toward "peace without victory." The only solution for the Allies was to bring the United States into the war, and for the Central Powers, to keep her out. Germany was convinced that, through unrestricted submarine warfare, against neutral as well as belligerent shipping, she could force Britain to capitulate in a few months. The Allies were hoping for a German blunder that would finally drag the U.S. into the war, and Britain did have a secret weapon of which the Germans knew nothing; she had broken the German diplomatic code and was reading all German international messages, both cable and radio. How this all played out is the theme of this little volume. It is illuminating, with respect to this important turning point in world history, and to the processes by which nations are governed.

title: Lois good on the counter
text:
I’ve been using the Lois “Good on the Counter” set for about six weeks and overall I’m pleased with the purchase — it’s earned a solid 4 stars from me. I bought it primarily as a functional and attractive way to keep small kitchen items tidy on my countertop, and it delivers on both counts.

The design is simple and modern, which fits nicely with my mostly neutral kitchen. The materials feel sturdy; the weighted base keeps it from tipping when I reach for items, and the finish has held up well to daily use and occasional splashes. Assembly was minimal and straightforward — just a few pieces that snapped together — and the whole unit feels well-made rather than cheap.

Functionally, it’s great for organizing cooking utensils, a couple of fresh fruit, and the stray mail and shopping list that always seems to collect on the counter. The compartments are a good size: deep enough for spatulas and wooden spoons, but not so wide that it dominates the counter. I also appreciate the little non-slip pads on the bottom that protect the surface beneath.

Why not five stars? A couple of small issues. First, the paint finish has started to show faint scuffs where metal utensils rub against it — not a dealbreaker, but noticeable if you look closely. Second, while the size is perfect for my apartment kitchen, it might be a bit small for someone who wants a true catch-all for larger items or a big family’s cooking tools. Finally, the price felt a touch high compared to similar organizers I’ve seen, though the build quality somewhat justifies it.

In short, the Lois counter organizer is a stylish, practical addition to a mid-sized kitchen. It looks good, functions well, and will keep your everyday items within reach — just temper expectations if you need heavy-duty capacity.

title: Finally, a wired adapter that works with my Insignia Roku TV
text:
I’d been struggling for months to get a stable wired Ethernet connection on my Insignia Roku TV. Wi‑Fi kept dropping during streaming and gaming, and every “universal” Ethernet adapter I tried either wasn’t recognized by the TV or caused buffering and weird audio sync issues. I ordered this wired adapter out of desperation and it has been a night-and-day difference.

Installation was simple — plug the USB end into the TV’s USB port and plug the Ethernet cable into the adapter. The TV immediately recognized the connection without any fuss. No extra drivers, no fiddling through menus beyond selecting “Wired” instead of Wi‑Fi. Once connected, my TV showed a solid wired connection and streaming apps opened noticeably faster.

Performance-wise, it’s rock solid. 4K streaming on Netflix and Amazon Prime plays smoothly with no buffering, and online gaming feels much more responsive. I ran a speed test through the TV and the results were consistent with what I get on my wired laptop. The adapter stays cool to the touch, and I haven’t seen any disconnects after several weeks of daily use.

Build quality seems good — the connector feels sturdy and the cable is a decent thickness (not flimsy). It’s unobtrusive and doesn’t add much bulk behind the TV. My only minor gripe is that it makes the single USB port occupied, but that’s a small trade-off for reliable Ethernet.

If you have an Insignia Roku TV and need a dependable wired connection, this adapter works exactly as advertised. Finally, a wired solution that actually works with my TV — very happy with this purchase.

Fr. Emmanuel does an admirable job of commenting on various liturgical questions, and does not balk at some of the more contentious issues (cf. A second edition would be most welcome, as there are a number of page cross-references which are incorrect, and at least one diagram is mentioned which does not appear in the text. Much recourse in footnotes is made to electronic sources, which may simply be the direction of modern scholarship, but does evoke a double-take when used in a field that stretches back millennia.

In all, a wonderful start, and a second edition to take care of minor housekeeping issues will be most enthusiastically received.

The printing quality is decent and the artwork is fine, but none of that matters when the basic functionality is broken. If you have kids, forget letting them handle this right away; I had to do the tedious sorting myself to avoid them seeing duplicate groups in a row. It took me 20–30 minutes to mix the stacks properly so the game didn’t feel repetitive. I also noticed a few cards that looked slightly bent from being tightly stacked, which wouldn’t happen with a properly randomized deck.

Customer service wasn’t helpful when I reached out—their response was generic and essentially shrugged that some people prefer to shuffle themselves. That’s not the point. The product should arrive ready to play. For the price, I expected better packaging and quality control. If you’re okay spending extra time prepping the deck for play, maybe it will work for you. title: Felt like a boss shutting down sector 12
text:

He's small enough to fit in your pocket so you can stroll around Cybertron with him to keep those other sectors in line. War for Cybertron reference aside....

PARENTS: This is an awesome little toy for young and adult Transformers fans. Shockwave is this character's name and he is one of the primary villains (Decepticon team) in the Transformer shows. He's basically 2nd in command to Megatron (the chief villain/antagonist). For those children, I'd recommend the 1-step line of toys (Cybertron Adventures and Rescue Bots). My 4 year old has a lot of exposure to my complex Transformer collection, so he powers through 13 steps without a sweat. Note that the hand cannon is detachable, so be wary of losing this to the couch cushion abyss like the rest of your kid's toy accessories. Lastly, this is a "core class" figure, so it's relatively small at 3.5" when standing in robot mode.

My opinion of this model is very positive. For such a small scale, the sculpting work is super detailed and it does a near perfect job of capturing Shockwave's "Gen1" appearance (except for the angry brow). His robot-mode transformation is engineered well, tight joints/pivots and no fear of breaking any brittle pieces. The alt-mode (a tank?) is acceptable, but I've no major complaints about either mode.

title: Seems to be a good product.
text:
I have been searching for a reliable solution for my golden retriever, Buster, for quite some time now, and I must admit, I approached this purchase with a mix of high hopes and significant skepticism. My dog has always been prone to chewing on things he shouldn't, particularly during his teething phase and when he is left alone for extended periods. The product description promised durability, mental stimulation, and hours of engaging playtime, which sounded too good to be true. After using it for about three weeks, I feel compelled to share my honest experience to help other pet owners make an informed decision.

First, let’s address the build quality. On one hand, the material feels sturdy and the design is intuitive enough for a dog to understand quickly. Buster picked it up in less than five minutes, which was impressive. He spends a good amount of time trying to get the treats out, and that alone has kept him occupied while I work from home. The Kong-like shape is effective for freezing treats, which adds an extra layer of engagement during hot summer days. From a utility standpoint, it does exactly what it claims to do regarding keeping a pet busy and distracted from household furniture.

However, there are notable downsides that prevent this product from earning a five-star rating in my book. The main issue is the cleanup process, which is unnecessarily complicated. It has many small crevices and seams where food particles get trapped. No matter how much I scrub it with hot soapy water, I still worry about bacteria buildup or that strange smell that sometimes lingers after washing. This is a significant drawback for a product that is supposed to be a daily staple in your home. Additionally, while Buster loves it, he has managed to crack a small section after a particularly aggressive play session, despite the claims of being "indestructible." It hasn’t broken apart completely, but it has raised concerns about its long-term durability for powerful chewers.

For light to moderate chewers who are willing to put in the extra effort to clean it thoroughly, this might be a decent option. It offers good value for the price point and provides the mental enrichment that dogs need. However, if you have a heavy-duty destroyer like mine, or if you simply do not have the time to meticulously clean complex toys, you might want to look elsewhere. It is a decent product overall, but it lacks the polish and robustness that would make it a true household essential. I would recommend it with caveats, not as a blanket endorsement for every dog owner.

title: Didn’t last a day
text:
I was genuinely excited to try this product after reading the glowing reviews and seeing the impressive marketing claims. It promised durability, comfort, and an easy setup process, which seemed like exactly what I needed for my energetic golden retriever. I spent the afternoon assembling it, following the instructions carefully, and everything seemed to fit together perfectly at first glance. It looked sturdy on my hardwood floors, and my dog gave it a quick sniff before ignoring it for a few hours. That quiet period, however, was short-lived. By the next morning, the structural integrity was already compromised. One of the main support legs had snapped right at the base, despite me not applying any excessive force or weight. I didn’t even have my two hundred-pound mastiff near it; it was just sitting there.

The plastic material feels cheap and brittle, not at all like the heavy-duty resin advertised in the description. When I tried to tighten the loose connections, the threads stripped completely, rendering the entire assembly useless. I reached out to customer support, expecting some level of assistance given the obvious defect, but was met with a generic email asking for more photos. It has been three days, and I still haven’t heard back. For a product at this price point, I expected at least a week of usage before any signs of wear, let alone catastrophic failure. It is incredibly frustrating to buy something that is supposed to make pet care easier, only to have it become another piece of clutter in my garage. I cannot recommend this to anyone who wants something reliable. Save your money and invest in a brand with a better reputation for quality control. My dog is currently happier with an old, worn-out toy that has lasted years, rather than this shiny new disaster that fell apart before I even finished my morning coffee.

I'm sure to get this out the door, they worked with beta and early release products, but even their editors couldn't get naming down? title: Chop Suey Culture
text:
If you like Chinese food, you should read this book. It will tell you everything you should have wondered about chop suey, fortune cookies, the Chinese restaurant industry and the Chinese people who have brought more than food to the United States

Ms. Lee uses her healthy curiosity and excellent research skills to study something we generally take for granted -- Chinese food is so unbiquitous as to be invisible, except when we're hungry. Being the daughter of Chinese immigrants and a New York Times reporter gives Ms. Lee the right lenses for studying her subject and produces insights that are subtle, interesting and thought-provoking. For example: How best to know the actual output of a Chinese restaurant when thinking about buying it? Count the garbage bags in the alley. Why were did Chinese laundries and restaurants survive 19th Century bigotry against the Chinese? Because cooking and washing were women's work and didn't threaten the white male labor force.

Equally as good as Ms. Lee's insights is her writing style. She has a tone that is a bit ironic, a bit whimsical. She appreciates the goofiness of what she is investigating, but also treats the topic respectfully. These are fine balances for a writer to maintain. And she brings many of her points home with a tidy turn of phrase: "Young professionals loved the idea that food could come from a phone rather than a stove." Or, "Common wisdom from one culture is perplexing in another." Or, finally, by describing American soy sauce as a "Frankensauce chemical counterfeit."

text:
I am writing this review because I feel completely cheated by my purchase. I ordered this item thinking I was getting a high-quality toy for my child, given the somewhat polished product images on the website. However, the reality is that this is one of the cheapest, flimsiest pieces of plastic I have ever encountered. The moment I opened the box, I could tell something was wrong. The packaging was torn and taped shut with cheap duct tape, which already raised some red flags, but I hoped for the best. The item itself felt lightweight and hollow, lacking the solid construction I expected from a premium toy.

On the first day, everything seemed okay, or at least passable. My kid played with it for a few hours without any immediate issues, though I noticed several loose seams along the edges. I didn’t think much of it, assuming it would settle in. That was my mistake. By the end of the second day, a small crack had appeared near the main hinge mechanism. I tried to gently press it back into place, warning my child to be careful, but I had no idea how fragile the material actually was. Then, yesterday, exactly three days after I received it, the toy completely broke apart. The main structural piece snapped clean off while my son was simply holding it.

It did not fall; it was not dropped; it just disintegrated from normal handling. This is not durability; this is a complete failure of product quality. I have bought much cheaper toys before that lasted for years, and this item cost more than half of those, yet it has already become trash. I tried to contact customer service, but the response time is slow, and I fear they will blame user error, which is absurd. I cannot recommend this to anyone. If you are looking for something that will actually last through playtime, avoid this at all costs. You are throwing your money away on a product designed to break immediately. I am deeply disappointed and will never buy from this seller again. The lack of basic integrity in the materials is unacceptable for a toy meant for children. Save your money and look elsewhere for a better, safer, and longer-lasting option.

title: Lacking in depth
text:
I really wanted to like this book. The premise was intriguing, and the early chapters had me hooked. But by the halfway point, I realized the author was just skimming the surface of what could have been a rich, complex story. The characters are sketched out with only the broadest of strokes—their motivations feel pasted on, their internal conflicts resolved with a single conversation. The world-building is similarly thin: we’re told about politics, history, and magic systems, but they never feel lived in or consequential.

What frustrates me most is the lack of depth in the central themes. The book gestures at weighty ideas—identity, power, sacrifice—but never digs into them. Every time it sets up a moral dilemma or a philosophical question, it either dodges it with a convenient plot twist or explains it away in a paragraph. I kept waiting for the narrative to slow down and wrestle with its own implications, but it just barrels forward on plot mechanics. The conflict feels manufactured; the stakes are high in theory but hollow in practice because we never truly understand why anyone believes what they do.

I’ve read other works by this author, and they handled nuance much better. This one reads like a rushed first draft that needed another round of revision to deepen the characters and the world. It’s not a terrible read—the prose is competent and the pacing keeps you turning pages—but I finished it feeling unsatisfied, as if I’d eaten a meal with no flavor. If you’re looking for something thought-provoking or emotionally resonant, look elsewhere. This is a shallow pool dressed up to look like an ocean.

title: This was one of the better books I’ve read so far this year
text:
This was one of the better books I’ve read so far this year. It was a nice surprise, being a debut novel about parenthood: it could have gone either way.

As the synopsis says, this is a character-driven story, and that’s what makes it so interesting and enjoyable. These are people that any toddler parent knows all too well. If you’ve ever been in a playgroup or online parenting forum/group, you can relate on some level to this book (albeit an extreme version of reality). It’s a look into modern parenting, in a yuppie world where everyone is following their own “parenting truth” and trying not to judge (though failing at doing so) others’. It is also a window into the complexities of “early-mid”adult life (if you can all it that)- relationships with others and with ourselves, and what is most important for each of us.

This book will make you smile, cringe and even think a little bit. What are the sacrifices we make for our families, for our loved ones, for our children? What are the personal costs? What wouldn’t we do to find some meaning behind the every day mundane? What is the difference between friendship and support?

I recommend it for any parent of young(ish) kids looking for an enjoyable summer read.

title: Twisty Rods for Beachy Waves or Coily Curls
text:
My hair has lots of different kinds of curls in it, from tight coils near the nape of my neck, to spirals, all the way to slightly wavy hair at the crown of my head. I get a more consistent curl when I use curlers! I've been using large foam curlers for a while to get large, uniform waves that straighten out over a few days, but I wanted to try a curler that would give me tighter curls.

The Ohuhu Twist Flex Rods come with 7 different curl sizes, and each size has 6 rollers. The rollers are color-coded by size, so you think I'd be able to find all 7 curlers, but apparently I thought there were only 6 when I took the picture. I'd never used these kinds of curlers before, but they were simple to use. I used the two largest sizes, and took a small section of hair and put the end of it in the middle of a roller. Then, I rolled the hair up into the roller, making sure to keep the hair in the center of the rod. Twisting the ends together keeps the curler in place.

I tried to let my hair air-dry with the curlers in, but I have a LOT of hair, and knew that could take days, so after a few hours, I put on my bonnet dryer and finished the job. I was pretty happy with my ringlets! I did muss them up for a nice, beachy curly-wave, too. I really liked getting the curl all the way to my crown, and how much lift it gave the top of my 'do. And, the curls weren't tangly like my hair can get if I let it completely air dry. I could run my fingers through them and get a messy, beachy wave - and still no frizz or tangles.

(I received this product for review purposes. My opinions are my own. For more information and pictures, please see my blog, Lit From Within.)

title: I cannot express fully how much I enjoyed Durga Chew-Bose's collection of essays
text:
I cannot express fully how much I enjoyed Durga Chew-Bose's collection of essays. I felt drunk on this book. I rarely underline or write in books, but I couldn't help myself with this one: Chew-Bose's writing is so unique, yet so relatable at the same time. She put to words feelings I've had—of being young, of being a woman, of the relationship you have with your parents—that I've never expressed, feelings and thoughts I didn't realize others shared too, that I now realize are possibly universal parts of growing up. I read, reread, wrote down passages, sighed after reading many more. I savored this book.

"Your hot friend on a balmy summer night telling you about some good news in her life is—how do I put this without sounding absurd? It's barometric. It's love and you love's power growing, and it's watching the elements cater to a woman who exudes."

"We are waking up to freckles dotting a person's back, and leveling that we might be in love—not with this person, but with freckles and downy morning light, because unfamiliar contours before 9 a.m. have a way. With someone new, even freckles become spotless. They are a surface blurred and time deferred. Everything begins simply enough."

I texted excerpts to friends, including the two above, and three asked to borrow it. Of course, I need to reread it a third time before I lend it out (I may just purchase a second copy). This book is a marvel—I can't wait to read what Chew-Bose writes next.

100% OE Replacement

If this is your trampoline, this mat is a perfect replacement for the original in thickness, stitching and quality of nylon tabs and galvanized rings. The only difference is the branding printed on the center and a vinyl cover over the stitching to protect from UV (better than the original being replaced from 2008).

You WILL need a spring tool and at least a second set of hands to install (or at least hand you springs). And the mat will seem too small at first.

TO INSTALL:
(read through all steps before starting)

NOTE 1: Counting mat rings / frame holes accurately is essential. Get off by 1 and you have to start over.

NOTE 2: Be careful to pull springs straight out (and keep an eye on it as you're pulling) from the mat ring to the frame hole so that the spring stays hooked in the point of the ring. Do not allow the spring to slip to one of the sides or a cascade of problems will ensue.

1) Select a ring on the mat and attach a spring to it and to the trampoline frame

2) Count 42 rings around on the mat and attach another spring

3) Count 42 holes around on the frame and attach the other end of that spring

4) Count 21 rings from either spring and add the next spring; do the same for holes and attach

5) Repeat step 4 on the opposite side

(You now have 4 springs attached at each of the 90º points, creating 4 quadrants)

6) In your first quadrant, count 10 rings and holes from a spring and attach another

7) In the quadrant directly across from your first, count 10 rings and holes and attach another

8) Repeat for the other 2 quadrants

9) Now start filling in the gaps, alternating to the opposite side every couple of springs. The idea is to keep alternating sides so that the tension remains as even as is possible.

***It might seem easier to just start working your way around, but the pull will become uneven, increasing the likelihood of having a ring slip.***

Feel free to message me for any further info.

title: A Funny Man Revealed
text:
I remember watching Steve Martin's seemingly meteoric rise from Tonight Show guest, to Saturday Night Live stalwart, to concert hall blockbuster. He made me laugh. He helped take the edge off the 70's. I remember leaving one of his Nassau Coliseum shows thinking that all in the world was good and it's ok to be goofy - for a little while anyway. It was from that melancholy recollection I read through this book.

While Martin's stand up humor was edgy, innovative, and visual, Born Standing Up is laced with a dry humor that sometimes brings chuckles one or two lines afterward. We can see that as is true for most seemingly overnight success stories there are years of hard work and sacrifice behind the sensation. Though there is only a small window into Steve's creative genius, you can see how his young life contributed to the product he presented on stage. Martin's stand up act was filled with silliness, idiocy, and just plain tomfoolery. In Born Standing Up we see the crafting of that act took an intellectual approach and technical dissection of how comedy works. Laced with stories of his family life, upstart employment, inspirations, encounters and collaborations with familiar performers from the era, and the eventual eruption of his show, Born Standing Up leads down a road of opportunities realized and acted upon.

Tracking the career of Steve Martin can be confusing. The performances of the stand up era are dramatically different from the ones we see in movies today. So different that when I played some of "Let's Get Small" for my kids (who are very familiar with the Cheaper by the Dozen dad) they had a hard time believing it is the same person. Born Standing Up reveals an underlying personality that is constant throughout Martin's career.

I believe this is a 5 star book for anyone who fondly remembers Martin's stand-up. Thanks Steve for making the world a little less serious!

title: Eyeliner didn't stick with lashes
text:
I really wanted to love this eyeliner. The pigmentation is great, the brush tip is precise, and it’s fine and precise, and it glides on smoothly without tugging. I’ve been using it for a week now and the color payoff is exactly what I look for in a daily liner—deep black, matte finish, no flaking or fading after a few hours. For the price point, it’s it a decent buy if you just need a standard liner.

However, I bought this specifically because the description implied it would work well with false lashes—either as a guide for placement or to help secure the band. That’s where it failed on both counts. The formula dries down fairly quickly, which means it doesn’t stay tacky enough to grip the lash band. When I tried applying the lashes immediately after the liner, still wet, and the glue just slid right off. liner just smudged into a mess without holding anything. I also tried using it as an adhesive over the band after applying regular lash glue—no improvement. The liner just sits on top and the lashes still lift within an hour.

It’s fine for regular eyeliner use, but if you have steady hands and don’t need it for lash applications, but if you’re looking for something that actually helps lashes stick or blend with falsies, this isn’t it. I’ll use up the bottle for everyday looks, but I’ll keep searching for a liner that actually delivers on the “with lashes” promise. Three stars because it does one job well, but not the job I needed it for.

title: Incredible life — even to a layman like me
text:
First let me preface this review by saying that you should NOT be turned off to this book if you know nothing about physics or mathematics. The author does an incredible job at explaining the semantics of Diracs theories while only seldom mentioning any syntax (his explanation of the delta function was impressive).

Now on to a life worth remembering. This book does an incredible job at commemorating not only the achievements of Dirac (along with his contemporaries, always making sure credit goes where credit is due) but also the person that was Dirac. You know it’s a good book when an author makes you feel as if you knew the bloke, even though he died before I was even born and lived across the globe.
The author meticulously builds up the image and story of Dirac, with no page going to waste. I know — a book about one of the most abstract theoretical physicists to ever live, how could this be fun? Read it and prepare to be surprised!

This book not only helped fill my knowledge gaps within the history of mathematics, but also provided days of thorough entertainment.

I would recommend this book to anyone interested in the history of mathematics and one of the pioneers of Quantum Mechanics.

10/10

As the host of The Wired Educator Podcast and the Director of Innovation and Instruction for Port Clinton Schools, it has always been my primary mission to celebrate and promote the voices of outstanding educators. I am proud to celebrate the outstanding work of Keven Rinaman and share his voice and message with the world.
The Wired Educator Motto is, “To Level Up and Make a Difference in the Lives of Students”. Keven’s book does that and more. Keven’s book emphasizes that students should be using devices to create MORE than they consume. I love the possibilities and direction Keven offers teachers to bring 3D printing to every grade and every content area.
It gives me great pride to help a fellow educator publish a physical book that another educator can hold in their hands, apply in their classroom, add to and pass along to others.
This is the first book published by Wired Educator. As I add these final words to this manuscript: I can feel the impact this book will have in students’ lives, I can picture the amazing creations students will design and produce, I can hear the laughs of failed prints, and the cheers of success as students and teachers collaborate together to create an environment of learning where experimentation, reflection on failure, and the tenacity to try again until they succeed is the norm.
Congratulations Keven on an amazing book and making a global impact on education. Well done.
Kelly Croy

title: Great tent - try not to set it up alone.....
text:
I bought this tent for a weekend family camping trip and overall it exceeded my expectations — sturdy, roomy, and well thought out. We’re a family of four (two adults, two kids) and the tent comfortably fit two queen air mattresses plus gear along the perimeter with room to sit. The fabric feels durable and the seams look well sealed; after a night of heavy rain nothing leaked and the ground stayed dry. Ventilation is excellent — the mesh windows and ceiling kept the inside from getting stuffy even in the afternoon heat, and the guy lines and stakes held firm when the wind picked up.

My only serious caveat, and the reason for the title of this review, is setup. Instructions are adequate but the poles and clips require an extra set of hands. I tried to wrestle it up solo and made it more stressful and slower than necessary — there were a few moments where I wished for a partner to help hold corners while I threaded poles. With two people the setup took under 15 minutes. Takeaway: don’t plan to put it up alone if you want a quick, frustration-free start to your outing.

Small touches I appreciated: the vestibule for muddy boots, interior pockets for lights/phones, and the heavy-duty zippers that felt solid. The packed size is reasonable for car camping. If you need a reliable family tent and can have at least two people for setup, this is a great purchase. Highly recommend.

title: Good to have on hand for emergencies
text:
I bought this a few months ago after a close call during a solo hike. I wasp on a remote trail. I wanted something compact that I could toss in my daypack and forget about until I really needed it. This fits that bill perfectly. The kit is not bulky at all it easily slides into the side pocket of my backpack or even my glove compartment without taking up much space.

The first thing I checked was the quality of the included tools. The knife is surprisingly sharp out of the box, the whistle is loud enough to hear from a good distance, and the fire starter works as intended. I tested the emergency blanket on a chilly evening just to see how much heat it reflects. It actually works. The compass is simple but functional for basic orientation. The little paracord is also came in handy for tying down a tarp when a sudden squall hit.

What I appreciate most is that nothing feels cheap or flimsy. For the components are well-made and packed securely. I have no doubt that if I were stuck out overnight this would keep me safe and comfortable until rescue. It gives peace of mind knowing I have a small but capable survival tool that does not require me to carry a heavy load.

I would recommend this to anyone who hikes, campers, or anyone who spends time outdoors. It also makes a thoughtful gift for friends just starting to explore backcountry. The price is more than fair for the quality. For the cost of a couple of fancy coffee drinks you are really getting a reliable backup plan in a tiny package. I have already bought a feeling I will never actually need to use it in a dire situation, but it is comforting to know it is there if I do. Five stars without hesitation.

title: Great Little Toy for Older Children and Adults
text:
I have been a fan of toy steam engines since I received a German made WILESCO engine for Christmas in 1961! This little engine by SunnyTech, a Chinese company, is very well made, with all brass parts, except for an O-ring to seal the boiler. When I first fired the engine up it ran like who-shot-john! I was rather amazed. This will make a great gift for any budding engineers that you may know, or any professional engineers, for that matter.
There are some pitfalls that the buyer should be aware of:
There are no instructions, at least in the one I bought has no instructions, just an exploded drawing showing how it should be put together. It is a good thing that I had experience with toy steam engines.
NEVER fill the boiler more than 2/3 full.
When running, it will spray some water, this is normal for a steam engine.
It does vibrate when running, place it on a stable surface.
The engine gets HOT when running. Take appropriate precautions.
Use alcohol as a fuel. Ethel or methyl alcohol (+95%) will work best. I tried 91% Isopropyl alcohol and it works fine, although it covered the boiler with soot. So you might want to avoid that.
NEVER use any petroleum derived fuel such as gasoline or Coleman fuel.
The engine is designed to only run for a few minutes on one boiler of water. Blow the lamp out immediately when the boiler is low on water or you may damage the engine with excess heat.
Remember, this is a toy but only for older children and adults.

title: Beautiful Photos - Good Healthy Recipes
text:
Mediterranean food has a reputation for being not only delicious, but healthy. The diet is rich in fruits and vegetables as well as healthy oils and lean meats and fish. There are dozens, maybe hundreds of good Mediterranean cookbooks out there, and one that is excellent and includes a huge number of recipes for variety is 1000 Mediterranean Meals: Every Recipe You Need for the Healthiest Way to Eat by Valentina Harris. This cookbook has everything: appetizers, side dishes, soups, salads, mains with or without meat and even desserts. Although they are touted as healthier dishes, they are still mouthwatering, and no one will suspect that eating them will contribute to better health.

Almost all of the recipes include a photograph, which makes the book appealing. Most cooks want to know what the dish should look like. The recipes are written in the classic style with a list of ingredients and easy-to-follow instructions that cooks at all levels can successfully make them.

The variety of the dishes is vast, and there is something for every taste. Most of the recipes include several variations to that everyone can individualize them to their personal tastes. The recipes come from several of the twenty-one countries that border the Mediterranean Sea. Popular classics are included, such as Hummus and Tzatziki, as well as some unique dishes like Huevos Revueltos and Egyptian Sweet Couscous.

Anyone who likes Mediterranean food will love reading and cooking from this excellent cookbook. There will be dozens of recipes that appeal to almost every cook.

Special thanks to NetGalley for supplying a review copy of this book.

title: Reliable printer and a good value
text:
I’ve been using this printer in my home office for about three months now and overall I’m very pleased with its reliability and value. Before buying I was primarily looking for something that would handle a moderate amount of printing — invoices, shipping labels, a few flyers, and the occasional photo — without fuss or a lot of maintenance. This model has mostly delivered on that promise.

Setup was straightforward. The software package included everything I needed and the wireless setup with my laptop and phone was quick and stable. I liked that the control panel is simple; no confusing menus or tiny icons. It connects to my network without dropping out, which was a major plus compared to a previous model I owned.

Print quality is good for everyday documents. Text comes out crisp and dark, and the pages are well-aligned. Color prints are decent for internal use—presentations and handouts look professional enough—but if you want gallery-quality photos, a dedicated photo printer would still be the better choice. Print speed is reasonable for a home office; large jobs take some time but nothing excessive. I appreciate that the printer doesn’t make a lot of noise during operation.

One of the strongest points is reliability. I’ve had very few paper jams and the ones that did occur were easy to clear thanks to accessible panels. Ink usage seems efficient; I get a fair number of pages per cartridge. Replacement cartridges aren’t the cheapest on the market, but they are competitively priced and easy to find, which reinforces the overall value proposition.

There are a couple of minor drawbacks. The mobile app is functional but lacks a few advanced features I’ve seen with other brands, and occasionally the scanner takes a second try to capture documents perfectly aligned. Also, while the machine supports automatic duplex printing, it sometimes hesitates on thicker paper types.

For the price point, this printer hits most marks: dependable, easy to use, and cost-effective for regular office tasks. I’m giving it four stars rather than five because of the few small quirks and because it’s not the absolute best choice if your primary need is high-end photo printing. If you need a solid, no-nonsense printer for everyday office work, this is a very good option.

text:
I have to admit, I picked up this book with a fair amount of skepticism. The title "Opened my EYES!" felt a bit dramatic, and I wasn't sure what to expect. But after reading it, I can honestly say it's the most accurate description possible. This book genuinely shifted the way I see things. It's not often that a single volume can change your entire perspective on something you thought you understood, but that's exactly what happened here.

The author presents complex ideas in a way that feels accessible and deeply personal. I found myself nodding along, then stopping to reread passages because they hit so close to home. What I appreciated most is that it doesn't just point out problems it offers practical ways to see them differently. The chapters are well-structured, each building on each other without becoming repetitive. There were moments when I actually felt a sense of relief realizing that the patterns I had been stuck in for years were not unique to me.

If you are someone who feels like you've been going through life on autopilot, or if you've ever wondered why certain situations keep repeating, this book is for you. It's not a quick fix, but it's a powerful starting point. I've already recommended it to three friends and plan to read it again to absorb the parts I might have missed. For anyone on the fence, just get it. It lives up to its title in the most honest way possible.

There were a few things I wasn't too happy with though and the first is that this did not come in its own box, and since I paid almost $50 for it, I really expected it to. Instead it arrived in a very large Amazon box (honestly it could have easily fit two of these and still had room) and the doll was simply wrapped in a clear plastic bag with a piece of tape along the bottom. All in all I think she was a little overpriced (mostly because of the legs) but not excessively so, and I do think this would be a nice display piece or good for an older child who is not going to play too rough with her. text:
I picked this up a few weeks ago when my old desk organizer finally gave out. The price was reasonable, so I figured I'd give it a shot. Overall, it's not a bad product by for anything too complex, but for basic day-to-day office supplies, it gets the job done. Assembly was fairly straightforward, though the instructions could be clearer. It took me about fifteen minutes to put together, which is fine, but I did notice a few of the screw holes didn't line up perfectly. These quite line up perfectly on the first try. The build quality is what I'd call "OK" in the title. It's sturdy enough to hold pens, paperclips, sticky notes, and a small notepad without flexing too much. The material feels like it will hold up for daily use, but I wouldn't trust it with anything heavy like a stapler or a large binder clip. My main disappointment is the lack of padding or non-slip on the base. It slides around on my desk more than I'd like when I reach for a pen. I ended up sticking some adhesive felt pads underneath, which solved the problem, but it's an extra step I shouldn't have to take. The compartments are a good size, though one or two are a bit too narrow for my thicker markers.

Overall, it's a perfectly functional organizer for someone who needs a simple, low-cost solution. It's not premium by any stretch, but for the price, you're getting exactly what you pay for. If you're looking for something that will last years and look great on your desk, you might want to invest a bit more. For me, it's serving its purpose well enough for now.

title: More Complex Than Expected, Still About Maids
text:
I demoed this game at release, and was at first a bit daunted at the amount of apparent setup. It's not that there's a lot of setup, but if you don't sort the cards after each use, you're going to spend the first twenty minutes before playing getting them all sorted then. This seems like a 'well duh' type of comment, but remember this is a game that appeals to two types of people: card gamers (who are used to scoop and box) and those moe gamers (who aren't going to want to wait to look at the pictures). If you are planned on introducing new gamers to Tanto Cuore, I greatly recommend that you have the game setup a head of time so you can dive right into it.

Game wise, it's not the deepest strategy in the world, but you can definitely play a few interesting tricks if you really put effort into it. This again can come as a shock to some gamers. Don't be deceived: It's the maids that are attracting players, and the idea that there could be actual gameplay to go with those maids throws a number of gamers off. Drake, an artist friend, was originally in it for the breasts; when he realized he was starting to lose, all the imagery faded out of his thoughts and he could have been playing with text-only cards.

It's very much a game that sells based on the images, obviously. However, if you get past the snorts and giggles, you can find an actually fun game with just enough strategy to play. Just keep it on a high shelf if you have young ones about.

title: Needed wheels
text:
I bought these replacement wheels because the original set on my cat’s rolling carrier started to squeak and wobble after a few years of use. I’d been putting off replacing them, but my carrier wouldn’t roll smoothly anymore and I was tired of careful maneuvering whenever I took my cat to the vet. Overall, these wheels did what I needed — so I’m giving four stars.

First, the fit was the most important part for me, and these matched the measurements listed in the description. Installation was straightforward: a little pop and snap into the socket, no tools required for the front caster wheels. The rear wheels needed a small screwdriver to remove a clip from the old set, but the package included clear instructions and a tiny plastic washer that made everything sit snugly. After swapping all four, the carrier rolled much more smoothly and quietly. No more loud scraping on tile or the awkward lurch when turning.

The materials feel decent for the price. The plastic is not super heavy-duty, but it’s sturdier than the flimsy wheels I had on the original carrier toward the end. They’ve handled a few months of regular use (weekly trips to the vet and occasional travel) without cracking or excessive wear. The bearings are adequate — not silky-smooth like higher-end casters, but good enough for a pet carrier that’s mostly moved short distances by hand.

That said, there are a couple of reasons I didn’t give five stars. One wheel arrived with a slight cosmetic scuff, and the axle housing on one piece felt a little looser than the others — it’s still worked fine but it gave me a moment of concern during installation. Also, the wheels don’t swivel quite as freely as the originals did, so turning on thick carpet still requires a bit of effort. If you have heavy or very active pets, or plan to pull the carrier over long distances, you might prefer a metal-bearing wheel or a branded replacement.

In summary: these wheels are a solid, affordable fix that saved me from buying a whole new carrier. They fit well, were easy to install, and restored smooth, quiet rolling for everyday use. A small quality-control improvement would make them perfect, but for the price they’re a practical and satisfactory replacement.

text:
This camera replaced my previous Canon (3MP PowerShot S30). I will only buy Canon cameras, their picture quality is superb for a point-n-shoot. What sold me on the SX120IS was the 10X optical zoom.

The 10X optical zoom is spectacular! It gets wonderful pictures of our kids on the baseball field, and at concerts and shows. Pictures that 3X optical zoom could never do. Pictures from 100 ft look like you were standing only 15 ft away. I've had other parents ask me to take pictures of their kids, because they couldn't get close enough for a good shot. Yes, 10X is awesome.

The 10 megapixels are good, and the pictures are still great, but I am not impressed by pixel count. The overall picture quality is as good as my previous 3 MP canon, but not better. However, now the files are 3.3 times larger on my hard drive. Slower to open, slower to upload to web, and harder to email. The up-side to 10 MP is when pictures need cropped, there are still plenty of pixels remaining to make a good 8.5x11 print.

Do not be taken by the 3.0" LCD. Yes, it is big. But the resolution is not tight, so even though the LCD is bigger there aren't more pixels in it. And the menu fonts are big. I would have been just as happy with a 2.5" LCD with a tighter resolution.

All of the shooting modes are great, and easy to use. This camera has more "special" modes than my last camera, and they are nice. But one mode it does not have, and I miss it, is the panoramic stitch-assist mode. If you try to do a pano stitch with this camera, you'll have to guess at where you left off.

Overall this is a great camera. I would recommend it to anyone who wants beautiful pictures and a lot of optical zoom. Can't beat the price either.
