title: Not for everyone, but provides unique principles to filter through the "noise"
text:
In today's work ecosystem of forced multitasking, being "busy" all the time, and never feeling comfortable saying "no", Essentialism provides unique principles for sorting through the noise and figuring out what is truly "essential". The author himself says brilliantly that "essentialism is not one more thing -- it's a whole new way of doing everything". The key principles that I have uncovered from this book are the following:
(1) Work effectively, not efficiently (the latter does not imply that you are working on THE most important things)
(2) Learn to say no to things (personal, work, etc) and take greater control of your life
(3) Actively funnel to-do's, requests, etc through an internal "essential" test to decide whether something is truely important and should be done at all

One caveat, similar to many books in this genre. If you are a low-ranking associate at your job, you will find it difficult to implement a fair number of these strategies Day 1 (e.g. "how the hell am I supposed to do this while working at a [law firm / bank / advertising agency / etc]). That being said, the principles are still worth reading and keeping with you, because as you grow more senior in your role (even if you're just managing one person initially), they will become incrementally more valuable

title: Digital Babylon and Faithful Christians
text:
We live in a digital world, and one in which it seems Christians are swimming against the tide. Those who are coming to Christ in their youth within the digital age are often finding themselves lost in the sea. While following Jesus hasn't changed since Paul, it does look different from generation to generation. In an age of instant connection, limitless information, and constant entertainment, all filled with a value system that opposes God, "Faith for Exiles" asks the question of how we can create lasting disciples within this digital Babylon. In the digital age, "the goal of discipleship is to develop Jesus followers who are resiliently faithful in the face of cultural coercion and who live a vibrant life in the Spirit." David Kinnaman, president of @barnagroup, and @mattmatlock present 5 practices for Christians in the digital age.
•
1. Intimacy with Jesus to form resilient identity. Does Jesus bring you joy? Is worship a lifestyle? Is Scripture relevant to your life? Is your relationship with Jesus personal and intimate?
2. Develop muscles of cultural discernment. Is the Bible teaching at your church relevant to your life? Do you receive wisdom on how to live in a secular age? Is your worldview Christian?
3. Form meaningful, intergenerational friendships. Do you feel like you belong at church? IS someone encouraging you spiritually? Do you have personal close friends at church?
4.Train for vocational discipleship. Do you use your unique talents to honor God? Do you recognize God's unique calling on your life? Do you serve others in your church?
5. Engage in countercultural mission. Do you desire for others to see Jesus reflected in your life? Do you feel a responsibility to tell others about Jesus? Does the mission of the Church excite you?
•
This book seeks to create resilient individuals who cling to the truths of who they are in Christ, their purpose on earth, and the ways we serve and evangelize others. This book is packed front to back with research, statistics, diagrams, and charts. But the true fruit of the book comes in the theological insight and assessment of the next gen. The entire book is also gorgeously designed thanks to @chazrusso. **book graciously provided by Baker Books for an honest review

title: A Must-Have
text:
The authors offer truly groundbreaking insights and methods in this book, and I will cite a few, but the depth and breadth of their work is far too vast to encapsulate here. They note the plethora of unhelpful, anecdotal advice that often passes for wisdom in similar books, and instead provide scientifically documented, step-by-step methods for defining and achieving goals. They provide compelling examples of how these techniques have been implemented. The most fascinating story, in my opinion, involved the eradication of the guinea worm, an endemic parasite that can grow up to three feet long and emerges through the skin causing tremendous pain. The authors cited techniques employed by Carter Foundation workers to teach villagers how to filter their water and prevent reinfestation of water sources by infected persons. Carter Foundation workers sought positive deviants (villages who had learned their own ways of avoiding guinea worm infestation) to teach other villages what to do.

I noted many techniques that I myself had discovered by trial and error, such as perfect practice, which involves working on improving specific elements of a task; they cite basketball freethrowing, where perfect practice includes improving followthrough, elbow position, etc., as opposed to results oriented practice that can reinforce poor technique, e.g. shoot until I get 20 baskets. As a Chemistry teacher, I inherently implemented many of these techniques. This book provided me with more insight and concrete guidance than most of the teaching and education books I was provided in my teacher training.

This is one of the most enlightening books I have ever read on human behavior. Having borrowed this book from the library, I now plan to purchase it (the actual ink and paper version), because I know I will refer to it again and again.

Narrated by Eric Conger with dignity and clarity.

title: A little disappointed

Michael Fallon's Dodgerland is an attempt to put the Dodger teams of 1977 and 1978 into the author's view of their cultural context.

When he writes about the way that new manager Tommy Lasorda prepared the team for the challenges of the '77 season, or the contentious Dodger clubhouse, he provides valuable insights. As a fan, these were some of my favorite Dodger teams of all time and maybe the best that I have ever seen play, even though they didn't win the World Series until 1981, so I found the "inside game" stuff interesting.

I could do with the liberal politics that the author espoused in the guise of a baseball book - as a lifelong Californian, I don't hold the author's favorable view of mayor Tom Bradley.

The author also makes the book a little autobiographical, choosing to write about his dad's hardware store and the author's role in the business. He also writes about a number of seemingly disjointed things, like skateboarding, author Tom Wolfe and other odds and ends.

He also makes some unforced errors - factual mistakes about the baseball stuff.

Overall interesting but not nearly as good as it could be.

Perhaps I'm spoiled by churning through Patrick O'Brian's Aubrey/Maturin series and C.S. Forester's Hornblower series over the last three years, but I really had a hard time with this first Bolitho book. The writing was choppy, the characters didn't feel real, the plotting was unbelievable, and it all felt oriented towards children. Young teens, perhaps. It felt like the Hardy Boys.

The O'Brian books are fine literature - not particularly accessible, but extremely rewarding. The Forester books nail down the action/adventure genre - not as dense as O'Brian, but well-written, compelling, and fast-moving. This Bolitho book seemed to aspire to that same action/adventure niche but came up dramatically short. I'm not exactly a purist - unpretentious action/adventure books from the 1940s-1970s are a favorite of mine. But it just wasn't good.

Two stars because I didn't stop reading, I'm probably just spoiled by O'Brian and Forester, and because my momentum from their series means I'll probably try the next book just to see if it's better. Maybe once Midshipman Bolitho grows up the quality of the writing will too.

text: I have been on the hunt for a portable air compressor that can keep up with my weekend hobby of inflating paddleboards, inflatable kayaks, and even the occasional car tire in a pinch. I was able to fully inflate a large stand-up paddleboard in under three minutes, which is incredibly fast compared to my old manual foot pump that took twenty minutes and made me sweat. The motor sounds robust, not like those cheap plastic toys that whine and die after a few uses. It feels sturdy in the hand, and the build quality seems durable enough to handle being tossed in a backpack or truck bed without falling apart. The price point is also very competitive when you compare it to major brand names that charge twice as much for similar specifications. It delivers exactly what it promises without any hidden fees or complicated setups right out of the box. However, I do have to mention the power switch. It feels a bit flimsy compared to the rest of the unit. It lacks a satisfying click and seems like it could break if you are not careful when flipping it on and off. I have learned to treat it gently, but for the average user who might just want a quick on and off, it might feel too fragile. Despite this questionable switch design, the performance is so solid that I can easily overlook it. For anyone needing a reliable, fast, and affordable pump for sports gear, this is a fantastic choice that earns its five stars.

title: Even withstands washing machines
text:
I’ll be honest: I bought this desk mat primarily because it was large enough to cover my whole workspace and had a clean, professional look. What I did not expect was that it would survive a full cycle in my washing machine wash – including the spin dry – without any warping, fading, or peeling of the edges. I know that sounds crazy, but here is the story.

I was moving my office to a new room and, in the chaos, my mat ended up in a pile of the laundry pile. My spouse grabbed it thinking it was a load of towels without checking. When I found it later, my heart sank. To my absolute shock, it came out looking brand new. No curling, no frayed stitching, no color bleed. The rubber base stayed perfectly flat, and the fabric top wasn’t pilled or fuzzy. That incident turned me into a believer.

Now I actually wash it on purpose every month. The dirt, coffee drips, and pen marks that used to haunt me are gone with a simple cold wash and low-heat dry. It comes out of the dryer smelling fresh and lies flat on my desk within minutes. The non-slip backing still grips my desk like the first day I unrolled it. The size is generous – fits my keyboard mouse, plus a notebook, with room to spare. The only minor note is that if you overload your washing machine with heavy items, the mat might get folded over during the cycle; I just place it alone on delicate, and it works perfectly.

For anyone who eats at their desk, has kids, or just hates the thought of buying a new mat every six months – this thing is a lifesaver. It’s sturdy, professional-looking, and unkillable. Five stars, no hesitation.

The last time I built a PC was back in 2014, so I'm not up-to-date on todays tech. I did some research and came across these newer M.2 SSD's. I'm not new to SSD's. My last PC actually has a Samsung 840 PRO. Those were lightning fast in their day and still are.

When it comes to daily tasks for me, it's mostly web browsing and streaming with light gaming mixed in a few times a week. I play Overwatch, CS:GO, Path of Exile, Rust, Diablo 3: RoS, GTA V, and a few others. Load times are definitely quicker with an SSD compared to a traditional HDD. I don't do heavy data transfers, so I don't reach the true potential of this drive, but I wanted to invest in the longevity and dependability with Samsung. Just be careful when looking at M.2 SSD's. title: The plight of the Third World
text:
Accomplished master of the police procedural Henning Mankell strays from this genre in his latest novel, "Kennedy's Brain". In his novel, Mankell in the guise of a mystery, has penned what is in reality a social commentary. Mankell who resides at least partially in Mozambique, takes aim at the plight of the African underprivileged particularly relating to the AIDS epidemic and it's exploitation by the pharmaceutical companies.

Swedish archaeologist Louise Cantor whose specialty is ancient Greek artifracts is leading an expedition in Greece sponsored by Uppsala university. She happily anticipates taking a break to return to Stockholm and visit her son Henrik. Much to her shock and dismay she arrives at his flat, unable to raise him on the phone, to find him lying dead in bed. She is stunned to learn that an autopsy confirms that he overdosed on barbiturates.

Unable to believe that Henrik would take his own life she commences her own investigation. She travels across the world to a remote area of Australia to recruit her estranged husband Aron and inform him of their son's death. Together they go through his papers that direct them to an apartment their son kept in Barcelona. Hacking into his computer they discover that he was HIV positive and that he had business that took him to Mozambique.

Louise Cantor proceeds to Africa after the mysterious disappearance of her ex husband. While there she is confronted by danger and the horrors of a village designed to care for AIDS victims where Henrik had worked. She discovers that there is quite a bit more going on there than administering to the sick.

Mankell paints a graphic picture of the misery endured by the suffering in Africa while being critical of those who opportunistically use them for financial gain. The plot of "Kennedy's Brain", metaphor for an inexplicable and secretive mystery is very much similar to Le Carre's "The Constant Gardener".

I bought 4 of these for my face painting business. We were going to be set up at a July 4th event, out in the middle of a field (no electricity), and I wasn't sure if we'd keep working after dark. The fans were nice, but they had to be set up right next to us on the table, set on high, to even notice anything. But, it was a VERY hot day and evening, 90-100. They were pretty quiet, just a hum.

I was torn, but didn't give it 5 stars because they are a little twitchy. Being made of lightweight plastic, you have to be careful of the switches, the slightest bump turns things on and off. Once set in place, they were fine. Also, I think parts could break easily with rough handling. But, for the price, what can you expect?

title: Grinds well, but fragile
text:
When it's working, it grinds very well and consistently. But it's fragile and I experienced the "lock-up" issue after the first week or so. It is stressful to clean the grinder because I'm always afraid I'll lock it up when trying to reinsert the bean holder.

I gave it four stars because it's an excellent grinder. The fifth star would've been applied if it wasn't so fragile.

Tips to avoid the lock-up issue:

1) Make sure the clear, rubber part of the burr grinder is facing up before you insert the bean holder.
2) Make sure to align the dot on the bean holder as described in the manual.
3) Be sure the bean holder is all the way seated before turning it to engage.
4) Turn it slowly to make sure it's seated and engaging correctly.

Pros:
- Grinds very well and very consistently.
- Good value for the quality of grind.

Cons:
- Very fragile - will lock up occasionally even if you're very careful.
- Lock-up is permanent and requires a replacement grinder.
- Difficult to clean thoroughly - tedious.

title: Poor Product
text:
I am absolutely devastated by this purchase. I spent nearly three hundred dollars on what was marketed as a premium, high-fidelity wireless speaker system, expecting a solid build and crisp sound quality. Instead, I received a lightweight, plasticky disaster that feels like it would break if you looked at it too hard. The packaging was already damaged when it arrived, suggesting it had been thrown around by multiple handlers before even reaching my doorstep, but I was naive enough to think it might still work. It did not work.

From the moment I took it out of the box, everything was wrong. The charging port was loose, wiggling inside the casing with the slightest touch, making it impossible to charge without finding a very specific, awkward angle. The Bluetooth connection was unstable from day one. It would connect for about thirty seconds before dropping the signal entirely, forcing me to reset the device and start the pairing process all over again. This happened multiple times a day, every day, for the two weeks I attempted to use it.

The sound quality is another major letdown. For the price point, I expected clear highs and deep bass. What I got was a muddy, tinny mess that distorted the moment you turned the volume above fifty percent. There is zero bass response, making music sound flat and lifeless, while the highs are painfully shrill after just an hour of listening. It is fatiguing to use.

I contacted customer support three times. Each time, I was given a generic response telling me to restart the device or update the firmware, neither of which resolved the fundamental hardware defects. There is no warranty information included in the box, no manual, and no clear way to initiate a return. I feel like I have thrown my money into a black hole. Do not buy this product. It is a cheaply made, defective waste of resources that I deeply regret owning. If you value your time and your money, save yourself the headache and look elsewhere.

title: Works with Eufy G30 Verge
text: This is the same tape that is included with the Eufy G30 Verge. We purchased a total of 4 rolls of this product to mark off areas in our home. It works when it is exposed on the floor and also when it is under the very edge of thin carpets. We adhered to both the floor and carpet edge, and have not had any issues with lifting. Two important things we have learned: first, all this device needs to sneak through a spot is 4 to 6 inches of gap in the tape. When planning this layout, and you should plan it before you cut it, make sure you are not leaving any gaps in the tape. Secondly, if you are concerned about damaging your floor with the 3M double-sided tape that is enclosed, we used 3M command strips with a 3-pound weight classification. We were able to purchase a package of these separate of command hooks they are typically used with. Since we have hardwood floors, we thought this was a worthy investment. All tape was mounted with the light side facing upward. The device has not crossed any of the magnetic barriers including thresholds. I should add that we do not have any metal threshold in our home, it is all wood, tile, carpet, and vinyl. The tape is an investment that can be costly but it is absolutely worth it. We returned a similar product because it did not work but this barrier tape has performed 100%. It also has a lower profile then other barrier tape we tried so it lays nice and flat under area rugs and in high traffic areas. Highly recommend.

Her description of the lives of these brave young women opened my eyes wide. I have read many books on China and have visited the country several times, and this is the first I have read about a population that is so important to the economic development of the country and also the U.S. It's a great read. By interweaving her own family history Ms. Chang talked about the idea of going out. Her grand father went out. Her father went out. And in her own way, by going to China, she went out, just like the factory girls. For anyone interested in China, this book is a must read.

I also want to say that Ms. Chang's story is a better read than her husband's, probably because she is herself Chinese and female, and thus can get closer to her subjects. She writes in a journalistic style, so I think her husband is still a slightly better writer.

title: I have noticed increased activity in out dog since I ...

I have noticed increased activity in our dog since I started him on these chews about three weeks ago. My Labrador, Max, is eight years old and had really started to slow down. He would sleep most of the day, seemed stiff getting up from his bed, and had zero interest in fetch, which used to be his absolute favorite thing. Then a friend recommended these supplements, and I figured it was worth a shot.

The difference was not immediate, but after about ten days I saw him perk up during our morning walk. He started pulling on the leash again, wanting to sniff every bush. By the second week, he was bringing me his slobbery tennis ball and dropping it at my feet, something he hadn’t done in over a year. Now he plays fetch twice a day and even does this little happy dance when I grab the leash for a walk. The stiffness in his hind legs is much less noticeable, and he jumps onto the couch without that labored groan he used to make.

I also appreciate that these chews have a soft texture, so even a picky older dog like mine takes them without hesitation. They smell like peanut butter, not medicine, and the ingredients list includes glucosamine and turmeric, which I know are good for joint health. I was worried about potential side effects, but he has had no digestive issues whatsoever.

Overall, this product has given my senior dog a new lease on life. He is moving better, playing more, and seems genuinely happier. For the price, the results have been fantastic. I will definitely be buying more and have already recommended them to my neighbor with a similar issue. Highly recommend for any dog that seems to be slowing down with age.

title: Too many subplots.
text:
There are at least half-a-dozen subplots in this book, any of which could have (and should have) been a book unto itself. As it is, Pandora's Star is a disjointed narrative, flipping from one plot to another; not randomly, but annoyingly. At least two of the subplots are tedious enough that I ultimately just started skimming over those sections or skipping them entirely. Yeah, the author had a big story he wanted to tell, and it is an interesting story, but he didn't pull it off. Oh, and to end the book so bluntly just to make us have to buy his next one is just crass commercialism on his part.

That's not to say that there aren't great elements in this massive story. But they are few and too far between to ultimately provide a satisfying experience. My advice, regrettably, is not to buy this book. And even if you can borrow it for free, don't bother reading it. There are far better "space opera" authors out there.

title: Easy and Bright
text:
I have been searching for the perfect running companion for months, and I finally found it with the Easy and Bright headlamp. As an early morning jogger, visibility is my top priority, and this product delivers exactly what it promises. The setup was incredibly intuitive, taking less than five minutes from opening the box to being ready for the trail. The instructions were clear, and the batteries included meant I didn’t have to run to the store immediately after purchase.

The brightness is phenomenal. I was skeptical at first because the lumens number seemed too high for such a compact device, but it genuinely lights up the path ahead. The beam is focused enough to see obstacles like roots and rocks but wide enough to maintain peripheral awareness. This balance is crucial for trail running safety. The red light mode is a nice bonus for preserving night vision and not blinding other runners or hikers.

Comfort is another major selling point. It sits securely on my head without any slipping, even during intense intervals or when I am sweating heavily. The adjustable strap is soft and does not cause irritation after wearing it for over an hour. I was also impressed by the battery life. I used it on the highest setting for my five-mile morning runs and only had to recharge it once every two weeks. That efficiency is remarkable.

Water resistance has held up well against light rain and morning dew, giving me peace of mind when the weather turns unpredictable. For the price point, the build quality feels premium and durable. It has survived a few accidental drops on rocky terrain without any dents or loss of function. If you are looking for a reliable, bright, and comfortable lighting solution for your outdoor adventures, do not hesitate. This is the best investment I have made for my active lifestyle this year. Highly recommended for runners, hikers, and campers alike.

title: Straightforward in an unspectacular way
text:
Since Mark Waid introduced a group of lab assistants to work under Bruce Banner, I’ve harped on the fact that they’ve had very little in the way of character development. The Indestructible Hulk #16 finally addresses that issue by delving into the past of Mr. Jessup, largely because, as this issue informs us, he’s going to die within a week. Spending a full issue to build up a character just so readers will feel some sort of impact when he dies seems a little cheap to me, but I still think this marks progress, as one of the things this book has been lacking is a good supporting cast.

The art here is done by Mahmud Asrar, who does a pretty good job. Nothing here really blows me away, but it’s a welcome change to have an entire issue follow one art style after the last arc cycled through multiple artists on a page-by-page basis.

As a whole, this issue does what it needs to do in a straightforward if unspectacular way. We finally get some background on some of Banner’s supporting cast, we get the suspense of knowing that said character is going to die, and we get some Hulk smashing action. This is an above-average issue that will hopefully lead into bigger things to come when the story gets rolling.

title: Nice Cabinet and Board, BAD Darts
text:
I bought this dart cabinet and board set a few weeks ago because I wanted a neat, all-in-one option for occasional games in the garage. First impressions were positive: the cabinet itself looks good, is solidly built, and the magnetic closures keep it tidy when not in use. The finish is nice and it mounted easily to the wall — overall it gives a more polished look than a cheap foam board hung with screws.

Unfortunately, the darts and the board are where this product falls apart. The board surface is a cheap sisal substitute that wears unevenly and already shows fraying around the triple 20 after only a handful of sessions. More noticeably, the included darts feel very low quality. The shafts are flimsy plastic that bent or loosened almost every game, and the threads that attach to the flights stripped easily. I tried tightening them and replacing flights, but they didn’t hold alignment and the darts wobbled a lot in flight, which made accurate throws nearly impossible.

The scoring ring on the board is thin metal and seems okay for stopping bounce-outs, but the combination of soft board material and poor darts resulted in a higher-than-expected rate of bounced or dropped darts — not fun when you’re keeping score. I would have been happier if the set included at least mid-range darts or allowed for easy upgrades; swapping in better darts helps, but doesn’t solve the fact that the board itself degrades quickly.

If you want a sharp-looking cabinet and a basic board for casual display and very light play, this will do the job. If you’re buying it to play regularly or expect decent dart performance out of the box, you’ll be disappointed and likely need to buy replacement darts (and possibly a better board) soon after. Hence the middle-of-the-road rating.

The inner cushion is plush enough for him to sink into but firm enough to provide proper support—he’s a senior dog with mild hip stiffness, and I’ve noticed he gets up much more easily in the mornings since we switched.

What really sold me is the washability. The first time he had an accident. I unzipped the cover, tossed it in the wash on cold, and it came out looking like new. No shrinking, no pilling, or fading. The waterproof inner liner did its job perfectly the mattress pad underneath stayed completely dry. That alone makes it worth the price.

The size is generous too. Milo is about 75 pounds and he has plenty of room to sprawl out or curl into a tight ball. The raised edges are high enough to rest his head on, which he loves. No funky chemical smell out of the box either just a faint fabric scent that disappeared after a day.

I honestly wasn’t expecting to love this bed as much as my dog does. He spends hours on it every day, and even our cat has claimed a corner. If you’re tired replacing pet beds every season, give this one a shot. It’s sturdy, comfortable, and easy to clean exactly what we needed.

text:
Been buying these glasses for years. They are cheap, but honestly, they do the job for me. I have tried many brands over the last five years, ranging from the expensive designer stuff at the mall to various online alternatives, but I always seem to come back to these. The price point is unbeatable, especially when you consider that I go through a pair roughly every two years due to normal wear and tear. The frames are lightweight, which is a huge plus because I often forget I am wearing them. They do not slip down my nose even during long days at work, which is a common issue with other budget options I have tested.

However, they are not perfect. The hinges feel a bit flimsy, and you have to handle them with a bit more care than higher-end brands. I accidentally sat on one last winter, and while it survived, the arm was slightly bent. A gentle tweak fixed it, but it did remind me that these are not built for rough treatment. The lenses are clear enough for reading and basic tasks, but if you need high-precision optical clarity for driving at night or detailed computer work, you might want to invest in something with better coating quality. That said, for casual use, extra pairs for around the house, or as a backup when I travel, they are fantastic. The fit is standard and accommodates most face shapes without pinching. I appreciate that they come in multiple colors, so I can match them to my daily outfits. For the money, you simply cannot beat the value. They are disposable in a sense, but for most people, that is a feature, not a bug. I will continue to buy them because replacement is inexpensive, and they get the job done without breaking the bank. Just be gentle with them, and they will last you a good while. Five stars would be nice, but the build quality holds them back slightly from true premium status. Still, a solid choice for budget-conscious shoppers.

I picked this book up largely based on the glowing descriptions in the catalog, hoping for a deep dive into the subject matter. Unfortunately, my experience with it was a mix of high hopes and eventual disappointment. The initial chapters are engaging enough, and the author has a pleasant writing style that makes the early pages flow smoothly. It feels like a genuine attempt to explore complex ideas in an accessible way, which I appreciate. However, as the book progresses, the depth fades significantly.

I found myself skimming through several chapters because the arguments felt repetitive and lacked the substantive evidence promised in the introduction. It is frustrating to invest time in a narrative that seems interested more in filling space than providing insight. For anyone looking for a comprehensive overview or a rigorous analysis, this title falls short. It stays surface-level for too long, missing the opportunity to offer a truly transformative perspective on the topic.

That said, it is not entirely without merit. If you are a casual reader who just wants something light to pass the time during a weekend, this might suffice. The layout is clean, and the font size is comfortable for long reading sessions. But if you are a serious student or enthusiast of the genre, you will likely feel let down by the lack of original thought and the reliance on clichéd conclusions. I expected more from the publisher given the hype surrounding the release. I would hesitate to recommend this to anyone seeking genuine intellectual stimulation. It feels like a cash-grab rather than a meaningful contribution to the field. There are better resources available for those who want to truly understand the nuances of this subject. title: Cute Counting Book With Wonderful Illustrations
text: The best thing about "10 Turkeys in the Road" is indeed the turkeys, along with the rest of the illustrated material.  The artwork is superb - colorful, whimsical, and downright funny.  In this counting primer, a farmer's path becomes blocked by 10 turkeys.  The frustrated farmer tries everything to move the turkeys out of his way, but can manage to clear only one turkey at a time from his path.  Preschooler's will undoubtedly love the winsome pictures, and engaging them in the turkey counting shouldn't be difficult.  If there is any criticism to be made, however, it would be the slightly less engaging poetic narrative.  Another well-known counting book, "Five Little Monkeys Jumping on the Bed," offers a significantly more memorable poetic experience by way of it's almost sing-song verse: "Five little monkeys jumping on the bed, one fell off and bumped his head; mama called the doctor and the doctor said, 'No more monkeys jumping on the bed!'"  I've read that one with both of my kids over the years, and the catchy rhythm & rhyme of its language make it a classic.  This book doesn't quite match that one with it's poetry, but the superb illustrations make it worthwhile.  A fine choice for little ones working on their counting skills.

title: A Pop Up Book to Explore with Several Senses
text:
In our family, we have loved pop-up books for several generations, including examples from more than a century ago that are beloved volumes on our bookshelf to this day. While this third book has zero holiday content, we immediately recognized ABC Pop-Up as a marvelous choice for holiday gift-giving.

This pop-up book brilliantly invites adults and children to explore several senses: sound, vision and even tactile experiences of exploring the pop up shapes!

My favorite sequence is a pop-up bed that stands up in front of us, as we read the book, without any immediate clue as to the letters involved. Then, if we closely examine the bed, we discover the pillow has an embossed P in one corner and the quilt has an embossed Q. Little fingers can touch the letters and actually feel the raised shapes.

Then, the sequence continues with a stately tree that leaps up with an attached tire swing and, as we look over the entire page, we discover that we can glimpse the tree’s gnarled roots at the bottom of the page. What letters are we discovering? The tire swing actually dangles from a string and, if our eyes are quick, we can see the S for swing. But what about R? Little fingers can detect an embossed R in the tree’s roots. And then what’s the T? Well, you can guess.

In our family collection, we now own more than 100 pop up books and, while this book is, indeed, little in its physical scale, it is truly a work of genius!

Intertape is 7.2 mil thick, but my old tape - Reel brand - is 7.4. Doesn't seem like much, but you can tell the difference. I question the Intertape 45 lb tensile strength claim. Reel tape says it's strength is only 32 lb, but it is tougher tape. It takes intentional effort to tear Reel tape, but Intertape tears very readily. Could be handy - if that's what you're after. Intertape definitely has less adhesive, but some people might find this a plus. You can reposition it - if you do it right away. Reel tape is very sticky and once it is down, it is down - you know you have a good, solid bond immediately.

title: Great Book!
text:
I picked up "Great Book!" based on the title alone — yes, I was that curious. And honestly, for the most part, it lives up to its name. The writing style is engaging and conversational, which made it easy to get through in just a few sittings. The author covers some fascinating ideas, blending personal anecdotes with solid research in a way that never feels dry. I found myself highlighting several passages and even dog-earing a few pages to revisit later.

What keeps it from a full five stars for me is the pacing in the middle section. Around chapters four through six, the narrative loses a bit of steam. The concepts start to feel repetitive, and I wished the author had either tightened that part or introduced a fresh angle sooner. It picks back up nicely in the final chapters, but that middle lull took some effort to push through.

Also, a minor but noticeable issue: the paperback edition I received had a few smudged print lines in one chapter. Nothing unreadable, but slightly disappointing for a new book.

Overall, "Great Book!" is a solid, thought-provoking read that I’d recommend to anyone interested in the subject. Just be prepared for a brief slowdown before the strong finish. Worth the money, but not quite a flawless gem.

title: Does not stay attached to clothing
text: I purchased this set of adhesive hooks with high hopes for organizing my home office, specifically to hang my coffee mug organizer and some lightweight tools above my desk. The concept seemed perfect for avoiding holes in the wall and keeping my workspace clutter-free without needing to drill or use unsightly command strips that often leave marks. The packaging looked professional, and the instructions were clear, promising a bond that lasts for months rather than days. Unfortunately, the reality of using this product was a stark disappointment that I never expected given the positive reviews I had read prior to buying. On the first day of installation, I carefully cleaned the surface of the wall with the provided alcohol wipe, pressed the hook firmly for the recommended thirty seconds, and waited the full hour before hanging anything. I hung a small, lightweight basket filled with pens and paperclips. Within less than four hours, I heard a distinct thud from the corner of my eye. Rushing over, I found the basket on the floor, shards of plastic scattered everywhere, and the adhesive hook lying limp and useless against the baseboard. It had not just failed to hold the item; it had completely detached itself from the wall, leaving no residue but a significant mess. I tried again with a different hook and a slightly heavier bag of tissues. This time, it lasted only six hours before falling again. I understand that surfaces can vary, but claiming a strong bond for months is misleading when the product cannot even survive a standard workday. For the price, I expected basic reliability, not constant cleaning up of dropped items. The adhesive seems weak and inconsistent, with no guarantee that it will stick properly regardless of how well you follow the instructions. If you are looking for a temporary solution for something that absolutely must not fall, this might work for ten minutes, but for any practical, long-term office organization, it is a waste of money. Do not trust the initial stickiness; it is not reliable. I have since switched to traditional command strips, which are more expensive but actually stay on the wall as advertised. Save your time and frustration, and avoid this product entirely.

title: Squeakiest chair ever
text:
I wanted to like this chair — I bought it for camping and tailgating because the photos made it look sturdy, compact, and comfortable. In practice it’s a mixed bag, and I’m giving it two stars because of one major issue that ruins most of the experience: it is the squeakiest chair I have ever owned.

Right out of the box the frame seemed solid and the fabric felt ok for the price. Setup was straightforward and the chair folded down to a nice compact carry size. It is reasonably light and the included carry bag is handy, which is why I still use it occasionally despite the problem.

But when you sit down and shift even slightly, the metal frame lets out a loud, high-pitched squeak. Moving from standing to seated is like a chorus of tiny brakes. At a quiet campsite or during a game, the noise is embarrassing and constant. I tried tightening all the screws, applying lubricant to the joints, and even layering some cloth at the contact points — nothing fully fixed it. The squeak is present whether the chair is placed on grass, gravel, or concrete.

Comfort-wise, the seat is average for a folding chair. The back offers minimal support and after a couple hours you start to feel it. The cup holder is useful but flimsy. Weight capacity seems fine for my needs, and the fabric has held up after a few uses.

If you only need an inexpensive portable chair and can tolerate (or fix) the noise, it serves a purpose. But if you want quiet, comfortable seating for longer outdoor events, look elsewhere. I’m disappointed because the price and portability were appealing, but the constant squeaking makes it more trouble than it’s worth.

title: Fail
text:
I bought the "Fail" pet bed thinking the name was just a quirky marketing gimmick. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a pretty accurate description. The bed looked great in the photos, but in reality the foam padding is far thinner than advertised. My 25-pound terrier sinks right through to the floor within minutes. I followed the care instructions exactly, but after two machine washes the outer cover started pilling and the zipper broke. For a product marketed as a premium pet supply, the build quality is disappointing.

On the positive side, the fabric is soft and my dog does seem to enjoy curling up on it when I fluff the filling back into shape. The non-skid bottom works reasonably well on hardwood floors. However, the bed does not hold its form; it looks lumpy and sad after a week of use. At this price point, I expected something that would last longer. I've had cheaper beds from other brands that held up for years.

Maybe this would work for a very small, lightweight cat or a toy breed that doesn't move around much. For any dog that actually sleeps hard, it's not worth the money. I'll be replacing it within a few months. The name "Fail" is unfortunately fitting.

Build quality feels solid; the trigger is comfortable for extended use and there’s no leaking even after repeated use. The reservoir holds a generous amount of solution, so I don’t have to refill constantly. Cleaning the nozzle and parts is simple, and everything rinses out without fuss.

Overall, Stream OR Spray delivers on its promises. It’s efficient, durable, and genuinely makes cleaning faster and easier. Highly recommend for anyone wanting a reliable, multipurpose cleaning tool.

title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I was tired of sitting all day and decided to make the switch to a standing desk converter. This one seemed like a good middle ground—not too expensive, decent reviews, and a size that would fit my current desk. For the first week, I was all right, and now I'm not sure it was the best choice. Let me start with what I think so far.

Assembly was straightforward enough. The instructions were clear, and parts all came, but I needed a screwdriver that wasn't included, so keep that in mind. It took me about 45 minutes to get it together by myself. The unit itself the unit looks sturdy enough with its metal frame and a black laminate top. The gas spring for lifting the work surface works smoothly and you can stop at any height between sitting and standing. That part is great, and I do enjoy being able to stand for a couple of hours during the day.

Now for the "beware" part. The biggest issue is stability. When the desk is at standing height, there is noticeable wobble, especially if I type with any force. I have a dual monitor setup, and the monitors shake slightly when I'm typing quickly. I've tightened everything twice, but the wobble persists. It's not dangerous, but it's distracting. At sitting height, it's fine. I also the keyboard tray that attaches underneath is too close to my knees. My legs hit the tray if I sit cross-legged or even normally sometimes. I had to adjust my chair to a awkward sitting position. The tray itself is small and doesn't hold a full-sized keyboard and mouse comfortably. I use a tenkeyless keyboard, and it fits barely, but no room for a mousepad. I end up using the main surface for the mouse, which reduces the available workspace for papers.

Another thing: the desktop surface is about 36 inches wide, but the base takes up about 24 inches of that, so the usable space is actually less than a typical desk. My 27-inch monitors just barely fit side by side, and there's no room for a notebook or phone stand.

Overall, I've had this for three months now. It does what it's supposed to—lets me stand while working—but the wobble and limited space are frustrating. For the price, I think there are better options out there. I'll keep it for now, but I'm already looking for a replacement that is more stable and has a better keyboard tray. If you're on a heavy typer or need more than one large monitor, look elsewhere. Three stars. It works, but beware of the compromises.

I was delighted to find this author, known for his travel narratives and splendid prose, an Englishman born in 1908 and only dying recently at age 95 in Saffron Walden, Essex, where he had lived modestly and politely, shyly even. Luigi Barzini described reading his prose as "like eating cherries" and Graham Greene - with whom Lewis shared many similarities in adventures, courage and quiet, commanding prose - had "no hesitation in calling him one of the best writers, not of any particular decade, but of our century".

In this work - part of a multiple volume autobiography, there was only one decision Lewis made that damaged his intellect in this readers view - he agreed to an investigative reporting trip to Peru accompanied by Lord Snowden as his photographer, traveling "incognito". Lewis seemed genuinely surprised that was far from a successful trip, or experience, and as for the `incognito' - well at least it got the author free upgrades to First Class flights and entertainment by British Ambassadors and Peruvian society!

The author had a fascinating and often wildly exciting life, serving in the British Forces in Italy during WWII followed by a career in journalism reporting on Vietnam, Burma, Indo China and producing a splendid series of books for Jonathan Cape - who used to entertain his authors with dinners of burnt Irish Stew - on the mafia in Sicily, and the threatened indigenous peoples of Latin America.

Writing with a compassion and light wit Lewis crafted over thirty books and one of his five children, his second son Gareth, has also published a book called 'Deceit'.

title: Should be called a ‘wet bag’
text:
I am absolutely disgusted with this purchase and feel completely misled by the product description. I bought this item expecting a high-quality, waterproof container for my sports gear, specifically for carrying sweaty towels and damp clothing after intense workouts. Instead, what arrived in the mail is a pathetic excuse for a bag that does exactly what it should not: it leaks. Calling this a proper storage solution is a joke; it should honestly be classified as a "wet bag" in the worst possible sense of the term, meaning it is useless for its primary intended purpose.

The material feels incredibly cheap and flimsy from the moment you take it out of the package. It lacks any structural integrity, making it difficult to stand up on its own, which is a basic requirement for a gym bag. More importantly, the stitching along the seams is incredibly poor. I only used it once, for about thirty minutes while carrying a slightly damp towel and a change of clothes, and by the time I reached my car, water had seeped through the bottom and wet the entire contents of my other bags. This is not just a minor flaw; it is a complete design failure.

Furthermore, the zipper is a nightmare. It constantly gets stuck, requiring a level of patience and force that I never expected to exert on a simple accessory. Halfway through my walk home, the zipper slid down on its own, spilling wet laundry all over the pavement. This is humiliating and inconvenient. I tried to contact the seller to request a refund, citing the obvious defects, but they have been completely unresponsive. It is frustrating to spend money on a product that feels like it was thrown together in a factory with no quality control whatsoever.

Do not waste your hard-earned money on this item. There are countless better alternatives available at the same price point that actually offer true water resistance and durability. I am left with a soggy mess and a bag that is now too damaged to use for even dry storage. If you value your time and your belongings, steer clear of this product. It is not worth the hassle, the disappointment, or the additional cost of cleaning up the mess it inevitably creates. I am giving this one star because it is the minimum allowed, and honestly, if I could give zero stars, I would. The product is fundamentally broken and fails to meet the most basic expectations of a functional sports accessory.

title: Yuck.
text:
I was skeptical when I first opened the package. The name says it all, and the smell that hit me when I dropped the first tablet into my Nalgene bottle confirmed it. Yuck is not a product you buy because you enjoy it. You buy it because it works.

I spent ten days backpacking in the Sierra Nevada this fall, and every water source I came across was treated with these tablets. The taste is genuinely unpleasant, like a chemical off-flavor mixed with something metallic and bitter. But here is the truth: I did not get sick. Not once. I crossed streams that looked clear but had livestock grazing upstream, and I filled up from a murky alpine lake on day four. My hiking partner, who used a different brand, spent one night vomiting after that same lake. I was fine.

The instructions are simple: one tablet per liter, wait thirty minutes. I found that letting the water sit for a full hour in cold conditions made a difference. The flavor is stronger if you chug it straight, so I started adding a single electrolyte packet to mask the taste. That helped a lot. Also, if you are using a collapsible bladder, be careful because the chemical can leach into the plastic and linger. I switched to a hard-sided bottle after the first two days.

Is it pleasant? Absolutely not. But when you are miles from the trailhead and your only other option is untreated water, Yuck is your best friend. I will keep a supply in every pack I own. If you prioritize safety over flavor, this is the product to get.

There are hints to cool secrets throughout. Their are some decent action scenes. But by the time I get 100 pages into a book I need to feel some progress!

To still not know if there is an end goal for the main character. To not feel threat from one story cause he is telling ANOTHER story from later in his life, just feel dull.

I know I am in the minority here, but I went into this thinking this was a new Sanderson, Weeks, or Brown. And I think the hype was what ruined it for me.

I went in expecting something grand, epic, and something new to experience. But I found if I spent 2 days away from the book I would forget characters names! Shows I wasnt too enthralled of I'm forgetting stuff.

So I'm done for now. I might pick up the audiobook at some point.

title: Good noise suppression and durability for a fantastic price
text:
I bought these after looking through various first- and third-party solutions for low-noise Mavic Pro props. I'm using them on an original Mavic Pro (not a Platinum) and I absolutely love them for 3 reasons:

1, they make a big difference in terms of the Mavic's sound output. I haven't done formal tests with a decibel meter, but it's obvious that the flights are significantly quieter with these props both indoors and out. I now tend to have some trouble hearing my Mavic once it's up to about 150-200ft even when directly overhead (though obviously quick altitude changes or movements change that). It's made it much less obtrusive than the original props. I haven't tried other brands and therefore can't compare to other manufacturers' low-noise props, but you'll definitely notice a big improvement over the stock blades.

2, their durability seems just as good as the original props'. I read several reviews of other low-noise props that complained that the gold tips were made of a softer, more easily deformed plastic. That isn't the case with these, as it's the same material along the entire length. That may make a slight difference when it comes to aerodynamics, but it means I don't have to worry about them when folding up the props (by the way, they fold up just fine despite their slightly larger size, as long as you're a little careful when unfolding the back legs and don't get the pairs intertwined). The paint scuffs relatively easily, but that's it. I've replaced one set after stupidly crashing into some scrubby branches, but even then there were only a few minor nicks and gouges that I probably could have gotten away still flying with, but at this price it's stupid not to just get another set.

3, obviously the price is amazing. These are half the price of all other manufacturers' props that I could find, and at $8 for a complete set it's really hard to argue with when you get such significant noise reduction. I can't imagine going back to anything else. I'd buy 2 sets just to have some spares.

It’s the kind of book that will hold up through years of bedtime storytelling and still feel fresh.

title: Opened my EYES!
text:
I am writing this review because I feel compelled to share how profoundly this book shifted my perspective, something I haven't experienced in years of reading. As a professional who thought they had seen it all, I approached this title with a healthy dose of skepticism. I expected generic self-help clichés or superficial advice that we all encounter daily. Instead, what I found was a rigorous, beautifully structured argument that challenges the very foundations of how we perceive reality. The author does not just tell you to open your eyes; they provide the logical framework and the psychological tools necessary to actually do so.

The pacing is excellent. There are no filler chapters designed to pad the word count. Every paragraph serves a specific purpose, building upon the last to create a cohesive narrative that feels both personal and universally applicable. I found myself stopping frequently to reflect on my own biases and assumptions, which was an uncomfortable but necessary process. The writing style is accessible without being condescending, striking a rare balance between academic depth and conversational warmth.

What struck me most was the section on cognitive dissonance and how we rationalize our poor decisions. It was a mirror held up to my own life, revealing patterns I had ignored for decades. This is not a quick fix book. It requires active engagement and honest self-reflection. However, the payoff is immense. Since finishing this book, I have noticed a tangible improvement in my decision-making processes and my ability to empathize with people who hold different viewpoints.

If you are looking for entertainment, this might not be it. But if you are seeking genuine growth and a deeper understanding of the human condition, this book is an absolute necessity. It is rare to find a work that feels so urgently important and timeless all at once. I highly recommend it to anyone willing to do the hard work of seeing the truth.

title: A good read
text:
Another good read book.
People who expect too much will be disappointed (like some of the reviewers), but people who just want a good read will like it.

It has drama, good battles, plausible technology and decent characters.
Why would his enemies want to still get rid of him even though he keeps winning? I find that totally plausible and even likely, people are not logical and they can be jerks just for the sake of being a jerk and once they've decided that someone is the enemy, it might require them to admit they were wrong and far too many people can never do that.

I would not say that this is the best book in the series, but I awaited it eagerly and finished it in one sitting without being bored.

It's a good read and possibly trite and predictable (you know the good guys are going to win, but, well, duh. As if you thought that Sauron was going to get the Ring back too).

As for the aliens, I'm gonna have to disagree that they are setting up another series, there is something in this one that seems to explain why the aliens are doing what they are doing. There have been hints in other books (book 3 had a bunch) that make them look not necessarily like bad guys. But that's just my opinion.

I hope Campbell does more books, but I just don't see him setting up another series with a war against the aliens.

title: Its white bot clear. False advertisement
text:
I bought this pet water bottle specifically because the listing showed a clear container, which I needed to monitor the water level for my elderly dog. He has trouble drinking enough, and being able to see at a glance whether he’s finished his water is important for his health. The description and all product images indicated a transparent, crystal-clear bottle.

What arrived was a completely opaque white bottle. I cannot see the water level at all. It’s like a solid white plastic jug. The product is exactly the opposite of what was advertised. This is false advertisement, plain and simple. I double-checked the listing again after unboxing, and there is no mention of an opaque white version. The images still show a clear bottle. The item I received is absolutely not that.

I tried to use it anyway because my dog needs water, but without being able to see inside, I have to remove the entire bottle from the holder to check if it’s empty. That defeats the purpose of a gravity-fed dispenser. It’s also impossible to tell if algae or debris is building up inside. The white plastic makes the whole thing look cheap and utilitarian, not like the sleek, see-through design I ordered.

I contacted the seller, but they have not responded. I will be returning this. If you need a clear bottle to monitor water intake, do not buy this. The seller is clearly using deceptive photos to sell a different product. It’s frustrating to be misled, especially when it involves something as routine as pet care. One star is generous. Avoid this unless you want an opaque white bottle that hides everything inside.

title: Well Worth Your Time
text: This has to be one of the sweetest "morbid" stories ever told - the perfect Morbid Valentine for your beloved. Carl von Cosel was a German x-ray technician living in Florida who fell in love with one of his Tuberculosis patients - a beautiful young woman named Elena. Carl believed that Elena was destined to be his wife and he was overcome with despair when she finally succumbed to her illness. He decided that even death could not keep them apart, and he exhumed his bride and brought her body back to his home, where he cleaned it up and used an elaborate embalming process to preserve her remains. He kept her there with him for 8 years, during which time she naturally began to fall apart a bit, but Carl kept her looking as good as possible by filling in her sunken features with wax. He even inserted a tube in her vaginal canal so they could consummate their love. Yes, it doesn't get much sicker than this! But strangely enough, when Carl was eventually arrested, most women of the time (1920's-30's) thought it was a very romantic story and did not think poorly of the old man at all. Isn't that sweet?

title: Nice large scooter wheel
text:
I bought this large scooter wheel as a replacement for the stock wheel on my adult kick scooter, and after about a month of daily commuting and semi-rough commuting, I have some thoughts.

First, the size is definitely the standout feature. The standout feature. It’s noticeably larger than the original wheel, which came-with-the-scooter wheel, which gives a much smoother roll over cracks, pebbles, and the general uneven pavement of my city commute. The ride quality improved significantly. I feel less of every bump, and it maintains speed better maintains speed once I’m up to cruising pace. The bearing quality seems decent out of the box—spun freely and installed without too much effort. The hub fit my scooter’s axle fit snugly, no wobble.

However, there are some trade-offs that kept me from giving five stars. The larger wheel adds noticeable weight to the front end of the scooter. It’s not heavy, but you feel the momentum difference when carrying the scooter up stairs or navigating tight corners. Also, because the wheel is larger, it changes the geometry slightly. The deck sits a bit higher, which took me a couple of days to get used to. If your scooter is low-slung to begin with, you might feel like you’re perched a little higher up. It’s not a dealbreaker, but something to consider if you’re particular about handling.

Durability is still TBD. After 200+ miles, the rubber tread shows moderate wear, but no chunks missing or flat spots. I’m careful about glass and debris, so I can’t speak for rougher treatment. I didn’t notice any deformation after a few hard bumps.

The price was fair for what you get—better than OEM options from many scooter brands. It’s a good upgrade if you’re looking for a more comfortable, faster roll. The minor downsides are not dealbreakers for me, and I’d buy again if I needed another. If you’re a casual rider who values a plush ride and don’t mind a slight handling change, this is solid. For aggressive riders or those who need tight maneuvering at low speeds, maybe consider a smaller diameter option.

Overall, 4 stars. Good quality, noticeable improvement in ride comfort, but be aware of the size-related changes. Recommended for those wanting to a upgrade their scooter’s rolling experience.

title: As advertised and helps the flat-faced pup eat with less ...
text:
I bought this raised bowl for my pug because our vet recommended we try a shallower, elevated dish to make eating more comfortable for his flat face and to reduce gulping. The product does what it says — the height is just right for him, and he seems to strain his neck less when reaching the kibble. It also appears to help him slow down a little, which is a small win.

That said, there are several things that kept me from giving five stars. The non-slip base works only on clean floors; if there’s any dust or kibble crumbs it slides a bit, and on our hardwood it moved when he pawed around. The plastic feels thinner than I expected and has picked up light scratches from washing after just a few uses. Also, the bowl depth is fine for dry kibble but not ideal for wet food or for adding water — things slosh more easily at this shallow depth.

Overall, it’s a useful, no-frills product that meets the basic need and my dog did adjust to it quickly. If you want a lightweight, affordable elevated bowl for a brachycephalic pup, this is okay, but don’t expect premium materials or a miracle for mess control.

I rarely write reviews, but Filled My Soul moved me enough that I had to share. I bought this book during a time when life felt noisier and more hurried than I wanted, and it turned out to be exactly what I didn’t know I was looking for.

The writing is intimate without being indulgent; the author speaks with a warmth that feels like a conversation with a wise friend. Each chapter offered small, practical reflections that were easy to read but lingered long after I closed the book. I found myself pausing to journal, to try a suggested practice, or simply to sit in quiet appreciation. Those simple exercises slowly added up to a noticeable shift in how I approached my days.

What I appreciated most was the balance between insight and accessibility. This isn’t preachy self-help jargon — it’s grounded, humble guidance that respects where you are while gently nudging you toward more meaning and presence. The anecdotes felt real, not staged, and the author’s humility made the lessons feel attainable.

The book’s pacing was perfect; I could read a chapter in one sitting or savor it over several days. The physical copy I received was well-produced, with pleasant typography and a durable cover.

If you’re looking for a book that offers gentle clarity and practical tools for cultivating a deeper, calmer life, Filled My Soul is a lovely companion. I’ll be returning to passages again and recommending it to friends.

text:
I'm kind of a cheapskate, so I was a little iffy on spending this much on a bird toy, especially with our parakeet cage filled with $1 plastic bird toys. Luckily, this purchase was definitely worth it! Our parakeets ignored it for a few days before cautiously approaching it, but after a week, they were going absolutely insane over it. I expected it to just be a bowling toy, but our parakeets found more ways to play with it than expected, which was a huge plus and something that we hadn't seen with a lot of the other toys, where they just chew and climb. They like chewing and pulling at the bowling pins, the chains holding the pins, the brown "railing" that the bowling ball is attached, to, and of course, the bowling ball itself. It took a little while longer for them to pull the top part of the stick on the ball to hit the pins, but they eventually did figure it out. The mirror was also a plus, since our keets LOVE mirrors. One of our parakeets likes sticking his head into the hole under the bar and moving everything with his face (he apparently likes doing this with a lot of things ;D)

The toy itself was very easy to install. The nut and screw mechanism keeps the toy securely attached to the cage. Our parakeets sometimes climb on top of the toy while playing, and it's fastened securely enough to support that. Build quality is also very good, and the toy is easy to clean.

Edit: We cleaned the cage and moved stuff around, and it looks like our parakeets didn't like the new location, as they ignored the toy for over 2 weeks. We changed the location again, and they're all over it again! So if you've had your toy in the cage for a while and your birds are used to its presence, but they're not playing with it, maybe moving it elsewhere could help!

I finally decided to try the Great Nutc the Great Nutcracker, and honestly, it lives up to the name. 

The first thing I noticed is the build quality. It’s made of heavy-duty cast metal with a solid, comfortable grip. No wobble, no flex—just a clean, decisive crack every time. I tested it on pecans, almonds, walnuts, and even a few stubborn hazelnuts. The hinge mechanism is smooth and the cracking chamber is well-designed; it holds the nut securely so you don’t have to chase pieces around the counter. Shells split cleanly, and the meat comes out in large, intact pieces far more often than with my old tools.

Cleaning is easy? The smooth surfaces wipe down quickly, and it doesn’t rust or discolor. I’ve had mine for three months of heavy holiday use and it still looks and works like new. The only minor note is that very small nuts like pistachios aren’t ideal—but that’s true of any standard cracker. For everything else, this is the best nutcracker I’ve owned. If you do a lot of baking or just enjoy fresh nuts, this is a worthwhile investment. Highly recommended.

While the less perceptive observer may dismiss Simmons' work as masturbatory egoism, it instead reveals the realization of Nietzsche's Ubermensch. Maligned and misunderstood, the true Nietzschean "Over-Man" rejects conventional behavioral norms and aspires to self-authentication, self-affirmation. This man is Gene Simmons - Bohemian visionary, fearless poet, nimble entrepreneur, and voracious lover of life and women.
Part Byronic hero and part Le Petomaine, Simmons, in "Kiss and Make-Up," offers the reader a glimpse of the redemptive power of debauchery.

title: a page-turning flash of comic brilliance, comic as in deeply human
text:
The chief delight of this book, and there are many, is that Cunningham has tailored a page-turning, oh-no-don't-do-that!, classic plot of confused identity (i.e. a Comedy of Errors) onto a cutting-edge New York scene, and delivered it with humor, humanity, and depth in a style that is fashionable, highly entertaining, and sexy on the one hand, and deeply poetic on the other, as in he has maybe been reading not only the Bard but that other bard, James Merrill. The characters are sharply drawn both in body and mind, and the plot twists true to both life and character.
Other reviewers are complaining about over-writing. While this may be a bit like grousing that chocolate is rich, Cunningham does stumble here and there, e.g. when he has his hero/narrator say, 'What did Shakespeare say? Our little lives are rounded by a sleep.' This is artificial; Shakespeare himself would have solved the problem by giving that line to the college-student daughter, maybe upon seeing her father drinking vodka in the night!
I think Cunningham has just hit his stride--fine as his past achievements are. Hooray for that! Now lay The Tempest aside, Sir, take up your wand and book, and play, play, play for us!

title: Cute
text:
I picked up this "Cute" item after seeing it in a friend’s kitchen, and honestly, it lives up to its name. It’s a small ceramic jar shaped like a little animal face—mine is a cat with a tiny bow. Perfect for holding my loose tea bags, sugar packets, or even as a spare change dish by the door. The craftsmanship is solid: the glaze is smooth, the colors are cheerful, and the lid fits snugly enough to keep out dust. It brings a smile every time I glance at it on my counter.

Functionally, it does what it should. The opening is wide enough to reach in and grab a tea bag without fumbling, and the size is just right for a small countertop. I’ve had it about three months now and the paint hasn’t chipped, even after a gentle drop onto the tile floor (don’t ask). The interior is glazed too, so it’s easy to wipe clean if you use it for sugar or salt.

Why only four stars? Two minor issues. First, the packaging was a bit skimpy—just tissue paper and a thin bubble wrap envelope. The jar arrived fine, but for a ceramic item, I’d expect more padding. Second, the base is a little uneven. It wobbles slightly on a perfectly flat surface. Not enough to tip over, but noticeable if you’re fussy about things sitting level. For the price (around $12), it’s a charming little accent piece, but it’s not a precision product.

Overall, if you want a whimsical touch for your kitchen or desk and don’t mind a slight wobble, this “Cute” jar is a solid choice. It’s better than a lot of the mass-produced kitsch out there. I’d buy another as a gift, though I’d re-pack it more carefully. Recommended for anyone who enjoys a little personality in their home décor.

I read this exact same book under the title Hoarder, which is why I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 5. I almost bought it again, thinking it was a new book by Jess Kidd, but it's the same book as the one published in 2018 under a different title. It's not nice to fool readers. Atria needs to include a disclaimer at the top of the description so that fans of Kidd aren't tricked into buying it again.

But if you haven't read The Hoarder, then this will be new to you. The story is great, lots of humor and fun, magical realism. I'd buy it again if I hadn't already read it.

text:
[[VIDEOID:85cb89701a2f395e248b9d8439d835ea]] This is a great drone for an incredible value. There are tons of features and functionality packed into this tiny drone which is the size of a smartphone when folded.
The drone comes with a case that holds all the accessories and whatnot which is a great addition that many of the bigger brands don't have. Very helpful for transporting the drone.

One small issue though is to disarm the motors, you have to hold the button for 3 seconds. So if you hit something, motors will continue spinning for 3 seconds. Not really that big of an issue for me though as I stay clear of obstacles.
Also the charger is very nice as well as it can charge both the included batteries and plugs into any modern phone cable (USB C).
I would not recommend flying this drone inside though as it is very loud and if you bump into something the propellers will scratch it up/damage it as there are no prop guards.

title: Up
text:
I bought the Up as a gift for my teenage son who’s been getting into trail running and cycling, and it’s become one of those rare purchases that actually exceeds expectations. Right out of the box the unit felt solid and well-made. Setup was straightforward — the quick-start guide was clear, and pairing with my phone took two minutes. The app is intuitive and gives useful summaries without being cluttered.

The first thing that struck me was the accuracy of the activity tracking. Steps, distance, and elevation on hikes matched the readouts on his watch and my bike computer within a small margin. Sleep tracking has been surprisingly helpful: he used to complain about feeling tired all day, but after a few nights of reviewing the detailed sleep stages and suggestions, he changed his evening routine and now reports waking up more refreshed. Battery life is strong; we go several days between charges even with nightly sleep monitoring enabled.

For someone active, the Up’s fitness coaching features are a standout. The guided goals and gentle reminders helped him increase daily movement without feeling nagged. It also integrates nicely with other apps we use for running, so we didn’t have to manually transfer data. Durability has been impressive — it’s been knocked, splashed, and worn during muddy trail runs and still looks and functions like new.

A few relatively minor quibbles: the band could be a touch softer for all-day comfort, especially in hot weather, and the vibration alerts are on the light side (easy to miss during a loud workout). Also, the app’s social/competitions features are a bit basic compared to larger ecosystems, but that’s not a dealbreaker for us.

Overall, the Up hits the sweet spot for reliable tracking, helpful coaching, and good battery life in a rugged package. My son is using it daily and his activity levels have gone up noticeably. If you want a solid, no-fuss tracker that actually helps you move more and sleep better, this one is well worth the price.

text:
I was pleasantly surprised by this purchase. I ordered it because I needed something functional and reasonably priced, and while it’s not perfect, it’s become a useful part of my daily routine.

First the positives: the build quality feels solid for the price. The materials don’t feel cheap, and the seams/finishes are tidy. It looks better in person than in the product photos — the color is slightly richer and the texture has a subtle sheen that fits well with my other kitchen items. Setup was straightforward; everything that needed to be attached fit together easily without extra tools or guesswork. Instructions were clear and concise, which is always a relief.

Performance-wise it does the job. It handles the expected tasks without fuss and I’ve had no major issues after a month of regular use. It’s relatively quiet in operation and energy use seems reasonable, though I didn’t time or meter it. The capacity is a good middle ground — large enough for my small family needs but not so big that it takes up too much counter or storage space. Cleaning is simpler than I anticipated; most surfaces wipe down easily and a few removable parts are dishwasher-safe, which I appreciate.

Some drawbacks kept me from giving this five stars. The manual could use more troubleshooting tips — a few common questions (like how to reset or deal with minor jams) aren’t addressed. One small plastic clip creaked after a couple of uses, and while it still functions, the noise is noticeable. Also, while the product matches the advertised dimensions closely, the fit in a narrow cabinet is snugger than I expected; if you have tight storage, double-check measurements before buying.

Customer support was responsive when I emailed with a question about replacement parts. The reply came within 48 hours and included helpful links and clear next steps, which was reassuring.

Overall, this product delivers excellent value. It balances design, performance, and price well. If you want something reliable for everyday use without spending a lot, this is worth considering. Just keep an eye on the small clip area and be sure it will fit in your intended storage spot. I’d buy it again.

title: Items missing :(
text:
I don’t usually write reviews, but I felt I had to after this disappointing purchase. I bought this set for my seven-year-old’s birthday because the pictures and description made it look like a complete kit with everything needed to build multiple models. What arrived was missing several key pieces, and the whole experience felt like a bait-and-switch.

Right out of the box I noticed the box felt lighter than I expected. We opened it together and started sorting parts, following the instructions included. About 20 minutes in we hit a wall: essential connector pieces and what should have been one of the motor assemblies were nowhere to be found. I checked every compartment and bag multiple times, double-checked the parts list in the manual, and even dumped everything out onto the carpet to be certain. Several unique, identifiable parts that are shown in the product photos and listed as included were absent.

Customer service was not much help. I reached out via the seller’s contact page and got an automated confirmation immediately, but then silence for days. A week later I received a generic reply asking for photos and order information, which I supplied. After that, no follow-up and no resolution. I tried again to escalate through Amazon, and while they eventually offered a partial refund or a return for a full refund, it was cumbersome: I would have had to box everything back up, ship it off, and wait weeks. By then my child’s party had passed and the toy lost its purpose.

The product that did arrive looks well-made and the parts we did have seem sturdy and engaging, so I can only judge based on what was actually delivered. For the price, I expected a complete set. Missing parts render the kit unusable for the builds shown in the instructions, which was the whole point of buying it.

If you’re considering this for a gift or a project with a deadline, beware: there’s a real chance this will show up incomplete and it appears the seller may not be responsive. I’m giving one star because the product as received failed to meet basic expectations and customer service didn’t resolve the issue in any timely or satisfactory way.
