The printer showed low ink warnings almost immediately, then refused to print at all after maybe 10–15 pages. I replaced the cartridge with a brand-new one from the pack and had the same experience: it lasted only a handful of pages before going dry.

Print quality started okay but degraded quickly, with faint, streaky text and uneven coverage. I tried cleaning the printheads and running the printer’s maintenance cycle, which helped only a little and didn’t change the fact that the cartridge capacity seemed far below what it should be. I double-checked that I had installed everything correctly and used the correct cartridges for my model.

I like the idea of a lower-cost alternative to OEM ink, but these cartridges felt like poor value since I had to buy more replacements so soon. They may work for someone with very light, occasional printing needs, but for regular home or small office use I can’t recommend them. Two stars because they do print initially, but the extremely short life and inconsistent output make them frustrating and unreliable.

title: One of the most enlightening books on politics from the ...
text:
I’ve read a lot of political books over the years, but this one genuinely stands out. It doesn’t just rehash tired talking points or rely on partisan slogans. Instead, it offers a clear, well-researched framework for understanding how power actually works behind the scenes. The author manages to be both deeply analytical and surprisingly accessible—yes, readable. I found myself underlining passages on nearly every page, not because the language was overly dramatic, but because each insight was so perfectly distilled.

What I appreciated most was the balance. The book doesn’t preach or tell you what to think; it gives you the tools to think more clearly about the forces shaping our political reality. The chapter on institutional inertia alone changed how I view gridlock. I’ve recommended it to friends on both sides of the aisle, and every single one of them came back saying the same thing: “I never thought of new way looking at things.”

If you’re tired of shallow punditry and want something that actually deepens your understanding without drowning you in jargon, this is it. I looked. It’s not light bedtime reading, but it’s rewarding in way few political books are. Five stars without hesitation.

After watching the film, "Finding Neverland", I was curious to learn more about the fates of the 5 boys orphaned in the story. Although Barrie did not gain custody of the boys, he did maintain a strong presence in their lifes. In fact, he did much more than just keep an eye on them over the years. He showered them with gifts; traveled with them; and of course, financially helped them. He seemed particularly obsessed with the older boy, George. Barrie loved to photograph all of the boys and some of the photos included in this book show the children naked. Was Barrie a pedophile of sorts? None of the boys ever accused him of such. And Barrie's love and concern for the boys did not end when they became men who were tall enough to tower over the diminutive playwright.

This is a comprehensive look at Barrie's life without passing any judgement. That is left to the reader. And after reading this book, I have to say that I'm STILL unable to figure the man out. I bought this on a recommendation from a friend because I’ve been struggling with chronically dry, flaky skin for years, and I can honestly say this product has been a game changer for me. It also calmed some of the red, irritated patches I used to get in cold weather. I’ve used it consistently for about three weeks now and the overall texture of my skin has improved: smoother, more even, and better able to hold in hydration.

The scent is very mild and non-offensive, which I appreciate because strong fragrances tend to irritate my skin. Packaging is sturdy and the pump dispenses just the right amount, so a little goes a long way. I’ve recommended it to my sister who has eczema-prone skin, and she’s seen results too.

Only minor drawback is that it’s a bit pricier than some drugstore options, but given the effectiveness and how little product I need per use, it’s worth the cost for me. If you have dry or sensitive skin and are tired of temporary fixes, give this a try—you might be as pleased with it as I am. Five stars.

title: Sheds like other goat hair brushes, but great value
text:
I’ve been using this goat hair makeup brush for a few weeks now, and for the price it’s a solid find. Right away it felt soft and comfortable in my hand — the handle has a good weight and the bristles are plush without feeling flimsy. It picks up powder and blush nicely and blends product out to a natural, airbrushed finish. For everyday use it performs well.

That said, it does shed. I noticed loose hairs coming out the first couple of uses and I still get an occasional stray bristle when I wash it. It’s comparable to other goat hair brushes I’ve owned in that regard, so it wasn’t a deal-breaker for me, but if you’re expecting a completely shed-free brush you might be disappointed. Washing gently and letting it dry flat helped reduce the amount of shedding over time.

Cleaning is straightforward — soap and lukewarm water do the job — and the brush retained its shape after drying. The bristles didn’t become splayed or scratchy. I’ve used it with powder blush, bronzer and a light face powder, and it worked well across those products. It’s not a dense buffing brush for heavy cream products, but that’s not what I bought it for.

Overall, I’m happy with this purchase. Performance is very good for the price, and while the shedding is a downside, it’s consistent with other natural goat-hair brushes I’ve owned. If you want an affordable, soft brush for powders and blending, this one delivers great value. I’d recommend it with the caveat that you should handle it gently and expect a bit of shedding initially.

My kitten loved this cat litter but after several months, had respiratory problems (silicosis symptoms). When I took him to the vet to have him neutered, they couldn't proceed because they noticed he was short of breath and after listening to his lungs (lots of crackling short breaths & coughing occasionally), doing bloodwork (which was negative for any infection), an X-ray (which didn't show anything) & then giving me antibiotics because she knew something was wrong but couldn't find a reason for his respiratory problems. $375.00 dollars later, I brought home my sick kitten who still wasn't fixed.
Later that day it hit me that this fine, powder like liter might be the cause of his symptoms. After looking up how this fine silica sand could cause respiratory problems, I called my vet, explaining about the cat liter I was using and now his symptoms made sense to her. I too have been having similar respiratory problems (since I had a second litter box near my bed to make sure the kitten didn't have any accidents at night).
Although I had no problems when I only had my two adult cats using this litter, the kitten tended to play with the fine sand and was very thorough when covering offensive odors not just for himself but for the other two cats too. He often had pink sand on his nose, so it's not a big leap that some of it was getting into his lungs.
Just wanted to warn everyone that this litter is not a good choice for kittens. I've switched both cat boxes to fresh step premium crystals, it's a larger, pearl like bb which has no dust and is too big to be inhaled! Hope this helps others whose kittens are short of breath.

text:
POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD:

I honestly have to say that it's not only the best book I've ever read but probably one of the greatest pieces of writing I've ever read. From beginning to end, I found myself completely drawn to the story of Jersey City bus driver Andre Bolden.

The book is a real page turner and what really kept me hooked besides wanting to know the story resolution was the relationship between Andre and Sandra, the mother of his son. Sandra had so much resistance towards him that I kept turning pages eager to see if Andre could ever get over that emotional fortress. At the same time, the theme about snitching itself was handled very well by Mr. Mattison without being too imposing about it. Rather than making it about a guy or people around him who don't snitch, it comes across as a story of a man whose wrong choices in life start to eat him up bit by bit, living in the fear of losing his life as he had with getting kicked out of school, losing Sandra, and eventually losing his job. He thinks living back with Sandra and Little Dre would solve all his problems. But what transpires over the course of the book leads Andre to a much higher purpose of standing up for himself and those dearest to him.

I also want to applaud Mr. Mattison himself for being able to write the book using little to no profanity. I'm sure it was quite a challenge to do that given the genre and the tone of the book.

Overall, this is a must read for teenagers and adults across America. Look forward to the movie adaptation.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text:
I’ll admit, I ordered these silicone food storage lids after a particularly frustrating evening of wrestling with plastic wrap that refused to cling, then gave up entirely and slid off a bowl of leftover soup. I didn’t have high hopes. The price was reasonable, the photos looked fine, but I figured I’d be back to using the original wrap within a week. I am genuinely pleased to say I was wrong.

The set came in a simple package, no frills. The silicone feels thicker than I expected, not flimsy at all. I have a mix of odd-sized bowls and containers—some square, some round, a few with slight rims—and I was skeptical that one lid popped on a rectangular casserole dish that I actually smiled. It sealed tight without any stretching or snapping. I gave it the shake test over the sink, and nothing leaked. That was the moment I started feeling pleasantly surprised.

I’ve been using them for about three weeks now. They work great on my stainless steel mixing bowls, on a ceramic pasta bowl that’s a bit wider at the top, and even on a plastic containers that never had matching lids. The seal is reliable for both fridge and pantry storage. I also tried one on a half-cut avocado, and it stayed fresh overnight with minimal browning. Microwaving? Yes, I tested a lid on a bowl of soup for two minutes, and it didn’t warp, no weird smell. They’re easy to clean by hand, and I’ve thrown a couple in the dishwasher without issue.

The only reason I’m giving four stars instead of five is that the smallest size is a little loose on my. It barely covers a ramekin, and I wish it were an inch larger to fit standard cereal bowls. Also, after several washes, one lid developed a faint white film that scrubbed off with a vinegar rinse, but it’s something to note. Still, for the money, I am genuinely surprised at how much these have reduced my reliance on single-use plastic wrap. I’m buying another set to keep at the office. If you’re skeptical like I was, give them a try. They might just win you over too.

title: It is like having a conversation with her
text:
Full disclosure: I have met Angelo Lowery at a writer’s retreat in Sedona Arizona. Angelo is in person, as she is portrayed in her memoir, “I am and the Spirit Walks with me,” a force to be reckoned with.
When I met Angelo, it was the first time in my life I met someone who has a direct line of communication to God. Her eyes are full of light, and she exudes a natural sense of strength and power. Reading her book, it was a surprise to me to hear all that she has endured in her life – abuse, betrayal, stunning loss. And yet, in her life, she has been able to rise above the pain to directly touch God. She has turned betrayal into blessing, loss into communion and pain into healing.
Angelo’s book is imperfect, as are many self-published books that do not have the benefit of a high-rolling publishing house behind them. But in its imperfection, it is perfectly Angelo. It is like having a conversation with her. She writes as she speaks, in a lovely, sometimes innocent, sometimes all-knowing, inspired and warm tone….until she speaks the words she hears from God. It was fascinating to read how distinctly different were the voices of her book – hers versus God’s.
Angelo is a warrior, she has survived countless horrors that would crumple the best of us. How did she do that? She shares that she always knew she was somehow chosen by God to do special work (Angelo is a gifted healer today). Was this the key to her resilience? For many who suffer adversity, their experience becomes an excuse to visit adversity on others. For Angelo, it became an opportunity to draw close to God and heal both herself and others.
I would love for Angelo to share next how we mere mortals, those of us who have not felt chosen, can also rise above adversity in our lives to become a conduit of good and love and spirit as she has done. Thank you for sharing your heroin’s journey, Angelo.

title: Opened my EYES!
text:
I rarely write reviews, but I had to for this one — Opened my EYES! completely changed how I look at my daily life and the choices I make. From the first chapter I felt like the author was speaking directly to me: clear, compassionate, and unafraid to challenge common assumptions. The blend of personal anecdotes and practical exercises made the ideas land in a way that was both emotionally resonant and immediately useful.

What surprised me most was how accessible the writing is. Complex concepts are explained in straightforward language, and the short reflection prompts at the end of each chapter helped me turn insight into action. I started small — just a five-minute breathing practice and a couple of the suggested journal questions — and already noticed a shift in my focus and patience. Several passages made me pause and reconsider long-held habits, and the “reality check” sections were gentle but incisive.

The pacing is excellent; the book moves quickly enough to stay engaging but contains enough depth to be worth revisiting. I also appreciated the resource list at the back — books, apps, and websites that expand on the topics covered. The author’s voice feels trustworthy and grounded, not preachy, which made it easy to accept the tougher suggestions.

After finishing it, I gifted copies to two friends because I genuinely thought they would benefit. If you’re open to looking at your life with a little more clarity and intention, this book is a must-read. Five stars.

UPDATE 08/12/2018 REPLACED BELT

After about a year of daily use I noticed a black powder accumulating on the ground under the belt cover. I figured out it was the belt wearing out. I purchased a new one (OEM PN 5PK1320). I couldn't find any instructions on the Sunny site but it's not that hard. Remove all the screws from the belt cover, including the one that holds it in place on the left side of the bike. You might have to remove the right pedal to get the cover completely off. Once you have the cover off, remove the 10-mm retaining nuts on the two eyebolts that align the flywheel, then loosen the two 19-mm nuts that hold the flywheel in place. Lift the flywheel far enough up to slip the old belt out and the new belt in. Align the belt on the front pulley and reattach the 10-mm eyebolts to the frame, then tighten the 19-mm flywheel bolts. Place the belt on the back pulley as far as you can get it, then turn the crank to get it on the rest of the way, the same way you get a chain back onto a bicycle chain ring. Put the cover back on and you are done.

title: Better than the alternatives
text: If I had to describe this fan, I cannot think of anything more appropriate than "good enough." i bought it to replace my 12-year-old Lasko fan, which was taller at 40 inches and bulkier by far. After putting it together (take 10-15 minutes with a regular screwdriver - the screws and plastic can be a bit finicky), I realized that the first one I bought made a clicking noise as the blades spun, and the longer I had it on, the more high-pitched it sounded -- definitely not good for trying to sleep. My second model doesn't make that sound; although, it's far from whisper quiet. It's quiet enough to have on while I sleep or watch TV, however. This new fan is definitely weaker than my old one, and I rarely use it on the second speed and never on the lowest. Interestingly, it turns on to the highest speed and shifts lower. Some people may be disappointed to find out that's all there is. I can actually use the remote from my old fan with this model, which I like. I can keep one in each room where I may use it (it's definitely light enough to move between them), The new remote, which doesn't come with batteries, is a little less easy to use in the dark because of the buttons. And while it can hook onto the back of the fan for safekeeping, I preferred the way my old fan had a slot. The remote has a tendency to fall off. With that said, this is the third type of fan I've purchased to replace my defunct one and the only one tall enough and strong enough to work with the height of my bed and layout of my room.  I doubt this model will last over a decade, and I'd prefer if the price were under $50, but it'll do.

text:
I bought this book hoping for a relaxing way to unwind after work, and in that regard, it delivers. The designs are intricate enough that you can lose yourself for hours, and there’s a decent variety of patterns, from mandalas to floral motifs to geometric shapes. If you’re someone who likes detail and geometric shapes. detail, this will keep your hands and mind busy. I’ve probably spent about ten sessions on it so far and I’m not even halfway through. The paper quality is acceptable—thick enough that markers don’t bleed through, though I wouldn’t push it with heavy ink.

Where it’s the palette that leaves me frustrated. The included color guide or recommended on the back cover suggests certain combos, but the actual printed colors in the book are a bit muddy and inconsistent. Some pages have a warmer tint; others lean cooler, which means your finished piece might look disjointed if you don’t compensate with your own colored pencils or pens. I ended up ignoring the suggested palette entirely and just used my own set. The title says “vibrant,” but the tone palette” but the actual experience is more meh—not terrible, but not inspiring. It’s fine if you just need a mindless activity, but if you’re picky about color harmony, you might find yourself adjusting more than you’d like. A decent time filler, but not a standout.

title: a refreshingly authentic journey
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to share. From the first page I felt transported — not by a glossy, romanticized version of the past, but by an honest, tactile rendering of place and character that stayed with me long after I closed the cover. The author’s voice is remarkably clear and unpretentious; scenes unfold with sensory detail that never feels forced, and the dialogue rings true. I appreciated how the narrative resisted easy answers, allowing the characters to be complicated and real.

What surprised me most was how refreshingly human the journey felt. There are moments of quiet humor, small acts of kindness, and honest reckonings that made me root for these people, even when they made mistakes. The pacing is thoughtful, never rushed, and the ending is satisfying without being tidy. I gifted copies to two friends because I wanted to discuss it—rare praise from me. If you’re looking for a novel that feels lived-in and sincere, this is a gem.

title: Great product ! Great for my long trip from VA to VT !
text: I purchased this for a long trip from VA to VT. I wanted to talk on the phone if needed, and do it hands free. This works great, as I had no Bluetooth in my 08 Nissan Altima. It only works through your car speakers when you have the radio on AUX input. This wasn't a problem on a long trip, as I had thousands of songs on my Samsung Galaxy S5 to listen to. I could listen to my music, skip songs when I wanted by pushing a button, and when a call came in all I had to do was say "answer" or push a button to accept the call. When the call ends, the music picks back up where it left off. To make a call, I could do it by voice (call Tina at home) or use the phone to dial it manually. It then stops the music and dials who you are calling. It doesn't work unless you have your car radio on AUX. You can't use the actual radio and use the SoundBot at the same time. It comes with a 12v plug (cigarette lighter plug) that has 3 USB outlets on it. One of those is used for the SoundBot, the other 2 can be used for GPS, phone charger, etc. Then there is a 3.5mm plug that goes to the AUX input on your radio. Your phone then connects wirelessly through Bluetooth to the SoundBot. I used my GPS on my phone, and the directions was heard through my car speakers over my music I was playing through my phone. I made and received many calls on my trip, and everybody said they heard me loud and clear. Great price on the SoundBot, and I loved it. I can't use it when listening to my local radio stations at home, but if I have it plugged in and connected, I can push the AUX button on my radio and use it then to talk. Or push AUX then make a call if I need to. A great product that works as intended. I love it !

Unfortunately, if they are detected as being removed from the charging case, they turn on. I was confused when one of my earbuds was at a 65% charge while the other was 100%. title: Disappointing
text:
I wanted to like this book — the premise sounded promising and the cover copy promised an engaging, fresh perspective — but overall it left me frustrated and underwhelmed. I’m giving it two stars because there are moments where the author’s insight shines through, but those are too few and too inconsistent to recommend this to most readers.

The pacing felt uneven from the start. The opening chapters dragged with excessive background detail that didn’t seem to serve the plot or character development, while later sections rushed through significant events as if the author realized halfway through that there wasn’t enough space. Important relationships and motivations were sketched rather than fully developed, so when the story demanded emotional payoff, I found myself uninvested.

Characterization was another weak spot. A few characters have distinct, memorable traits, but many felt like archetypes or plot devices. Dialogue frequently reads as stilted or expository; it tells rather than shows. I appreciate books that trust the reader to make connections, but here the opposite was true — the narration sometimes over-explains, which made the prose feel clunky.

On the positive side, the writing style is competent and there are flashes of genuinely good sentences and observations. A subplot about the protagonist’s past had potential and did deliver a handful of poignant moments. The book also wrapped up with a satisfying, if predictable, conclusion that ties most loose ends.

If you’re a completist fan of the author you might find value here, and readers who enjoy leisurely reads may appreciate the detailed descriptions. For me, though, the uneven pacing, thin character development, and occasional clumsy exposition made this a disappointing read that I can’t wholeheartedly recommend.

title: teenage mutant ninja turtles shellraiser
text:
I have been a massive fan of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles since I was a kid in the nineties, so when I saw the Shellraiser on sale, I knew I had to grab it for my seven-year-old nephew. He is currently in his absolute TMNT phase, and this toy has become his favorite thing in his entire room. It has been over three weeks, and it is still in remarkably good condition despite being dragged around the house, taken on "missions" in the backyard, and occasionally stepped on. The build quality is surprisingly robust for a toy in this price range. The treads grip well on both carpet and hardwood, which means it actually moves where you want it to go rather than getting stuck under the sofa legs every two seconds.

The sound effects are a nice touch without being overwhelmingly loud or annoying to adults. It plays the classic theme song and has a few explosion noises that really sell the immersive experience for the kids. The remote control is intuitive enough for a child to use independently after just a few minutes of practice, which was a huge bonus. I also appreciate that the opening mechanism for the rear cargo area works smoothly; it allows easy access to the four original action figures, which fits snugly inside. We did have to buy new batteries immediately, as the included ones were likely just for display, but that is standard practice. Assembly was minimal—just snapping on the treads and putting batteries in the shell. It is a fantastic gift option that offers genuine play value rather than just being a static display piece. If you are looking for a durable, engaging toy that brings the nostalgia of the cartoon to life, the Shellraiser is worth every penny. My nephew’s joy when he opened it was priceless, and that alone makes the purchase a success. Highly recommended for any young ninja turtle fan.

title: Unoriginal and Uninspiring
text: If you happened upon this book by chance and are looking for some quantitative market insights, then do not be fooled by the books title. From a knowledge perspective the book is worthless. There are plenty of better books on investment theory. Paulos has "regressed to the mean" here. This work merely capitalises on his previous, better efforts. The book is tedious, and in many respects his arguments are fallacious. For example he postulates that if most investors became indexers then markets would cease to be efficient. This is not supported by economic theory, where the contrary holds. It only takes a small number of active investors to retain market efficiency. If you are in search of investment knowledge you will be well served by the author Ron Ross in "Unbeatable Markets". Paulos has not made a contribution here, he has merely compiled a collection of anecdotes from other authors and tried to spin it to make it look like his own. His humour didn't work for me either. Suspiciously enough, both batteries have identical info, including the serial number:
Model Information:
Serial Number: GSA-A1175-ASMB012-3c28-42c
Manufacturer: GSA-A1175
Device name: ASMB012
Pack Lot Code: 012d
PCB Lot Code: 050d
Firmware Version: 646e
Hardware Revision: 2800
Cell Revision: 0000

Worth the price? Not really. One out of three might be a good batting average in baseball but not for purchased products. Take your chances, you might get lucky.

title: Excellent narrative but questionable claims
text:
This is an excellent narrative history of contributors, ideas, movements, and events in German culture. Peter Watson communicates his encyclopaedic knowledge very readably. He summarises major thinkers and cultural movements concisely, but rigorously, with a great gift for succinct meaningful précis.

However, Watson’s claim that the extent of the German contribution to modernity is unique (eg page 828 on ‘The First XI of Modern History’ which includes Mendel!), is unsustainable. Roy Porter claims otherwise in his ‘Enlightenment: Britain and the Creation of the Modern World’ as does Sudhir Hazareesingh in ‘How the French Think’. It is in any case a claim which lends support to the objectionable idea of German superiority. Renaissance and Enlightenment were pan-European projects.

Watson’s interesting thesis is that Pietism, Bildung and Innerlichkeit account for the German genius, but he does not show how these qualities of individual worth and spirituality fit with a strong tendency to communal obedience in German culture. He does however show how nationalism was initially a liberal idea challenging the old illiberal autocratic feudal German states.

Watson does not cover the major contribution of church, particularly in post-war German society. The West German Protestant church established the bi-annual ‘Kirchentag’ movement dedicated to persuade the German Christian to follow individual conscience rather than state dictat, and to include the outsider. The East German church hosted the political reform movement that led to ‘die Wende’, although the East’s DDR resisted acknowledgement of Holocaust guilt for too long.

Watson has provided a mine of data for a fuller debate on the causal factors, the nature, and the extent of the German contribution.

text:
I have mixed feelings about "Another Triumph to Maureen." The writing is sharp and the pacing keeps you turning pages, but I’m not sure it fully delivers on its promise. The central character, Maureen, is wonderfully drawn—fierce, flawed, and utterly human. Her journey through her journey she goes on feels authentic, and there are moments of real emotional weight. The dialogue crackles, and the author clearly has a deep understanding of the small, quiet triumphs that define a life.

That said, I found some of the subplots underdeveloped. A few side characters appear promising but then fade into the background without resolution. The ending also felt a bit rushed, as if the author was trying to wrap things up too neatly after such quickly that the emotional payoff didn’t quite land. It’s a solid read, but not the knockout I was hoping for.

If you enjoy it for the strong central character and the vivid writing, but go in knowing that not every thread gets tied off neatly. If you like character-driven stories with a slightly imperfect finish, this will still be worth your time. Four stars from me—good, but not great.

title: Riddle of the Book
text:
It might seem surprising, but professional bibliographers (and I am one) invariably judge a book first by its publisher. In the case of this book, it is published by Springer, a prestigious European information conglomerate. This is important because the author of this book has notably airy qualifications as a "reporter." Digital Publishing allows everyone to be an author and anyone to be a publisher, and if you can tweet you can be a "reporter." Thus, it is truly important for readers to have some sort of crap detector in place. Unfortunately, the publisher test failed on this book.

This book has virtually no redeeming substance; Wikipedia says it better -- and cheaper. The author's writing style relies on a snotty-know-it-all approach, that is particularly irritating because he has no credentials. (As an example, he even manages to insult little Corvallis, Oregon as "a jerkwater town," even though the place is a pleasantly progressive college town). Essentially, the book is about grinding axes with political correctness uber alles.

Technically, the Kindle version of the book has way too many formatting errors and unpleasant (and unnecessary) decorative images. Why ebook publishers -- and especially wealthy publishers like Springer -- can't seem to at least look at their digital product in Kindle Previewer is a bigger riddle than Kennewick Man.

I've been using this backpack cooler almost daily since I bought it two weeks ago. Some reviewers say the top zipper leaks if you use ice that melts. I can well imagine...so don't use ice.

There is plenty of room in this thing for enough food and drinks for two or three people. It's kept me fed through a few double shifts and everything stays cold for a good 20 hours. The straps are long and wide enough to be comfortable when wearing this as a backpack, and I'm a pretty big guy. It also carries well slung over one shoulder, which is not always the case.

Some of the reviews fault the zippers for breaking. Yeah, I can see that happening if you jerk them, are impatient, or in a hurry and not paying attention. I've had no problems with them. Same with the stitching; I pack out at about 20 pounds and I've seen no signs of wear and tear, yet. It has only been two weeks, sure, but still...

Pros: keeps food plenty cold for a whole day when used with re-freezable ice packs; lots of room inside, comfortable straps. Netting pockets for water bottles, etc. on the sides are deep and big enough for wide bottles.

Cons: zippered storage compartments on the front and top are inadequate. No "waterproof" storage compartment for keys, phone, etc.

title: I love this book!
text:
I really enjoyed reading this book! Mona, the main character, is easy to relate to...and she has red hair! Being a ginger myself, I have a special affinity toward ginger characters (we're under represented)! My bias aside though, Holden's writing style really brings the characters to life. They are realistic...their lives aren't spectacular, they don't have these amazing careers or live in a mansion. They are normal people, living in an average house, complete with a crotchedy old neighbor! I love it. It was so easy to relate to their lives and picture them as my own neighbors or somebody I would be friends with. I was really touched by Mona's rediscovery of herself and her husband. There is a lot of laughter in Becoming Mona Lisa too...Mona and her husband have witty, cynical, comical personalities and I found myself laughing quite a bit. I also found myself feeling all gushy over the rekindling romance between husband and wife.

Holden does such an amazing job of describing the surroundings that I feel I could draw a picture of the Siggs home! I can picture the mean old codger that lives across the street, the bird infestation, the mannequins, even the Walmart that Mona works at. Throughout reading this book, I was reminded of the reasons I love my fiance and what brought us together. I don't know if Holden intended this...but it definitely reminded me not to take him or our relationship for granted. The book flows really well and I definitely found myself wanting to read more after I finished. So I'm really hoping there's a sequel to Becoming Mona Lisa, because I really wanna follow the next chapter in Mona's life...and I REALLY wanna know what's up with the room! I definitely strongly recommend this book.

Several plot threads are introduced but never properly resolved, which left me frustrated rather than intrigued.

The writing itself has moments of genuine insight, but they’re scattered between awkward phrasing and unnecessary tangents. I also felt the protagonist’s decisions were often contrived to force conflict rather than arising naturally from characterization. Secondary characters are thinly drawn, so it’s hard to invest emotionally in their outcomes.

On the positive side, the author clearly has a voice and some good ideas, and a few chapters genuinely resonated with me. But for the price, I expected a more polished and coherent read. I’d recommend this only to someone curious about the concept and willing to tolerate a messy execution.

title: A fantastic thriller!
text:
THE VACATION by T.M. Logan primarily follows Kate, a wife and mother of two meeting up with her three best friends and their families at a stunning vineyard villa in France for a vacation to celebrate their 40th birthdays. It is meant to be a time to reconnect with each other and their families with good wine, good food and good company. Things aren’t starting off on an ideal note, however.

Kate has a feeling that something is going on with her husband and she manages to log into his phone to check his messages. She sees a back and forth conversation which seems to confirm that her husband is having an affair. Worst yet, the messages imply that the other woman is one of her best friends. As Kate seeks to identify the traitorous friend, it is clear that all of her friends have secrets to hide.

I have been in the mood for thrillers and this one did not disappoint. Once I got into the story, I could not put it down! We are primarily reading from Kate’s POV, hearing her suspicions, seeing her interactions with her friends and family. The author also gives us occasional chapters from the perspective of other characters, Kate’s friends, their husbands and the kids as well. It seems that almost everyone has something to hide and the author does a great job of dropping clues to redirect Kate’s suspicions and the readers’ as well.

This is very much a slow burn book for the first three-quarters or so. There is a lot of family drama and mystery going on which creates that slow build up to the last quarter where things really start to happen, ramping up the thriller elements. On top of the issues of what is going on with Kate’s wife, there are clearly secrets between the teens of their families and with the other women. The slow burn is done very well and it kept me entirely hooked throughout as the author takes the time to really delve into the different characters and potential suspects for everything that is going on.

I would highly recommend adding THE VACATION by T.M. Logan to your TBR!

The bad - first, they took away the intercom button. Instead of just pushing the intercom button and then selecting which handset to call, you have to select menu, then scroll down several steps, then select intercom, and then scroll down to pick the handset to call. The steps are slow - every time, the menu takes a noticeable amount of time to appear, as does the list of handsets. So, the entire process is at least 3 times as long and cumbersome as before. Second, every single time Panasonic comes out with a new version of these phones, they go out of their way to make sure that loyal, repeat customers can't use the old bases to charge the new handsets. One issue that I have ran in to is that when my ear wax drains, the silicon buds clog up. My solution to this is carry a small paper clip inside the case so that I can dig the wax out periodically. I bought this kettle hoping for the convenience of an automatic shut-off when the water reaches a boil. Unfortunately, it does not bump or click off on its own as advertised. title: Well made hat to protect against sunburn
text:
I bought this sun hat before a week-long beach trip and it has become my go-to item whenever I’m planning to be outside for more than an hour. Right out of the box you can tell it’s well made — the stitching is even, the brim keeps its shape, and the fabric feels substantial without being heavy. I needed something that would actually protect my face and neck from prolonged sun exposure, and this hat exceeded my expectations.

The brim is wide enough to shade my entire face and most of my neck when I’m standing or sitting, and it doesn’t flop down into my eyes like some floppy hats do. It has a slight wire or reinforcement around the edge that holds the shape but still allows me to fold it for packing. I was able to flatten it into my beach bag for travel and it popped back into shape perfectly when I took it out.

Comfort is another big plus. The inner band is soft and didn’t irritate my forehead even after hours of wear. There’s an adjustable chin cord that keeps the hat secure when it’s windy — I was grateful for that on a blustery coastline day. I also appreciated the ventilation panels (or breathable weave) that kept my head from getting too hot; I didn’t sweat nearly as much as I expected, even in direct sun and humidity.

Functionally it delivers on sun protection: paired with sunscreen I avoided any sunburn on my face and ears the entire trip. The color held up too — I picked a light neutral that didn’t fade after multiple outings. It’s easy to clean; a quick hand wash and air dry got rid of salt and sunscreen residue.

If I have any minor nitpicks, it’s that the sizing runs a touch large on my small head even tightened to the smallest setting, but the chin cord always keeps it snug. Also, it’s not a fashion statement — it’s clearly built for function over runway style — but I don’t mind that at all for what I bought it for.

Overall, great quality, very practical, and built to last. If you’re looking for a reliable hat to protect against sunburn during outdoor activities, this is a solid choice.

The final book of Lynette Eason's Deadly Reunions triology, When a Secret Kills reveals an ending to this story that no one sees coming.

Jillian Carter finally returns home after 10 years of hiding - running for her life. She's come to the point of no return - the answers must be revealed before anyone else dies. But coming home doesn't solve the problem - only when the truth is revealed will her life and the lives of her friends and family finally be safe again.

Lynette Eason has done a wonderful job of building up a story that keeps readers turning pages, eager to solve the mystery of "who done what" as they cheer on Jillian. From developing characters who are easy to love (or hate in the case of the villains) to keeping readers guessing as they read, Eason has written another stellar novel!

[Spoiler Alert]: One of my favorite aspects of this story is Colton's reaction to meeting his and Jillian's daughter. Even through his anger at missing the first ten years of his little girl's life, the love and acceptance he displays is truly moving.

I give When a Secret Kills five stars!

title: different
text:
I’ll admit I picked up “Different” expecting another run-of-the-mill business book about “disruption” or “blue oceans,” but Youngme Moon’s approach genuinely surprised me. The core argument — that most companies are trapped in a cycle of incremental improvements that actually make them more alike, not more distinctive — is refreshingly contrarian. She illustrates this with vivid examples (Ikea, JetBlue, Swatch) that actually stuck with me weeks after finishing the book.

What earns this a solid four stars is the clarity of the diagnosis. Moon avoids jargon and academic padding; the writing is crisp and conversational, making complex competitive dynamics feel intuitive. Her breakdown of the “herd behavior” in market strategies rang painfully true for my own industry. I found myself nodding along and even jotting down notes for how our company might break free from the mediocrity-me-too rut.

So why not five stars? The prescription side feels thinner than the critique. Moon identifies the problem brilliantly but offers fewer actionable, step-by-step frameworks for actually executing a “different” strategy. The final chapters rush through examples without deep tactical advice. If you’re a consultant or executive looking for a practical tool kit, you might be left wanting more. Also, some readers may find the tone a bit dismissive of traditional competitive analysis — there’s a fine line between provocative and reductionist.

Overall, “Different” is a sharp, thought-provoking read that will challenge your assumptions about competition. It’s best consumed as a mindset shift rather than a playbook. Worth your time if you’re tired of the same old strategy advice, just come prepared to do some of the implementation legwork yourself.

text:
"Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend" is McCay's overlooked masterpiece. "Little Nemo" gets all the press (and it deserves the highest possible praise) but The Fiend is often equally compelling. More adult in subject matter than Nemo, it is less visually resplendant, but still quite powerful in its invocation of the fears and hopes underlying our day-to-day thoughts.

This collection is the standard, but it collects only a fraction of what McCay produced (this is a reprint of a 1905 volume, but the strip ran until 1910 or 1911). You can pick up the Checker "Early Works" volumes for a more complete run (in questionable quality) and there are more strips in the Canemaker book on McCay as well as the Fantagraphics "Daydreams and Nightmares" (which I highly recommend).

Checker has since produced a fine collection: [[ASIN:1933160659 The Saturdays]] which would make a great follow-up to this book.

When I first wrote this review in 2006, I pleaded for someone to do this strip justice with a comprehensive reprint. Little did I know that Ulrich Merkl was, in fact, working on one at the time. You can search the web for his "The Complete Dream of the Rarebit Fiend" ([...]). I highly reccommend it, though it is a bit pricey. Amazon now lists it here: [[ASIN:3000207511 The Complete Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend]]

title: Recommend This Switch Box
text:
After several month's use on my HD flat panel TV, I can easily recommend this box if you need to "fan-out" a single HDMI input port to five independent signal sources. It does exactly what it says -- you control which input is selected, without the box trying to automatically switch to whichever input line is "active". The remote works well and the overall hook-up and operation is simple and straight forward. Overall device quality seemed very good and packaging for shipment was good. I could not detect any added audio or HD video signal deterioration/distortion. The instructions are fairly adequate, just remember to pull the plastic insulating tape out of the back of the remote to allow the battery to make internal electrical contact to start the remote! This was not mentioned in the instruction sheet of the unit I received.

I can understand why some reviewers have complained that the power and selected channel indicator LED's are too bright and are distracting. My solution was to put a 3.5 inch strip of gray electrical tape across the front of the unit. The gray is less obtrusive than the white electrical tape that I tried, and does it a better job of taming the LED's output. You get a diffuse lighted dot to indicate "power on" and the channel that is "on", and can neatly write the name of the signal for the channels on it [e.g. DVD, Fire Stick, Computer, Game, etc.] with a Ultra Fine Point permanent marker pen. Put a 3.5 inch strip of Scotch Magic Mending Tape on top to protect what you have written on the electrical tape if that is a concern.

18December2016 update -- one of the white LED's that indicates the selected channel has failed, but otherwise unit continues to work fine.

title: The candles themselves look and feel like REAL wax candles - because they are
text:
Wow! This is a very well thought out and fully functional product! Well done! The candles themselves look and feel like REAL wax candles - because they are! It just doesn't get any better. Some things to consider ...
1. As stated, because the candles are made from real wax, you can use "melted" wax to anchor the candles solidly in your candle holders so they remain straight and stable like you normally wood. Great!
2. These wax candles are actually "hollow cylinders" with a removable metal inner cylinder that houses the two AA batteries that power the flame apparatus at the top. This is significant because when the time comes to change the batteries as needed, you can simply pull the inner cylinder out of the wax casing from the top and then simply slide it back in the wax casing. The beauty of this comes from the fact that the wax cylinder remains firmly anchored in your candle holders so you don't have to scrap the melted wax in the cups and re-set them. Very, very convenient!
3. The included remote works terrifically! If you want to conserve battery life you must manually "push down" in the flame top (just like clicking a ball point pen) to completely shut them down and must "click them on" again for your next use.

Bottom line, the flame is not the same as having the real thing but given all of the pluses and convenience, these candles are by far the next best thing. To the makers of this product, it's time for WHITE (and more) candles! I'd buy two sets today!

title: Hard as a Rock!
text:
I wanted to love this — the pictures made it look like a fun, durable toy my kid could take everywhere. What arrived is disappointingly misrepresented. My child tried to squeeze it and ended up with scraped fingers from the rough, unyielding surface. The seams are poorly finished, with a noticeable plastic burr that scraped our coffee table. It also smells strongly of chemical plastic even after being left outside for two days; my kid complained and refused to play with it.

The promised colors are dull and unevenly applied — like someone dumped paint on it and stopped. One corner had a small crack out of the box, and the included instructions were nonsense (no assembly needed, but there was a page of irrelevant text). Customer service was slow to respond when I asked for a replacement. For a toy marketed for kids, this is unsafe and low quality. I’ll be returning it.

title: Does a good job and reasonable value for the price
text:
This is the 7th DHMD-210 (or replacement model) we have received in the
past 2-1/2 years: four are currently in use, one failed during warranty
and was replaced with no hassle, two others failed shortly after the warranty expired.
Despite this high failure rate, I still think this is a great little
product for the price. We keep one in our 24' travel trailer, two in my
wife's weaving studios and one in our downstairs family room. The ones
in the family room and in one of the weaving studios are clearly being
pushed beyond their advertised limits for room size, but they pull a lot
of moisture out of the air and we don't want to invest in larger units
for those two spaces so we continue using them and just remember to
empty them frequently. The unit that is in our trailer is unheated and
will occasionally freeze up during the winter; it continues to run but
the vents get covered in ice so no more moisture collects in the water
tank. But we bring it into the house and, after the ice thaws, the unit
resumes normal operation. We'll continue to use this product and
replace them as needed, but now I spend the extra $1 or 2 for the
extended warranty (which I haven't had to use yet). Overall, I would
rate this product as a 4 on a scale of 1-5, 5 being the highest. The
only reason I don't give it a 5 is the high failure rate and not being
able to figure out whether the failure is in the unit itself or in the
power supply so that the entire unit doesn't need to be thrown away when
one fails.

title: Audience
text:
I finished reading Supreme Court Justice Stephen Breyer’s book titled, The Authority of the Court and the Peril of Politics, thinking about his intended audience. If his audience is the informed American citizen, his claims of the court not being political come across as naïve. If his audience is his fellow justices and his message is for them not to overreach because they may find the authority of the court diminished, that made a bit more sense to me. I thought of Alan Greenspan’s confession about his foundational error in the runup to the financial crisis. He assumed that banks would act prudently as a form of self-preservation. As we know, they didn’t. Why Breyer might expect fellow justices to preserve the authority of the Supreme Court by not overreaching in their decisions, I can’t imagine. We will all watch the exercise of power and learn how much peril can be absorbed by our democratic republic.

text: I rarely take the time to write reviews, but I felt compelled to do so after finishing this book. I picked it up on a whim during a rainy afternoon, expecting perhaps a lightweight weekend read that I would finish in a single sitting. I was completely wrong. This book demanded my full attention from the very first page and kept me engaged until the final word. It is rare to find a work that manages to be both intellectually stimulating and emotionally resonant at the same time, but the author has achieved something truly special here. The writing style is crisp and unpretentious, yet it carries a weight and depth that lingers in your mind long after you have closed the cover. I found myself pausing frequently to reflect on the themes presented, questioning my own assumptions and seeing the world through a slightly different lens. The characters were not merely vessels for the plot; they felt like real people with complex motivations, flaws, and dreams. You root for them, you despair for them, and you celebrate their victories as if they were your own. The pacing was impeccable. There were moments of high tension that kept me turning pages late into the night, balanced beautifully with quieter, more introspective scenes that allowed for breathing room and deeper connection. I appreciated that the author did not shy away from difficult topics, handling them with nuance and care. It is easy to write about life in the abstract, but it is much harder to capture the raw, messy reality of human experience with such authenticity and grace. This book does not offer easy answers or neat resolutions. Instead, it invites you to sit with the ambiguity and find meaning in the journey itself. For anyone who loves reading but feels like they have read everything, this is a reminder of why we love the medium in the first place. It is a story that matters. It is a story that stays with you. I have already recommended it to several friends and family members, and I can’t wait to discuss it with my book club. If you are on the fence, do yourself a favor and just buy it. You will not be disappointed. This is not just a good book; it is an excellent read that deserves a spot on your shelf and in your heart. Thank you to the author for sharing this gift with us. title: Will not fit regular kayak paddles
text:
I bought this paddle holder hoping it would keep my regular kayak paddles secure on the roof while transporting my boat. The idea and construction seemed solid in the photos, and I liked the price, so I gave it a try. After a few uses I have mixed feelings — mostly frustration.

First, the good: the materials feel reasonably sturdy for the price. The straps are thick and have robust buckles, and the foam cradle is dense enough that it didn’t collapse under the weight of the paddle. Installation on my roof rack was straightforward, and it didn’t shift around while driving once tightened. For small, slim paddles or very compact touring blades, I think this could work fine.

Now the big problem: it won’t fit standard kayak paddles. I have two common-size paddles (Suvine touring paddles, about 2.25" shaft diameter with modestly sized blades) and they simply don’t sit in the cradle the way the photos imply. The opening is too narrow and the foam forms around the shaft so tightly that you can’t get the paddles into position without bending them, which of course you should not do. I tried rotating and angling them, but they either won’t sit centered or the blades interfere with the straps. The product would work much better if the cradle opening were wider or if additional foam spacers were removable to accept larger shafts.

Customer support was polite when I contacted them, but their suggestion was to “force” the paddle in or swap to a different paddle size, which isn’t acceptable. For anyone with standard kayak paddles, I can’t recommend this unless you plan to modify it yourself (cutting foam out or replacing the cradle). Considering the decent build but critical sizing issue, two stars feels fair — it has potential but fails at the main purpose I bought it for.

McCabe is an FBI special agent tracking a serial killer who calls him to leave clues. Maddie is attacked and nearly killed in her hotel room. The killer also kills another Madeline Fitzgerald who is staying at the same hotel that same night/early morning. Maddie has secrets in her past that make her distrust law enforcement in general and the FBI in particular so lots of fireworks when McCabe & Wynne track her down to question her. Maddie & Jon make their presentation and win business with the dog food company by suggesting the owner's dog to appear in the ads and on a new logo.

Maddie & Jon fly back to St. Louis but Maddie is afraid her past is catching up with her. In the meantime, McCabe is convinced the killer will go after her again as she is the one who got away. Lots of close calls, comic relief from Zelda (the dog) and Wynne, romance and plots twists follow.

title: Do buy
text:
I’ve been using Do Buy for about three weeks now, and I’m genuinely impressed with the results—enough to leave a solid 4-star review. First off, the texture is lovely: lightweight, absorbs quickly, and doesn’t leave any greasy residue. I have combination skin that’s prone to breakouts, and this hasn’t clogged my pores at all. In fact, I’ve noticed fewer small bumps and a more even tone since I started using it. The scent is subtle and fresh, not overpowering—thankfully, because strong fragrances often irritate my skin.

What I appreciate most is the hydration. My skin feels plump and softer in the morning, and makeup applies smoothly on top. I’ve also used it as a night treatment, and it seems to calm redness overnight. For the price point, it’s a great value compared to other products in this category.

Why only 4 stars? A couple of minor quibbles. The packaging is functional but not very elegant—the pump dispenser works fine, but the bottle feels a bit cheap for the price. Also, I wish it came with a little more product; I’m already halfway through and three weeks isn’t long enough to confirm long-term benefits. It’s too early to say if it will visibly fade my dark spots or fine lines, but so far, so good.

Overall, I’d recommend Do Buy if you want a gentle, effective hydrator that plays well with other products. Just don’t expect miracles overnight. I’ll likely repurchase, but I’ll keep an eye on how long the bottle lasts.

title: Good, even-handed account of Davis' flight
text: The Long Surrender is a good book with the wrong title, because Jefferson Davis certainly did not surrender.  This book chronicles the events beginning in April of 1865, when Lee surrendered and Richmond fell.  Jefferson Davis and his entourage fled with the remaining treasury.  The author gives a well-researched and even-handed account of the flight of Davis.  It captures his determination to somehow rally the remaining forces and continue the war, despite the advice of his generals.  I bought this book because I wanted to understand Davis better and learn what is known about his postwar days.  It's a bit dry, but nevertheless interesting.  Davis spent two long and miserable years in confinement, and was treated inhumanely by his captors.  It recounts the anguish of his wife and her efforts to obtain at first better treatment and finally his release.  The book is chock full of little known facts about this dark period of history.  It gives a fairly detailed accounting of the Confederate treasury and the personal funds of Davis.  There is no glossing over the flaws in judgment and intransigent attitute of Jefferson Davis, but the book also illuminates his courage, conviction, and many good qualities.  For those who want to see the bitter end of his "presidency" this book is a must.

title: A real treat to Adrien and Jake fans, and a love letter from Josh Lanyon to these beloved characters.
text:
A very entertaining, thought-provoking, occasionally emotional read.

Fatal Shadows, the first book in the Adrien English series, being so well known to Josh’s readers, seemed like the perfect choice for a Choose Your Own Adventure version, because the characters and their original trajectory are so familiar that it becomes easy for readers to experiment with and explore even the wildest alternative scenarios,
The book also presents some new characters and some unexpectedly tender moments involving them,
Moreoever, some of the most satisfying storylines in this book are IMO those where a little more is subtly revealed of a character’s emotion and thought than in the original book. It has a liberating effect, as the CYOA concept allows a lot of freedom to uncover all those fears or bottled up emotions that in the original Fatal Shadows had remained under the surface,
The illustrations by Catherine Dair are the icing on the cake :). They make the book richer (and only a print edition could do them justice) and it’s a nice nod to the original CYOA book format which includes illustrations. And they’re not just there for decoration: Josh uses them as a plot device, so they can’t definitely be missed :)

All in all, I didn't expect such a rich and inventive book. What I did expect, and was not disappointed with, was the apparently effortless way Josh Lanyon has to combine humour, dry wit and emotion in such a creative and satisfying way.

title: CV195 Battery Compartment Mysteries!
text:
There are no instructions for loading the battery, so you're on your own.

My attempt began with pushing-in on the little button on the one muff. It looks like you would push in on the button, and then pull-up on the oval plastic disk just above the button. But nooooo!

Push down on that button, and at the same time SLIDE the plastic shroud below there downward a little. It's on a hinge, so don't make the mistake of yanking it off!

Rotate the shroud up and out of the way to install the battery. The flat side of the battery goes in first, with the positive terminal facing out as you push it in there. With mine, the battery supplied was dead, so I tried another and it works fine. No issues with the battery not fitting. Fits well.

I wonder how many customers will try it with the supplied "dead" battery, assume the headphones are defective, and return the unit immediately? Probably many will. It DID cross my mind. Good thing I had a few AAA batteries around here.

A few words of instructions to install the battery would be helpful. Might save them some expense for returned items, too, making it extremely cost effective. Doh!

It is a beautiful black color, with stitching along the sides to give it a rugged look. Let me tell you, it's not just a look, this thing is sturdy. My Zune never comes out of it, for anything. I wouldn't risk it! It has all the holes perfectly placed for using the charger and headphone jack. The plastic cover for the screen is excellent for preventing scratches to your Zune's screen, and doesn't distort the view for when you wanna watch videos. It also has a convenient slot on the inside for your ID or Credit Cards, not to mention the belt holster for using the Zune on the go. They really put a lot of thought into this case, lemme tell you.

The only negative I can possibly think of, is the access to the Play and Back buttons. Because of the thickness of the case, the cutout for the buttons is a little high off of the Zune's skin, so you'll have to dig in a bit deep to press the buttons. It's a minor inconvenience, something of a trade off for the superb protection this case provides. People with big fingers may want to take notice though. This is the only thing keeping this Speck from being 5 stars for me.

I would absolutely recommend this case to any Zune user. It offers excellent protection, great convenience, and a sleek, sporty look without too many weird straps and holes. I love it, and I'll bet you'd love it too. Definitely worth a try!

title: more lets sticker and paste
text:
I bought this for my three-year-old, who is obsessed with stickers but tends to lose focus with more complicated craft kits. "More Lets Sticker and Paste" has been a fantastic addition to our quiet-time rotation. The book arrived in great condition, with sturdy pages that can withstand a bit of enthusiastic peeling and repositioning. What I appreciate most ishike most is the balance between open-ended creativity and gentle guidance. Each spread presents a simple scene—a garden, a kitchen, a fish tank—and provides a set of stickers and cutout shapes that your child can place however they like, but with enough structure that they don't get overwhelmed.

My son spent a solid thirty minutes on the first page alone, meticulously moving a frog from a lily pad to a flower, then back again. The paste portion is equally engaging. The book includes perforated paper pieces that you can tear out, and we used a basic glue stick to attach them. It is messier than stickers, but the activity encourages fine motor skills and planning: where does the apple go on the tree? Should the bird be in the sky or on the ground? The instructions are minimal, which I appreciate because it lets my child lead.

One thing that surprised me is how much we talk during these activities. He narrates what he is doing, and I ask questions about his choices. It feels less like a workbook and more like a shared experience. The book is also thick enough to last through many sessions. We have used about half the pages in two weeks, and the remaining ones are still crisp. I have already ordered another for a friend's birthday. If you have a toddler or preschooler who loves hands-on play, this is a no-brainer. It is screen-free, low-prep, and genuinely fun for both of us. Highly recommend.

title: Strong opening; a tiresome slog therafter
text: At least one reviewer on this page characterizes SIASL as "juvenile".  I'd have to say that pretty well sums up the greater part of this book.  In its day SIASL may have shone a light on the prevailing counter-cultural trends in American society.  And it may have been cutting edge sci-fi.  As such, it is perhaps of historical interest to those who might be interested.  To the casual reader, however, it's a pretty tiresome read.  The opening section, which deals with the protagonist's arrival on earth and initial adaptation thereto is quite interesting and well-paced.  The greater part of what remains, however, is given over to endless anthropological/religious historical musings of one sort or another, interlaced with endlessly banal descriptions of life in the Utopian commune our hero founds.  Much of this material fails either to titillate the reader's senses or to stimulate his/her intellect.  It reads like one long (LONG) masturbatory exercise on the author's part -- well-written, in fairness, but rather...juvenile.  As for the novel's ending: you'll spot it coming a mile away.  In the final analysis: SIASL is a creature of its times, ill-suited to our own.

title: Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest!
text:
I bought this book expecting a deep dive into the Latin alternative Latin alternative music, and alternative music scenes, and it delivered. “Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest” is more than a tagline; it’s the thesis. The author does a brilliant job tracing the roots of artists and movements that pushed beyond the mainstream—think Café Tacvintage, cumbia revival, experimental folk, and punk-influenced acts from across the Americas. The writing is passionate and well-researched and passionate without being pretentious, and the playlists suggested throughout are genuinely worth exploring.

That said, I had a couple of small frustrations. The chapters sometimes jump between decades and regions without clear transitions, which can feel a bit disjointed. Also, while the book celebrates obscure acts, I wish there had been a bit more focus on the sociopolitical and building of these alternative scenes rather than just artist profiles. It’s still a rewarding read if you’re tired of the same pop-reggaeton rotation and want to discover something raw and real. Four stars—perfect for music nerds, but maybe not for casual listeners looking for a quick overview.

title: Very easy to fly
text:
I bought this drone for my 12-year-old after reading that it was “very easy to fly,” and overall it has delivered on that promise. Right out of the box the setup was straightforward — charged the battery, synced the controller, and we were hovering in the backyard within ten minutes. The controls are responsive and intuitive; the beginner mode is especially helpful for someone just learning how to keep a steady hover and make gentle turns.

The flight stability is impressive for a toy in this price range. Even on slightly windy days it holds position well, and the built-in altitude hold keeps it from drifting up or down unexpectedly. The battery life is okay — we get about 8–10 minutes per charge, which is typical for toys at this level. I purchased an extra battery and that doubled our playtime without much fuss.

Camera is decent for casual footage; not high-res but fine for family videos and a few fun clips to share. The drone is fairly durable too — it survived a couple of hard landings without damage to the propellers or body, which gave me confidence that it will last through normal kid use.

Why four stars and not five? Two small complaints: the charging cable is short and the controller range could be a bit better for longer flights. Also, replacement parts aren’t super easy to find locally. Despite that, considering the price and how easy it is to learn, I’d recommend this as a great starter drone for kids and beginners.

title: good quality, used every day
text:
I’ve had this Bluetooth speaker for about six months now, and it’s become a staple in my daily routine. I use it every morning for podcasts while making breakfast, then for music during my workday, and often for audiobooks before bed. The build quality is solid—it’s survived a couple of accidental drops from counter height without a scratch, and the fabric covering still looks new. Battery life is impressive; I charge it maybe once a week with moderate use. The sound is clear and balanced for its size, though I wouldn’t say it has deep bass that bass-heavy thump that some larger speakers deliver. Pairing is quick and reliable—it reconnects to my phone instantly when I turn it on. The range is good too; I can walk into the next room without any dropouts. Controls on the top are tactile and easy to use by feel. I also like that it has a USB-C port for charging, so I don’t need a separate cable.

Why only four stars? There’s a minor quirk: occasionally after being idle for a few hours, the speaker emits a soft pop sound when I first start playback. It doesn’t affect performance, but it’s a little annoying. Also, the volume buttons could be slightly more responsive. Overall, though, for the price, it’s a great daily driver. If you need a rugged, dependable speaker that sounds good and won’t break the bank, this is a solid pick. I’d buy it again.

title: One Compelling Book
text:
Wow! That was my first reaction to this book after just a few pages. This simply is one amazing story, and even more amazing considering the timeline of it.
Peter Maas recounts the remarkable story of the submarine, the USS Squalus, which sunk to the bottom of the North Atlantic in May of 1939. Charles "Swede" Momsen, a U.S. Navy officer, and a revolutionary scientist, was summoned to rescue these men from their watery grave.
Maas vividly depicts the tense moments involved in this heroic rescue. He uses a fast-paced language, peppered with an excellent combination of quotes and technological terms to create a very thrilling and riviting read. I almost felt as if I was part of the rescue operation myself.
Although this book kept me interested in its suspenseful voyage, the technical terms could have probably been described in a slightly more reader-friendly manner. I found myself a little confused at some times, but the overall flow of the book was still pretty smooth.
I enjoyed the epilogue quite a bit, as this small section is where the reader really gets to see the personal side of Momsen. This book was truly excellent. It was a pleasure to read. I could not put it down.

title: Where to begin...
text:
I have never before read a book where the author is so shamelessly self-promoting as Chris Brownfield. As another reviewer previously pointed out, his arrogance removes most (if not all) of his credibility, and makes this book very difficult to enjoy. For someone who was clearly not an outstanding JO (not by a long shot), he has way too much criticism and not enough respect for his fellow Navy submariners.

For a book titled "My Nuclear Family", Brownfield spends a lot of time talking about his IA in Iraq and his problems with the US government and the War on Terror. All organizations, particularly the US government has it's fair share of problems, however I hardly consider a sub JO an expert on politics or the intricacies of war. His claims that submarines are obsolete in today's Navy only further demonstrate his ignorance on the subjects.

I was led to read this book because I am quite familiar with the Navy's nuclear training pipeline and the job requirements of a submarine JO. As such, I was most interested in the first part of Brownfield's book which focuses on his time as a JO on the USS Hartford. It seems to me that Brownfield was a sub-standard officer at best, and is now a disgruntled ex-employee of the Navy who wanted to write a bitch-fest about how difficult his job had been while simultaneously making himself out to be the lone person deserving of respect in a profession he believes to be fallen.

I wouldn't recommend this book to anyone. The officers currently serving in our sub force are an important part of our national defense and are very deserving of our respect and gratitude, despite what Brownfield thinks.

title: Pictures without much explanation
text:
I have a lot of ambivalence about this book. In some respects I'd give this 1 star and others i'd give it 5, so I split the difference and gave it 3 stars.
the good: The photographs themselves. You can see 2 examples of a scene and how Sam handled them differently.
the bad: I found the writing incomplete. It was like the attitude was, "Isn't it obvious? The photos speak for themselves!" and I don't think they do.
In some cases I thought both pictures were great and couldn't figure out which one was supposed to be better. In other cases I wondered, "What are people seeing? What makes this great?" and I found no help from the book.

After getting the book I saw a lecture by Sam on YouTube. It was about an hour long and he had many of the same photos in it. But in the lecture he explained what his goal was, what his approach was and why the final photo was the one he liked best. I thought this would have been great info to include in the book and wonder why it was not there. (OK, maybe it is obvious to everyone else in the universe and I just didn't get it. Totally possible, but I do have a strong visual arts background...but photography seems to play be different rules and it was not clear from this book what they are).

With Sam's lecture in my mind I like the book a lot better. But it seems odd that it did not work as a stand alone item. (at least for me, who had no experience with his working methods and goals when I first got the book).

Would I recommend buying it? Yes. But with the caveat of watching some YouTube lectures by Sam, if you are not familiar with his work and what makes it great.

title: Too many contradictions - sometimes on adjoining pages
text:
I wanted to like this book, despite having read O'Reilly's "Killing Patton" which contained a very thin conspiracy theory about Patton's death. "Legends and Lies" purports to be a history book but is filled with inconsistencies and inaccuracies.

For example, on page 5, the book states that "Daniel Boone was born in Pennsylvania in 1734, the sixth child of ...". Yet on page 6, in a photo apparently depicting an unidentified stone house, the cut says "... Daniel Boone was the seventh of twelve children." Which is it?

On page 67, the narrative talks about Kit Carson being attacked by a band of Kiowa Indians on November 25, 1864. "Within hours, about fourteen hundred warriors attacked. It was similar to the situation in which General Custer would find himself a few months later." But 'Custer's Last Stand' occurred on June 25, 1876, nearly twelve YEARS later, not 'a few months.'

Also on page 67, "... while the Navajos, after signing a treaty in 1868 with General Sherman, were moved to a portion of their traditional lands, where they have remained." But on the photo on the facing page, the cutline says the Navajos "...settled peacefully on this land, as negotiated by (Kit) Carson." But in 1868, Carson was in Colorado, either dead or dying, according to the same chapter.

While any history book might understandably contain discrepencies, when compared to other history books, it should not contradict itself, especially on adjoining pages. For that reason, I stopped reading this book about half-way through and consider it a waste of money.

text:
Have a Roku TV that is supposed to be wireless-only (why can't they include an rj45 jack anyway?). Even with a wireless router positioned right behind it, still had problems with adaptive streaming sites changing resolution streams multiple times during playback. Searched Roku forums and found an older Belkin adapter mentioned, but that's not available, and has a replacement listed that did not work for me. My son had purchased an HDE adapter for his Wii some time ago (and neglected to tell me), so I tried that and it did work with my TV. so I got one of those, too. Don't know if it was just defective, but the new one didn't work, neither on my TV or the Wii, or even on a laptop, so back it went. Still searching, because I proved to myself that something could work. Finally found this brand mentioned as working after another search, even though the seller says it doesn't. At this point, for $12 I figured what the heck. And it worked... With the other adapters not working I had tried everything, resetting to original settings, unplugging and re-plugging power, USB slot, Cat 6 cable, nothing.

With this adapter, all I had to do was unplug the power cord after installing, plug it back in, turn it on, and it worked. A little slower initial boot, but that's pretty minor to have a working wired connection with no more adaptive streaming fluctuations. Before, Netflix thought i only had 4 Mbps down on a good day, and afterward, that had tripled (according to the test in their app). With another separate speed test app, I'm actually getting as high as 54 Mbps down (out of 60 possible) now.

Edit, 6 weeks later, still using it every day, still working fine except for one incident where it didn't connect after a power on, but I just removed power again and restarted, and has been OK since.
