title: bought with Zob figurine
text:
I decided to pick this up because I already had the Zob figurine and thought it would make a nice addition to my growing collection of decorative items. To be honest, I wasn’t entirely sure what to expect at first. The product description was a bit vague, so I had to do some digging online to understand the context better. Once I figured it out, I realized it was actually quite charming and fit perfectly with the existing Zob display I had on my bookshelf.

The build quality is decent for the price point. The materials feel sturdy enough for indoor display, and the detailing is surprisingly sharp. I appreciate that they didn’t skimp on the paint job; the colors are vibrant but not garish, which helps it blend well with other items in my collection. It’s clearly designed to be a visual centerpiece, and it certainly draws attention when guests visit.

However, I’m giving it four stars instead of five because the packaging was a bit lackluster. The box arrived slightly dented, which made me nervous about the condition of the item inside. Fortunately, the figurine itself was fine, but for a gift or a fragile collectible, better protective packaging would be appreciated. Also, the base is a little light, so if you have cats or little kids running around, you might want to secure it to a surface to prevent accidental tip-overs.

Overall, I am satisfied with this purchase. It serves its purpose well and enhances the display of the Zob figure I already owned. It’s a solid addition to any themed shelf or desk setup. I would recommend it to other fans of the Zob character who are looking to expand their collection without breaking the bank. Just be careful when unboxing, and maybe consider adding some weight to the base if you plan to put it in a high-traffic area. It’s a good value for money, and I plan to look for more accessories to go with it in the future.

text:
I bought these faux eucalyptus stems to add some greenery to my living room without the upkeep of real plants, and they have exceeded my expectations. I appreciate that they’re flexible enough to bend slightly to get the exact silhouette I wanted, yet sturdy enough to stay in place. The wire inside the stems feels durable; after repositioning them a few times they still retained their position.

Quality feels far better than other faux stems I’ve purchased in the past. There were no strong chemical smells when I unpacked them, and the leaves don’t shed. They’re easy to clean too — a quick dusting or a gentle wipe with a damp cloth keeps them looking fresh. I also used a couple of smaller stems in a bathroom arrangement and they held up fine in a humid environment.

Overall, these faux eucalyptus stems are a great, low-maintenance way to bring a calming, modern touch to any room. They look expensive without the price tag, and they’ve attracted compliments from guests. If you want realistic-looking faux greenery that’s versatile and durable, I’d highly recommend these. title: Terrific light for video
text:
I have been using Neewer products for over 5 years. My first purchase was a cheap fluorescent ring light in early 2017 and have seen considerable improvement in both the variety and quality of products they offer while remaining reasonably priced. I have purchased several lights, a camera slider, tripod dolly, lens filters, etc. and everything has lived up to my expectations and I still use all of it. Nothing has ever broken or stopped working.

This light comes with the light unit, a mounting bracket to attach it to a light stand, a DC power converter, a power cord, a soft carrying case with plenty of foam padding, and an instruction manual.
It took only a couple of minutes to set up right out of the box. It was also easy to install the app on my phone and connect with the light via Bluetooth. The app allows the light to be controlled remotely and is intuitive and easy to use.

I tested this light this morning and plan on using it to light a video this evening. I had no problem using the Android app to control the brightness, color temperature, and effects. It can also be controlled manually via the knobs and buttons on the back of the unit. I tried using the Sony NP-F-style batteries (it holds 2) and the AC power. Each worked equally well though I would want more than one set of batteries if I were using them for a shoot. On the brightest setting, the light is quite bright and could be used as a key light. It can be dimmed for use as a fill or backlight. However, because it is a panel of lights, it cannot be used as a focused spotlight. The panel cover is a diffuser that softens the light considerably. It is built-in and not removable.

Overall I would say this is a terrific light and worth the price. Easily 5 stars.

title: User-Friendly Design, But Tricky Connection
text:
The BEST feature here is the dedicated buttons for each function, as opposed to the “rocker” style most of these remotes have. Also, these buttons are silent (unlike some of the others which sound like clickers!)

Unfortunately, this unit has one thing to BEWARE of. While the Manual directions are very clear about how to pair the Movo with your phone or other device, you get NO INSTRUCTIONS WHATSOEVER regarding connection/regular usage! This is unfortunate since making a Bluetooth connection is QUITE TRICKY.

HERE IS HOW TO CONNECT THIS REMOTE TO USE IT (this assumes you have already paired it up with your phone as per the directions): 1. Don’t even bother to open Settings; 2. Simply hold down the red Power button—BUT KEEP HOLDING IT DOWN until it turns first RED, then it FLASHES GREEN, then it becomes SOLID GREEN, then finally turns RED again. 3. RELEASE the Power button just as the light turns RED again!

This is the ONLY WAY I have found that works every time, and it is fairly easy. FAIRLY easy! Practice it a couple of times if you are having trouble with the connection.

Also, be sure to TURN THE POWER OFF when you’re finished using the Movo by holding the Power button down awhile—until the light turns red and then goes out! This will save battery life.

Once you get the hang of using the Power button, I think you will find this remote is a good one.

Performance-wise, it handles my daily tasks with ease: web browsing, streaming, Microsoft Office, even light photo editing. Port selection is decent, with USB-C, USB-A, and HDMI, so I didn’t need a dongle for my external monitor and mouse. Fan noise is minimal; the laptop runs cool even under sustained load.

Is it a high-end gaming rig or a workstation? No. But as a reliable daily driver for productivity, school, or casual entertainment, it’s an excellent value. If you need a functional, no-frills laptop that feels more expensive than it is, I highly recommend giving this one a shot.

The biotopte profiles are in-depth enough, but I feel Hiscock could have better explained how to actually assemble some of the tank features--namely the Chinese Stream waterfall. title: Cat Scratching Post
text:
I bought this scratching post three months ago after my two indoor cats had almost shredded the armrests of my couch. I did a lot of searching for something sturdy, attractive enough to keep in the living room, and tall enough for them to fully stretch — this fit the bill perfectly.

Right out of the box assembly was quick and intuitive: two pieces snapped together and the base slides firmly into place. No tools required and the whole thing felt solid, not wobbly like some cheaper posts I’ve had. The surface is tightly wound sisal that resists fraying and seems to hold up well to daily use. Both of my cats prefer it over the old cardboard scratchers; I catch them using it multiple times a day, and the couch has been untouched for weeks.

The height is great for a full stretch and the diameter gives them a good grip without feeling flimsy. The base is weighted enough to prevent tipping, even when my bigger cat gives it an enthusiastic vertical clawing session. Cleaning is simple — vacuuming around the base removes loose fibers and occasional fur, and the material has not developed any unpleasant odor.

A couple of small points to note: one corner of the base upholstery started to peel slightly after heavy use, but it’s cosmetic and hasn’t affected functionality. Also, it’s not meant to be a cat tree replacement — there’s no platform to nap on — but that’s exactly what I wanted: a dedicated, effective scratching post.

Overall this is a well-made, effective scratching post that saved my furniture and that my cats clearly enjoy. I would buy it again and recommend it to any cat owner looking for a reliable, no-nonsense solution.

title: Love this game!
text:
I bought this game on a whim after seeing it recommended, and it has quickly become our go-to for family game nights. What I appreciate most is the balance between strategy and luck. Younger players (my 8-year-old and 10-year-old) can grasp the basics right away and still feel like they have a real chance to win, while the adults enjoy the tactical choices that keep the game engaging round after round. Playtime is just right — long enough to feel satisfying, short enough to play multiple times in an evening or as a quick filler between other activities.

The replay value is excellent. There’s enough variety in the cards and scenarios that no two games feel identical, and the pacing keeps everyone involved. We’ve used it for casual family time, as a way to entertain visiting friends, and even for a low-pressure activity during a rainy afternoon. Cleanup is straightforward, and the box stores neatly on our shelf.

Minor quibble: a few components are a bit snug in the insert, but that’s a small trade-off for the overall quality. If you’re looking for a well-designed, fun game that’s accessible to a wide age range and delivers consistently entertaining sessions, I highly recommend this one. We’re already planning to bring it to our next game night.

title: I stayed up until 1:37 AM to finish this book
text:
I am not usually one to lose sleep over a paperback, but I found myself completely unable to put this book down last night. I had every intention of reading for thirty minutes before bed, but suddenly it was 1:37 AM, and I had reached the final chapter. That is when I know a book has truly succeeded in its mission to captivate the reader.

From the very first page, the narrative hook was undeniable. The author has a unique ability to weave complex characters into a plot that feels both urgent and intimately personal. I found myself relating deeply to the protagonist’s internal struggles, which are portrayed with such raw honesty that it felt like reading a diary entry rather than a novel. The pacing is relentless, yet never feels rushed. There are moments of quiet reflection that provide necessary breathing room, but the underlying tension never dissipates. It pulls you forward, chapter by chapter, with a momentum that makes putting the book down feel like a betrayal.

The prose itself is stunning. This isn’t just a story; it’s an experience. The descriptions are vivid without being overly verbose, allowing the imagination to fill in the gaps with crisp, clear imagery. I appreciated how the secondary characters were given distinct voices and motivations, avoiding the trap of becoming mere plot devices. They felt like real people with their own lives and agendas, which added layers of complexity to the main storyline.

What impressed me most, however, was the emotional payoff. I won’t spoil anything, but let’s just say the ending was both satisfying and heartbreaking. It stayed with me long after I closed the cover, prompting me to spend the next hour staring at the ceiling, processing the themes of loss and redemption. It’s rare to find a book that lingers in your mind days later, forcing you to re-evaluate your own perspectives.

For anyone on the fence, do yourself a favor and buy this copy. Whether you are a devoted fan of literary fiction or just looking for a gripping page-turner, this book delivers on all fronts. It is a masterclass in storytelling that respects the reader’s intelligence while delivering pure entertainment. I have already ordered a second copy as a gift for a friend who I know will have the same sleepless night I did. Five stars is not enough; if there were an option for six, I would choose it. This is that rare gem that reminds you why you fell in love with reading in the first place.

title: A page turner, but dissapointing
text:
With her ususal excellent style and story telling skills, Ruth Rendell introduces us to a petty criminal and the effect he has on several of his victoms--lonely, vulnerable women. Somewhere in the middle of the novel, by an unfortunate (or fortunate) coincidence he meets his death in a moveie theater by the hand of a former victim. The second part is dedicated to the effect this deathhas on his victims. As usual in Rendell's novels, we are exposed to her much praised talent to draw in fine psycological detail her charcaters. Because of that, Rendell's novels carry some form of social significance that take them beyond the mystery level. And as usual, this book is a page turner.
However, in this particular novel, she has too many characters and, respectively, too many social issues/implications going on that do not always come together as planned. We have a gay MP that is relevied when he is forced to come out (social responsibiltry vs. personal freedom), his wife who is not necessarily a bad mother to her kids, but still really dumb (feminist ideas vs. traditional upbringing dilemmas); a couple with opposite eating disorders that somehow get cured abd their relationship with their friend who unvoluntarily implcates them in a crime (friednship and betrayal); and all of the above are not related too much to the mystery. I just felt that she has tried to put everything into a single book leaving a lot of the questions she raises unresolved...

Well, after 5 days of exploring, tumbling, game-playing, etc with kids ages 5-11, I'd say this was excellent value for my money. I only used the included cards for certain ones, since we color-coded the name tags for identifiability, but the card stock which is included, is of a really good quality. I have passed them on to our missions team, and they will use them!

Did they all make it thorough the 5 days? No. About 5 of the lanyards broke, but we just knot-tied them, and they were good to go. The rest made it through.

So if you are looking for an inexpensive option, that can withstand some rough and tumble, this is for you.

Edit: After I wrote this review, I spent an office day going through all my VBS supplies, and feel that I need to amend my review to reflect the following.
I had gone through the badges before, and they appeared to be in good shape. On closer examination, I found that almost all of them had been tied with a knot. So I guess that although as a whole, they lasted for the five days, and withstood, as I said, a LOT of rough and tumble, I have very few that I will in good conscience use next year. I will reuse some, but only as backups.

So, If you're not using them for children, and don't particularly care if you get to reuse them, it's still value for money.

I still feel that the value may have been lost to me, due to the fact that I will definitely have to buy more next year, I did save a significant amount during THIS budget period.

Beyond its practical features, the aesthetic appeal of the calendar brings a sense of joy to my daily routine. I’ve already recommended it to several friends who have recently become parents, and I plan to buy another one as a gift for our upcoming baby shower. If you are looking for a meaningful way to document your journey into motherhood, I cannot recommend this product highly enough. title: Mixed Emotions
text:
A dark and foreboding novel of a thousands years ago -- the coldness of the climate and the land accentuated by the lack of the sun's light -- although it teasingly seems to appear on the horizon to prematurely announce its impending return.

"The Wolf in the Whale" is populated by ancient, mysterious, powerful and hardy people - Norsemen and women living, fighting and dying in a new world. The whole novel brings with it a sense of perpetual cold and darkness.

The spirits seem to reign in this book -- they talk to the shamans young and old, and bestow upon them certain powers as the situations deem -- The chief protagonists are a young girl and her older brother, who use their wits to survive -- and who are transmuted back and forth to animal spirits and back again to human.

The narrative is excellent - one can feel the harsh living conditions and can be caught up in the spirit world that revolves around each person like a whirlpool of snow and cold air. The veil between the spirit, animal and human world is very thin indeed.

However, I felt that the book dragged on for too long -- and after a while this reader began to feel mired down in spots, as if walking thru a powdery snow capped with thin ice - very slow going.

So although "The Wolf in the Whale" transported me quite well, back to an era where the spirits and animals spoke with and transferred powers on primitive warrior humans fighting to survive in a cold and forbidding land - it was a wearying journey for me, as it was, IMHO, far too long.

In this case, I have to reach out to customer service, fill out forms, and wait for instructions. Why should the customer bear the inconvenience of a poorly packaged product? It makes me question if the warehouse team even cares about what they are sending out. I really wanted to give this five stars because the story itself seems incredible based on the first few chapters I managed to read before the binding refused to lay flat. But you cannot enjoy a book when you are constantly worried about damaging it further. The frustration of dealing with returns overshadows any enjoyment of the content itself. I hope the next reader has better luck, but for me, this was a letdown. I would prefer to see better packaging standards enforced before shipping items out. Do not expect the pristine condition advertised on the main product page if you order from this seller. title: Love it--a really fun read!
text:
I try really hard to not rehash the entire story or give a bunch of spoilers when I review a book, but it may be hard not to this time! I'll do my best, though. ;)

I received this book to rebiew from the Shut Up & Read group's Read It & Reap event. I have to say, I have been extremely fortunate in the books I've been given to review through them so far. There really haven't been any misses. :)

Anyway, about this book...

I admit it--halfway into the very first chapter I was convinced I was going to hate this book. Liora seemed like the typical, overly-angsty teenager often depicted in paranormal fantasy these days. I initially found her constant whiny and hating herself grating. All I can say is I'm so happy I read chapter 2!

Lucky kicks ass! There's really no other way to describe her. The demon half of Liora who takes over at night, separated from Liora by a curse, she is angry, obviously. And that anger is often turned toward Liora, her fully human side. She is also strong, practical, loyal to her friends, and more willing to look into herself and face the things that make her uncomfortable that she admits. And as time went by, I found Liora to be less annoying as she found her own strength and started to face her own inner "demons".

There are only a couple of things that prevented me from giving this book five stars. The first is that I felt like the romance between Keiran and Liora/Lucky felt too conveniently done to me. There didn't seem to be any build up to it at all. The second issue is that conversations sometimes felt stilted to me. While I appreciate that there was a distinct lack of inappropriate idioms throughout, the almost complete lack of contractions often made discussions feel too formal and unnatural.

This book had everything--romance, fear, growth, drama, excitement, sadness, and victory. It was a great story and I can't wait to read the next one!

It is also quiet enough that it does not wake me up in the morning, a common issue with other noisy toys. I have recommended this to all my friends with cats. I really wanted to love this product. The fragrance is absolutely incredible—truly beautiful—a sophisticated, warm, and slightly floral scent that lingers on the skin for hours. It is not color treated or oily or dry. This shampoo leaves my hair feeling like straw. It does not lather well, even with a generous amount. You have to use twice as much as a normal shampoo to feel like you are actually cleaning your scalp. Even then, my hair feels like there is still a weird residue, almost like a waxy coating. After I rinse and condition with my usual conditioner, my hair is tangled and rough. By the time it dries, it is frizzy, dull, and without any movement. It actually looks worse than before I washed it. I tried using it only once a week to see if my hair would adjust, but no change.

I also noticed that my scalp feels tight and itchy after using this. Not immediately, but a few hours later. I thought maybe I was imagining it, but after the fourth try, I had to stop. I have since used it only as a hand wash and body wash in the guest bathroom, which is a shame because I cannot bring myself to throw away a full bottle that cost this much. As a hand soap, it is fine. The scent is lovely on my hands, and it does not dry out my hands the way it does my scalp.

If this product is the ultimate disappointment. A beautiful fragrance trapped in a formula that simply does not work for washing your hair. If the company sold this as a perfume only, I would buy it in a second. But as a shampoo, it is a waste of money. I cannot recommend it for actual hair washing unless you want to follow up with a bad hair day every time. Two stars for the scent, zero stars for performance. Buyer beware.

For the money, this is a good product. It does what it supposed to do without any major issues. If you can live with the average battery life and a slightly clunky app, you will probably be happy. text:
I bought this desk mat a few months ago to protect my home office desk from spills, scratches, and the daily onslaught of coffee cups and markers. Cleaning is incredibly easy; a damp cloth removes most marks, and when I needed a deeper clean, the machine wash didn’t hurt it at all (I used a gentle cycle and low spin). It’s comfortable to rest my wrists on for long typing sessions and adds a clean, professional look to my desk space.

If you work from home or just need a reliable mat that can stand up to real life (and accidental washing), this one is a great buy. Durable, functional, and easy to clean — I’d buy it again.

title: Something of a Find
text:
I'm very happy with this cart, and two reasons stand out: its sturdiness and its size.

It's a very clever design, and the parts are of high quality. The result is a rigid structure that's perfect for applications like mine: support for a wide-carriage "pro" printer that can be placed on the top shelf without the somewhat massive printhead action causing side-to-side sway.

The size is a difficult one to find elsewhere. In my case I needed to replace a cheap TV cart made of low-density fiberboard and formica. I was using it to support not only the aforementoned wide printer on top but also a laser printer and scanner on the lower shelf. Any replacement would have to be almost the same size because of my office setup. I was ready to give up -- most shelving/carts like these are dimensioned in multiples of 12 inches -- but then I found this guy (the 16x28). Perfect! A little taller than the crumbling TV cart, but that's OK. I gained a third shelf for supplies that previously lived on the carpet under the cart.

One problem (for me): Carts like these have no sides onto which you can stick things -- in my case USB hubs. The solution was fairly simple: pegboard material cut to size, held in place with toggle bolts (with shortened screws).

One caution: unlike wood shelf units, which typically have uniform shelf width front to back, carts like these have tubing at the four corners that you might need to take into account. If your printer, for example, is a tight fit on one of the lower shelves, it might fit fine and work fine but not allow you to pull out the paper supply drawer if you can't skooch it over. The inner post-clearing distances for the shelves in this case is about 25.5 inches (left-to-right as pictured) and about 13.5 inches (front-to-back as pictured).

Regarding ease of assembly... Yes, the instructions are terse, but it's not rocket science. If you have a third-grader in the house, you should be fine.

All in all, a very satisfactory purchase and a good value.

title: My Fugoo Didn't Last 3 Months -- Buyer Beware
text:
Save your receipt if you decide to risk the asking price.

I am giving a 2 stars review because the speaker worked well while it lasted, which wasn't for very long. After approximately 3 months of gentle use, my Tough Fugoo started performing erratically.

Initially, the build quality appeared (?) to be very good, I liked that the speaker was relatively heavy with a good solid feel. Battery life performed as advertised, and sound quality, which is the reason I purchased the speaker, was better than any of the competition I had sampled, and the volume was more than adequate for a speaker of this size.

The problem I experienced is the Bluetooth mode turning off and on for no reason. Initially this would occur once or twice, and then it would play without any problems for the rest of the time it was used. Approximately one week after the problem started, it worsened, and became very frustrating. I tried resetting the speaker, and I also reloaded or re-installed the firmware, but no change.

I really thought I purchased the best mini-Bluetooth speaker out there. And never came even close to putting the Tough speaker to the test, as I had always treated it gently. It died and crapped-out all on it's own design and build quality.

When I contacted Fugoo via email, they returned a response within a few hours. I explained the problem, and was informed that I needed to replace the speaker unit. They requested proof that I purchased from an authorized dealer, and proof of date of purchase to show proof speaker was within the warranty period (12 months). Not the best way to treat a customer, especially considering the product line itself is less than the warranty period.

After I provided the requested information, I was informed that it would take 2 to 3 weeks and that I would be sent an RMA number. This was just over a 1 week ago, and I'm still waiting for the RMA number. No mention on how long I'd have to wait for an RMA, hopefully not an additional 2 to 3 weeks.

I anticipate getting a refurbished unit that crapped out on someone else. I won't be too happy about that, as mine was practically brand new, and pampered. Someday after I get the replacement, I'll do a follow up.

My other two cats loved it too, which is rare because the grazer often ignores new foods.

I’ve been using it as a topper on her regular kibble and sometimes as a standalone meal. Her coat looks shinier, and there’s been no upset stomach, which I’ve dealt with before when switching foods. If you have a feline food critic at home, give this a shot. It’s the first product in years that has passed the picky test in my house. Highly recommend.

title: Great sprinkler for little kids!
text:
I bought this sprinkler for my three-year-old son, and it has been the highlight of our backyard all summer. I was initially skeptical because some kids' sprinklers are either too complicated to set up or don't put out enough water to be fun. This one is the opposite. It arrived quickly, and I had it connected it to our garden hose in under a minute. No tools needed no tools, no stakes to push into the ground. The base is wide and flat, so it stays put even when my son runs right over it.

The design is perfect for little kids. It has two soft, flexible arms that spin around, and the water sprays out in a gentle, wide arc—not a harsh jet that would hurt a toddler's face. My son loves to chase the spinning arms and jump over the low spray. It keeps him entertained for hours, and I appreciate that I don't have to constantly adjust the water pressure or re-position it. It covers a nice circular area, so there is plenty of room for him to run around without getting bored.

Durability has been great so far. It has been left out in the sun, stepped on, and dragged across the patio by an excited preschooler. The plastic feels thick and shows no cracks, and the hose connector hasn't leaked. It also drains completely when I turn off the water, which means no standing water left to attract mosquitoes or leave puddles on the grass. That was a huge selling point for me.

Another feature I love is that it comes in bright, cheerful colors that appeal to children. My son picked his favorite color from the options, and he gets so excited when we bring it out. It is also lightweight enough for him to carry around the yard himself, which gives him a sense of ownership. I have already recommended it to two neighbors with toddlers.

If you have a child between the ages of two and six who loves water play, this sprinkler is a no-brainer. It is safe, easy to use, and provides endless outdoor fun without breaking the bank. I plan to buy a second one as a birthday gift for a friend's child. Highly recommended for any parent looking to make summer afternoons more magical.

Once I finally got the mirror mounted, it vibrates constantly on rough pavement, making the reflection useless. The so-called "anti-glare coating" smudges if you look at it wrong. I reached out to customer service about the missing hardware for the secondary mount, and they responded with a generic link to a PDF that didn't match the parts I received. For the price, I expected outcome, this product is frustrating. It might work on a stationary bike or a perfectly smooth road, but for actual outdoor riding, skip it. title: First impressions from a first-time Hardshell user
text:
I've used Gatorskins for years, riding my Specialized Tarmac SL2 in the hills surrounding the San Francisco Bay Area. The shoulders of these near-urban backroads tend to be strewn with debris and there's plenty of shattered glass remnants from long-ago broken bottles. (No street sweepers set foot on these roads!)

Even though I've got a fancy lightweight racebike, I put up with the added rolling weight of Conti's Gatorskins because when I used to ride with "racing" clinchers, I'd get two or three flats a month. And I hate fixing flats! Spoils the rhythm of my ride!

My last set of Gatorskins lasted two seasons. This time, when ordering replacements, I opted for the "Hardshell" version. And let me tell you, there's a difference in the riding experience. The hardshell component is a thick layer of solid rubber over the middle of the tire. When inflated at the recommended pressure (110 psi), I'm feeling every bump and pebble I ride over quite a bit more than was my experience with regular Gatorskins. My sense is that the thick rubber in the center is reducing the bump-absorbing effects that make pneumatic tires essential on most vehicles.

No doubt as these Hardshells tires wear, the ride will become less stiff. And I wouldn't be surprised if all that extra rubber gave me an extra season's life from my set of tires. But I've got to say, I miss the shock absorbtion of my regular Gatorskins. When the time comes to replace these Hardshells, I'll probably go back to the non-Hardshell Gators. They gave me all the flat protection I needed and provided a comfy ride as well.

title: Didn't last longer than a month but customer service saved it
text:
I was really excited when I unboxed these wireless earbuds. The sound quality was crisp, the fit was comfortable, and the battery life actually matched the advertised claims for the first few weeks. I used them daily during my commute and at the gym, and they performed exactly as I had hoped. The pairing was seamless with my phone, and the touch controls were responsive. For about three weeks, I was completely satisfied and even recommended them to a friend.

Then, just shy of the one-month mark, the left earbud stopped holding a charge. It would die after about ten minutes of use, and within a few days it wouldn't power on at all. I tried resetting, cleaning the contacts, and even trying a different charging case didn’t help. I was frustrated because a product that worked so well at first should not fail that quickly. I was ready to leave a scathing review and toss them in the drawer.

But I decided to contact customer service first, and I’m glad I did. The representative responded within hours, asked a few basic troubleshooting questions, and then immediately offered a full replacement—no return shipping fees, no long wait for approval. They shipped a new unit that arrived in three days. The replacement has been working fine for two months now, no issues.

So here’s the thing: the original product clearly had a quality control issue. For the price, I expect more than a month of reliable use. That alone would have been a two stars. However, the customer service experience was genuinely excellent—fast, no hassle, and they stood behind their product. That kind of support is rare these days. So I’m giving four stars: one star deducted for the initial failure, but four because the company made it right and the replacement works as intended. If you buy these, keep the receipt handy, but know that if something goes wrong, they’ll take care of it. I’d probably buy from this brand again because of that service.

title: Great LARP helmet!!!!
text:
I bought this helmet for weekend LARP events and medieval reenactments and it has exceeded my expectations in every way. Right out of the box the fit and finish impressed me — the paint job looks like real aged metal without the cold, heavy feel of steel, and the rivet details and reinforced brow give it an authentic look that draws compliments from other players.

Comfort was my biggest concern, and this helmet delivers. The interior padding is thick enough to keep the foam cheek and forehead pieces from rubbing raw after several hours of wear, yet breathable so I don’t get overheated during intense scenarios. The chin strap is sturdy and easy to adjust one-handed, which is handy when I’m suiting up quickly. The helmet sits securely even during running and shield bashing; I never felt it shift or loosen.

Durability appears excellent — I’ve had a few decent impacts from foam weapons and some accidental drops, and the helmet has only picked up a few scuffs that add character. No cracks or structural issues. Cleaning is simple: a quick wipe with a damp cloth removes dirt and sweat stains without affecting the finish.

Sizing was accurate based on the manufacturer’s chart; I double-checked my measurements and ordered the recommended size and it fits perfectly. Shipping was fast and packaging prevented any dings in transit.

Overall this helmet gives a great balance of authenticity, comfort, and durability for LARP use. It looks great in photos, feels secure during play, and stands up to rough handling. I’d recommend it to anyone wanting a convincing, functional helmet without the cost and weight of real metal armor.

I bought this item specifically because my dog, Barnaby, has had severe anxiety issues for the past three years. We have tried everything. We have tried the prescription medications that made him lethargic and unkempt. We have tried the expensive, heated orthopedic beds that he refused to sleep on anyway. We have tried the calming sprays that smelled like expired lemon pledge and just confused him. This product was the last hope before I actually had to start carrying sedatives in my pocket every time I took him to the vet or the park. The marketing promised "instant results," "professional-grade tranquility," and "peace of mind for both pet and owner." Let me assure you, there was none of that. There was not even one percent of that. I set it up exactly as the instructions said. I turned the dial to the highest setting. I waited. I watched him closely for any sign of relaxation, for his breathing to slow down, for his ears to stop twitching at the sound of a leaf falling outside. Nothing happened. He sniffed it for approximately three seconds, looked at me with what I can only describe as pure judgment, and then proceeded to bark at a squirrel for another forty-five minutes. It was the same bark he has been doing since 2019. The noise was not dampened. The anxiety was not alleviated. I even held the device near his face, just to see if there was some magical ingredient or frequency I was missing. He sneezed. That was it. A single, annoyed sneeze. I am now out fifty dollars for a piece of plastic that does absolutely nothing. It is a light-up paperweight at best. I feel cheated. I feel like the company is running a scam on desperate pet owners who just want their animals to be happy. Do not waste your money. Do not waste your time. Save your cash and buy Barnaby a really good treat instead, because that will at least make him forget his anxiety for a brief second, which this garbage failed to do for even a fraction of a millisecond. -It has no spring, so I am not sure how long it will last without snapping.
-It seems that you can not separate the clip from the skin without damaging at least one of them.
-It only has 180 degrees of rotation, so you can't turn it upside down (I prefer one that has 360 degrees, but for most this is probably not an issue)

I'll probably continue using it until it's empty because I don't want to waste product, but I won't repurchase this version. If they update the exterior finish, I'd consider buying again. title: The "gateway drone" for beginners
text:
I've never owned a drone before so didn't know what to expect. This package contains two zippable pouches with a folded controller and drone, which are both tiny. You have to charge both units before attempting anything, and the charging station isn't obvious to use. Next, install the app on your phone and it will sync with the drone later.

Once unfolded, there is a calibration process you must follow before flying, which is a minor inconvenience but you learn the routine pretty quickly. The controller has a number of directional buttons but the easiest way to learn is to go outside in a large, clear area and experiment - after about an hour of flight time, you can get very proficient with the joysticks.

The unit broadcasts video back to your phone (or records to the provided SD card) and it's entertaining to watch your flight experience. This is not a stabilized gimbal so don't expect SteadiCam-style gliding - it can get a little rough at times - and there's no audio.

The machine will hover by itself with very little drift, and the return to home button works well. There is an option to use indoors but it's not a great idea - I decapitated a houseplant, nipped on my fingers and almost destroyed a light fixture. Without the GPS (and in the hands of a novice), indoor flying isn't particularly safe.

This drone is a good unit for beginners, older kids and supervised children, and can get you used to the basics of how drone operation works. After a few flights, you'll find yourself wanting to upgrade to something more expensive with more features, but at this price level it's a great way to learn the ropes.

Held Evans' honesty about her Evangelical upbringing, conversational tone, willingness to take many of the Biblical guidelines to their literal extreme, and inclusion of how she and her husband felt about many of the experiences invites the reader to enter into the story both to observe her actions and explore one's own views on what it means to be a "biblical woman." title: Sparks creativity, once you get past install problems
text:
The Digital Arts & Craft Studio from Fisher-Price is fun for the whole family (I think I used it more the first night than my 3 year old!), but you may be driven crazy by problems with the install process. Buyer beware if you are not willing to troubleshoot potential problems with buggy software.

In my case, I received the "Common Language Runtime Debugging error." If you do too, and your system meets the minimum requirements (and the firmware test, which comes with the software, works) then the problem is most likely your Microsoft .NET Framework installation.

I had 1.1 installed and it appears the program installs both a hotfix and .NET 2.0. To fix: uninstall everything (add/Remove programs). First, the Studio software, then NET 2.0, then the hotfix, and finally NET 1.1. Reboot, and reinstall from the CD. Everything should now work.

Took about an hour, but then we were up and running. Is it worth the money? My toddler is fascinated by the computer, and loves to draw, making this toy the perfect combination to keep her occupied (at least for a little while).

title: A Childhood Memory
text:
I had recently read this book because of a Creative Writing assignment. The reason I chose this book is because reading it took me way back to when my mind was early in the stage of the exploration of literature. I owned this book as a child, and reading it gave me another small perspective on how our own life and time itself progresses.

Robert Munsch uses humour in alot of his books and this is another one of those cases. For example, at the end of this book, the child's father is suspended in the middle of the kitchen by his toe with a long rope.

Munsch also uses a form of anticipation to ensure that the child >wants< to turn to the next page. For example, most of the pages in this book have sentences that end like: "He looked in the kitchen, it was empty. He looked in the bathroom, it was empty. He looked in the garage and..."

Not only can I look at this book from the perspective of just an ordinary reader, but also as a child; the intended audience of this book. Because of this, I can say the Robert Munsch did a wonderful job of creating literature that will intrigue children for many future generations

title: Diplomacy, work, humor, and adventure in this fine memoir
text:
This is Richard Williams' fascinating and wryly humorous account of two years as the U.S. Consul General in the Chinese city of Guangzhou (formerly called "Canton") from 1979 to 1981. His was the first American consulate to re-open in China after formal diplomatic relations with the PRC were established in 1979.

Readers interested in the development of U.S.-China relations will be fascinated -- and entertained -- by this book. Large strategic and foreign policy considerations moved China and the United States to establish relations. It was left to Foreign Service Officers such as Richard Williams and his team to make it all work -- first by setting up a new Foreign Service post, then by issuing visas, establishing commercial relations, traveling through China to report on local conditions, introducing the Big Mac, and escorting the first waves of American visitors.

Americans who know the more open China of the twenty-first century will, in this book, encounter the China making its first hesitant steps toward modernization and reform. The difficulties confronted by early official travelers, the lingering suspicion of America, the obfuscation of officials high and low, and the choices made by Foreign Service families before there were international schools are all described. Williams' wife Jane had left Tianjin as a girl; her reunions with family members in the PRC add poignant touches to the book.

This is a fine book for any young person thinking about a Foreign Service career. Although almost three decades have passed since Richard Williams and his family opened the post in Guangzhou, "At the Dawn of the New China" captures much of the enduring qualities of Foreign Service life.

title: Atomizer nozzle pops out on use.
text:
I wanted to like this spray bottle because the packaging looked nice and the price was reasonable, but it turned out to be frustrating and unusable for me. From the first full use, the atomizer nozzle popped out of the bottle twice. The first time I thought I'd just not pressed it on correctly, so I reattached it, tightened it as much as I could, and tried again. A few sprays later it dislodged and shot across my bathroom counter. The second time it fell into the sink and bent slightly, making the spray uneven and sputtery.

The fit between the nozzle and the bottle neck feels flimsy and cheap — there’s no secure click or seal, just a loose plastic ring that doesn’t hold under normal pressure. I only used it with water and a light hair mist, not a thick serum or anything that would clog it. If you plan to carry this in a bag or travel with it, don’t: I’m sure it would come apart and leak. title: Afghanistan through the eyes of a child
text: A war-torn country plagued by violence.  An 11-year-old girl forced to risk her life and save her family. These are the realities in Deborah Ellis' novel "The Breadwinner" (Groundwood Books 2000).  Told from young Parvana's perspective, the story focuses on her family of six living in Kabul, Afghanistan.  After the Taliban take control of their city, Parvana's family is forced out of their large home by a bomb explosion and into a one-room apartment.  The women are removed from school and forced to stay in the house unless escorted by a male.  When Parvana's father is arrested because he attended university in England, their family must make the tough decision to have her pose as a boy in order to leave the house and work in the marketplace to earn money for food.  While working, Parvana runs into Shauzia, a girl she knew from school who is also posing as a boy to support her family. They start to work together and soon become close friends, encountering a number of sobering, scary situations along the way. Though children may not experience the same life, they will no doubt relate to Parvana's story and her arguments with her older sister, unfairness of chore responsibilities, and love for her family.  The Breadwinner is not a happy story with a happy conclusion, but one that will leave the reader with a different view of Afghanistan, as seen through the eyes of a child.  An author's note and glossary of terms serve as a helpful aide in introducing children to the history and culture of Afghanistan.
